618Look: here is the radiant Sankarshana-kunda;
whoever bathes here has his desire fulfilled.153

619This is the village of Parasauli — look, Srinivasa:
in springtime [Krishna] performed the rasa here.154

620Look: here is the incomparable Chandra-sarovara;
here, absorbed in the rasa, Krishnachandra rested.

621Look: Gandharva-kunda is a most charming place;
here the gandharvas, singing Krishna's qualities, were beside themselves.

622All the play there was at Govardhana in the spring rasa —
it is the highest sweetness; who could describe it, and how much?

623Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Govardhanashraya-dashaka:155
"That supreme Rasa-sthali where in spring, in the rasa dance, Radha, [beloved] of Madhava,
surrounded by beautiful friends worthy of worship by hundreds of Lakshmis,
her neck adorned by Krishna's fragrant, radiant, nectar-sweet arm, dances charmingly —
it is on him; ah, what pious soul would not take shelter of that lofty Govardhana?"

624Look: the village named Paitha, most beautiful;
I shall tell a little of how it came by the name Paitha.

625During the rasa Krishna vanished in this forest;
the gopis wander about, searching for Krishna.

626Krishna, becoming four-armed, appeared [before them];
under Rai's gaze two arms entered His body.156

627Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in the section on heroines, the fifth and sixth verses:
"Though Hari in jest sometimes displays four arms,
the love of the Queen of Vrindavana makes Him two-armed.

628When the rasa was beginning, [Krishna], hiding, stayed in a kunja;
to conceal Himself from the gaze of the doe-eyed ones, with a bold design He skillfully displayed
four-armedness; — ah, such is the glory of Radha's love! — by its power
even the all-mighty Hari could not maintain that four-armedness."

629[The arms] enter the body — [He is] two-armed: this is a boundless wonder;
therefore the name Paitha spread among the people.157

630Having shown the village of Paitha and other charming places,
the Pandita turned back and came to Gauri-tirtha.158

631The Pandita joyfully says: look, Srinivasa,
here at Gauri-tirtha wonderful pastimes take place.

632At Gauri-tirtha is a captivating king of trees, a nipa;
look: here is the most beautiful Nipa-kunda.159

633This is the village of Aniyor near the hill;
who could tell of the play that took place here?

634Nanda and the other cowherds, giving up the worship of Indra,
at Krishna's word worship Govardhana Hill.

635They offered Govardhana many kinds of foodstuffs;
Krishna, in one form, partook of everything there.160

636In a voice deeper than [the rumble of] a cloud He proclaims,
"Aniyor, aniyor!" — He says it again and again.161

637The cowherd men and gopis feed Him with boundless delight;
therefore this place bears the name Aniyor.

638This is the place of the Annakuta — look, Srinivasa;
by seeing this place one's desires are fulfilled.162

639Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventy-fifth verse:
"Where the Enemy of Agha, eager, assuming a lofty, enormous body,
eats the foods offered by the best of the lords of Vraja and tricks Radha with a boon —
in that Annakuta I take shelter."163

640This is Sri Govinda-kunda — great is its glory;
here Indra performed the abhisheka of Govinda.164

641Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventy-fourth verse:
"Here the lord of the gods himself, bowing low out of great fear and clasping [His] feet,
with the waters of the heavenly Ganga, through Surabhi, performed a new festival of abhisheka —
openly, with delight — [installing] Govinda on the throne of sovereignty over the cows;
may that Govinda-kunda which arose from those [waters] always shine before my eyes."

642How many are the fruits of bathing in this Sri Govinda-kunda —
the Puranas proclaim them; who could describe them, and how much?

643Thus [it is said] in the Mathura-khanda:
"Where the Bhagavan was anointed by Maghavan, the enemy of the Yadus —
there Govinda-kunda arose; merely bathing in it grants liberation."

644Here Shakra praised Krishna in many ways;
at Shakra-tirtha bathing and tarpana bring abundant fruit.165

645Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Near the Annakuta is a tirtha made by Shakra;
by bathing and tarpana there one obtains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices."

646Look: near the kunda is a dense forest;
it was right here that Gopala stayed in hiding.

647Look: here is Dana-nivartana-kunda;
this is a very secret place — others do not know of it.166

648Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventy-eighth verse:
"Because here, in secret, the [play of the] toll came to its end,
this [pond] received that name in their assembly;
by that pond, hidden from those averse to rasa and known only to those who know it —
by Dana-nivartana may my dwelling be."

649Here Madhavendra Puri stayed beneath a tree;
Gopala appeared to him on the pretext of bringing him milk.167

650Look: over there on the hill is Gopala's place;
from time to time Gopala stays at Ganthuli.168

651Look: at the edge of Govardhana is Apsara-kunda;
here the most fortunate bathe.

652Look: here is an old palasha tree;
people call it Shyamadhak; this place is very secluded.169

653Saying this, he goes on with joy in his heart;
coming to his own dwelling place, he says to Srinivasa:

654This is my cave — I live right here;
seeing the beauty of Govardhana, I find great happiness.170

655This cave of Govardhana is most captivating;
here Radha and Krishna constantly enjoy their pastimes.

656Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixty-fifth verse:
"Where somewhere on them Madhava, with His loving friends, lavishly painted with streams of their minerals,
and Himself painted by them, sports with games
and with herding the cows, and somewhere in the caves enjoys festivals of amorous jests
together with Sri Radha — those [peaks], the best of mountains, I worship."

657Look: the footprints of Airavata; here Indra
spoke of Krishna's wonderful mercy.171

658Look: Surabhi-kunda — boundless is its glory;
who is able to tell of the many wonders here?172

659Look at the beauty of Rudra-kunda in the secluded forest;
here Mahadeva became absorbed in meditation on Krishna.

660This is Kadamkhandi: here Krishna
stands gazing at the path by which Radhika will come.173

661O Srinivasa, this place is Danaghati;
here Krishna, the king of connoisseurs of rasa, levies a toll on dairy goods.174

662Here Sri Chaitanya slowly
questions the brahmana who was with Him about the [play of the] toll and so on.175

663The brahmana told in detail of the [play of the] toll and so on;
hearing it, Gaurahari, delighted, softly smiles.

664Absorbed in prema, having the darshan of Harideva,
He performs a wonderful dance; everyone watches.

665The people are maddened with prema; streams of tears flow from their eyes;
all say, "This is an incarnation of Harideva."

666How the Lord manifested Himself at Govardhana —
O Srinivasa, who knows how to describe it?

667Danaghat is a most secluded place;
some call Danaghat by the name Krishna-vedi.

668Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventy-seventh verse:
"Where the young king of lovers, His heart eager for the play of the toll station,
becoming a toll collector on the pretext of the dairy toll [due to] King Madana,
in the morning, surrounded on all sides by His friends, stopped
Sri Gandharva, surrounded by her own [companions] — that Krishna-vedi I praise."176

669The play of the toll here is beyond compare;
Sri Rupa described it in the Dana-keli-kaumudi.177

670Look: here is Brahma-kunda — boundless is its glory;
the Puranas proclaim that on its four sides are beautiful tirthas.

671Thus [it is said] in the Mathura-khanda:
"Here Brahma-kunda arose, [where] Hari was pleased by Brahma;
and the ponds of Indra and the other guardians of the worlds arose too."178

672In the Adi-varaha Purana:
"There, O fortunate one, is a lake with trees, shrubs and creepers;
there are four tirthas, holy and auspicious.

673The tirtha of Indra is on the eastern side, the tirtha of Yama on the south,
the tirtha of Varuna on the west, and the tirtha of Kuvera on the north;
and I, staying in the middle, shall play as I please."

674Look at Manasi-ganga: here Sri Krishna,
with a joyful heart, goes boating and enjoys other pastimes.

675Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixty-fourth verse: "At the foot of the serpent, filled with the rasa of delight in the boating play of Gandharvika and the Crusher of Mura, Manasa-jahnavi with the surge of her waves raises up heaps of the shining stones of Govardhana — may she protect me."179

676The water of Sri Manasi-ganga is supremely pure;
who could tell what the fruit of bathing here is?

677Having said this and having had darshan of Harideva,
he joyfully speaks of the glory of Govardhana:

678O Srinivasa, Govardhana is full of bliss;
the road to it from Mathura is eight kroshas.

679In the western part of Mathura lies Govardhana-kshetra;
at its mere sight the grievous miseries of samsara depart.

680Whoever bathes in Manasi-ganga,
has darshan of Harideva at Govardhana

681and circumambulates Annakuta and Govardhana —
he never again comes and goes in samsara.

682This Govardhana Krishna held up with His left hand
and protected Vraja, crushing Indra's pride.

683At Govardhana Krishna's happiness has no limit;
the Puranas sing its glory in many ways.

684Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"There is a holy land named Govardhana, supremely hard to attain,
in the western part of Mathura, not far — two yojanas away.

685Reaching Annakuta from there, one should circumambulate it;
for him there is no return [to this world], O goddess — I tell you the truth.

686Having bathed in Manasi-ganga, having seen Hari at Govardhana,
having circumambulated Annakuta — why should a person still grieve?

687When Indra was pouring down water beyond measure, tormenting the cows,
to protect them I held up the best of hills."

688In the Skanda Purana, in the Mathura-khanda:
"[There is] the Bhagavan Govardhana, where Govardhana was held up
and all the Yadavas were saved, since Indra's rain was warded off.180

689Ah, Govardhana, where Vishnu always dwells!
There Brahma, Shiva and Lakshmi certainly live."

690In the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Having circumambulated Govardhana and seen the god Hari, the Lord,
[a person] without doubt obtains the fruit of the Rajasuya and the Ashvamedha."

691O Srinivasa, near Govardhana
there lived a brahmana — everyone knew he was wealthy.

692He was always in rapture, loved Balaichand,
and constantly meditated on the deeds of Balarama.181

693Fixing it firmly in his mind — "[He] will surely appear to me" —
he wandered through these forests of Govardhana.

694The good fortune of that brahmana cannot be described:
suddenly there came [to him] a command: "I shall meet you."

695For the sake of His dear devotee, Nityananda-Rama,
joyfully wandering among the holy places, came to Govardhana.

696Having come, He stayed right here, seeing that the place was secluded;
His form, which enchants Kandarpa, captivates every heart.182

697Seeing [Him] from afar, that brahmana thought to himself:
"From where has this avadhuta come here?

698With the radiance of His body He has lit up the forest;
this is not a mere human being — He [only] resembles a human.

699By His mercy my desire will be fulfilled."
Reflecting thus, the brahmana could not keep still.

700Taking yogurt, milk, curd, fresh butter and other things,
he came before Prabhu and, bowing down, said:

701"O avadhuta, this is my prayer:
be merciful, so that I may see the son of Rohini.

702Accept the little that I have brought."
Hearing this, Prabhu smiled and with great delight partook [of it].

703Taking the remnants, the brahmana went to his own place;
as he ate them, he was overwhelmed with prema.

704He could not go to Prabhu again:
at about the time of dusk, sleep overcame him.

705In the guise of a dream Prabhu Nityananda appeared to him;
seeing Avadhutachandra, the brahmana rejoiced.

706At that very moment Prabhu took the form of Baladeva;
the brahmana fell down and rolled at Prabhu's feet.

707How [beautiful] was Baladeva's form, enchanting the worlds!
On His body many ornaments glittered.

708When, having shown mercy to the brahmana, He vanished from sight,
his sleep broke — the brahmana looks around in all directions.

709To the place where he had seen Prabhu, the avadhuta,
he hurries — his mind finds no rest.

710A voice from heaven sounded: "Have patience now:
from here you will go there when the night is over."

711Hearing this, the brahmana reflects within himself:
"The hope I had has been fulfilled.

712I have found Prabhu — now I will not let [Him] go;
falling at [His] feet, I will take this attire off Him.

713At daybreak I will send for a goldsmith
and put many kinds of ornaments on Prabhu."

714Just as he said this, sleep overcame him;
in the guise of a dream Nityananda gave him darshan.

715[His] body was adorned with many kinds of ornaments;
seeing [this], the best of brahmanas offers abundant praises.

716When Prabhu vanished, his sleep broke;
in the morning, going before Prabhu, [the brahmana] told Him everything.

717Smiling gently, Prabhu took the brahmana by the hand
and in His mercy revealed to him the whole truth.

717aAnd again with sweet words He said to the brahmana:
"You have set your mind on putting ornaments on Me."183

718The brahmana said: "The ornaments I saw on Prabhu —
who is there who could make their equal?"

719Prabhu, who is subject to His devotees, said: "After some time
I shall certainly be adorned with many kinds of ornaments.184

720For now, set this wonderful stone of Govardhana
in gold and give it to Me — I shall wear it at My neck."

721The brahmana set the stone in gold and brought it [to Him];
the crest-jewel of avadhutas put it on His neck.

722This lila of Nityananda is rare even for Brahma and others;
He forbade the brahmana to reveal it to others.

723Out of love for His devotee He stayed here for some days;
by seeing this place one attains rare love.

724Look at this Chakra-tirtha, O Srinivasa:
by its mercy desires are fulfilled.185

725Chakra-tirtha is most renowned at Govardhana;
here is the swing pastime of Sri Radha and Krishna.

726Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventy-ninth and eightieth verses:
"The finest ponds, bearing the names of the Plough-bearer, Brahma, Kadamba-khanda, Sumano, Rudra, the Apsaras, Gauri,
Jyotsna, Mokshana, Malyahara, the Enemy of the gods, Indradhvaja and others,
which shine all around Mount Govardhana — them I praise,
and also Chakra-tirtha, the divine hill and the beautiful Ratna-pitha.186

727Ah, where every spring the host of friends, showing their joy,
again and again swings those two — Sri Gandharva and the Holder of the best of hills —
whose faces have blossomed with the abundance of the highest rasa of the swing play —
that renowned, bountiful place of Govinda I, ah, worship."

728O Srinivasa, Chakra-tirtha commanded
Sri Sanatana Gosvami to live here.187

729He lived here with a jubilant heart;
look: here is his hut in the midst of the forest.

730Every day he circumambulated Govardhana —
walking twelve kroshas: who else has such strength?

731Seeing his great toil in old age, Gopinatha
appeared before him in the guise of a cowherd boy.

732Carefully wiping the sweat from Sanatana's body,
with tears He spoke sweet words:

733"In old age you will not be able to toil so much.
O svami, what I tell you, you must surely accept."

734Sanatana said: "Speak — once I know it, I will accept."
Hearing this, the cowherd boy went and climbed Govardhana.

735Bringing a stone of Govardhana bearing the print of His own foot,
He again spoke most sweet words to Sanatana:

736"O svami, take this footprint of Krishna;
from today you shall circumambulate it.188

737By this the whole circumambulation will be accomplished."
Saying this, He brought the stone and gave [it to him] in the hut.

738Having handed over the stone, Krishna vanished from sight;
not seeing the boy, Sanatana became anxious.

739Seeing Sanatana distraught, [Krishna], remaining invisible,
overcome with tenderness, revealed who He was.

740Sanatana was drenched with his own tears;
after much lamenting he [at last] took firmness of heart.

741The son of the king of Vraja, subject to Sanatana's prema,
enjoys many pastimes in this flower forest.

742Sri Radhika comes with her friends;
going out to meet them, He brings them here.

743At this ghat of Manasi-ganga, taking a boat,
He becomes the boatman and ferries them all across.

744Here are wondrous pastimes with Sri Radhika;
Lalita and the other friends fulfilled the desire.

745Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Sri Govardhanashraya-dashaka, the sixth verse:
"She on whom Madhava the boatman, seating Radha, full of rasa, in the boat,
in the midst of the restless waters, rocking [the boat] as if it were about to capsize,
took the toll He desired from her as she praised Him in fear — that Manasa-jahnavi flows upon him;
who would not take shelter of that Govardhana, the surety of that young couple?"189

746In this village of Saunkarai a playful scene unfolded:
the friends made Krishna swear an oath.190

747Having sworn, Krishna says again and again:
"Besides Sri Radhika, I never know anyone else."

748O Srinivasa, this is the village of Sakhisthali,
where Chandravali lived; now it is called Sakhithara.

749Look: sitting here, at this place, Uddhava
speaks about Krishna to [Krishna's] beloveds from Dvaraka.191

750Here, beside Govardhana, Krishna in great joy
plays various games together with the cowherd boys.

751Look: here the two brothers, Rama and Krishna,
sat, surrounded by their friends.

752Saying this, the Pandita took Srinivasa with him
and, with joy in his heart, went to the bank of Radha-kunda.

753Sri Govinda-ghat is very dear to Govinda;
having bathed there, he says to Srinivasa:192

754O Srinivasa, beneath this tree
a pastime took place — I shall tell you of it.

755One day Sanatana came here from Govardhana
to see Rupa and Raghunatha.193

756Sri Rupa Gosvami was composing verses;
he compared a braid to the hood of a female serpent.194

757Sanatana Gosvami, seeing this, says something:
"You have given such a comparison — is it right or not?"

758Saying this, he came and stepped into the water of the kunda;
he sees girls playing beneath the tree.

759On a girl's head the braid hangs down over her back;
Sanatana sees it — and he took it for a snake.

760He says to the girl in great agitation:
"A snake is climbing onto your head by way of your back!

761Heedless girls, be careful!"
Saying this, he rushed forward to drive it off.

762Seeing Sanatana extremely agitated,
they all smiled slightly and vanished.195

763Sanatana was overwhelmed right here;
regaining his composure, he went to Rupa Gosvami.

764He says to Rupa: "What you wrote is true."
Sri Rupa understood Sanatana's heart.

765With joy in his heart Sri Gosvami Sanatana,
having stayed [there] for a while, went to Govardhana.

766Sri Rupa Gosvami too went to Vrindavana.
I shall tell something of the reason for which he had come [here].

767The Lalita-madhava, in which is the utmost limit of vipralambha,
he had earlier given to Raghunatha to relish.196

768Reading the book, Raghunatha weeps day and night;
from grief he fell into divine madness — he cannot keep his composure.

769Sometimes, abandoning the book, he goes and stays far away;
sometimes he lies fallen on the ground, holding the book to his chest.

770Moment by moment various states arise;
all were anxious whenever he fell unconscious.

771Sri Rupa Gosvami, considering a remedy in his mind,
quickly composed the Dana-keli-kaumudi.

772He says to Raghunatha: "Relish this;
give me the former book — I shall revise it."

773Raghunatha cannot part with that jewel of a book;
hearing "I shall revise it," he gave [it] to Sri Rupa.

774Reading the Dana-keli, Raghunatha, the best of the wise,
was constantly immersed in an ocean of happiness.

775Of all the ways of Sanatana, Rupa and Raghunatha —
O Srinivasa, how much can I tell?

776Saying this, the Pandita took Srinivasa with him
and set out for their lodging with great joy in his heart.

777All the places that lie near Radha-kunda —
to see them all, he quickly set out.

778Raghava Pandita says to Srinivasa:
this is called Nimgrama — it is known [so] for this reason:

779all of them, coming out from Govardhana,
gazing at Krishna's face, performed nirmanchhana with what is dearer than life.197

780Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the forty-third verse:
"Those gopis who out of love, even with their sons, dearer to them than life, perform nirmanchhana
over a tiny drop of the sweat trickling from Mukunda's pair of lotus feet,
and for a long time kiss His head, beautiful with a large peacock feather —
the dust of their feet I constantly and openly honor with nirmanchhana."

781Look at the village of Patala: here with Her friends
Rai joyfully gathers patala flowers.198

782This is the village of Deravali: going from Shashthighara
to Nandishvara, Nanda made camp here.199

783Look: ahead, by this kunja, is the village of Nava;
from here begins the boundary of the kunjas of Sri Kunda.200

784Now people call this village Kunjera;
here are the incomparable pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

785This is the village of Surya-kunda, called Morana;
look at the Deity of Surya, at Surya's temple in the forest.201

786With Her friends Rai worships Surya in great happiness;
Krishna, becoming the priest, playfully performs the puja [with Her].

787This merciful Surya grants love for Krishna;
what to say of his glory — who does not worship him?

788Thus [it is said]:
"To the father of the Yamuna, Surya, who removes all diseases,
whose form is the abode of auspiciousness — to him, the giver of love for Krishna, I bow."202

789Look: here ahead is the village named Keunai;
here Ghanashyama is distraught without Rai.

790"Keu na ai?" Sri Krishna asks the messenger;
hence Keunai — and now it is called Konai.203

791Look there: this is the village named Bhadayar;
it is here that Bhadra, the leader of a group of friends, enjoys her pastimes.204

792Look: over there is the village of Magahera;
there everyone gazes at the road by which Krishna goes away.205

793How distraught they all were cannot be told;
now people call this [place] Maghera.

794Thus showing other places of pastimes as well,
they came, filled with joy, to Radha-kunda.

795Whoever loves to see and hear about all these —
his terrible misfortune is removed without effort.

796That day they stayed right on the bank of Radha-kunda;
in talks about Krishna they spent that night until dawn.

797Thus, making the circuit along Govardhana,
they came, filled with joy, to the village of Ganthuli.

798Raghava Pandita says to Srinivasa:
I shall tell how the village came by the name Ganthuli.

799Here, having played Holi, the Two sit on a throne;
a friend secretly tied the garments of Them both in a knot.

800When the Two rose from the throne,
They see the knot in Their garments — the friends laugh.

801There was great merriment; They both were abashed;
someone, receiving the phagua, untied the knot.206

802Hence Ganthuli; in the water of this Gulal-kunda
people now see the phagu in springtime.

803Saying this, he went for darshan of Gopala;
seeing Gopala's beauty, he lost his composure.

804The Deity of Krishna Chaitanya whom Vitthala served —
supreme eagerness arose for His darshan.207

805Sri Vitthalanatha Bhatta, the son of Vallabha,
showed such affection that it cannot be told.

806From time to time Gopala stays at Ganthuli;
in every way He fulfills the desires of the devotees.

807Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the crest jewel of sannyasis —
by His pilgrimage to the holy places this earth is blessed.

808In Mathura, Sri Vrindavana, at the Kunda, at Govardhana,
the pastimes He reveals are seen by the fortunate.

809In the mood of a devotee the Lord does not set foot on Govardhana;
He wished to see Gopala.

810Gopala came to the village of Ganthuli on a pretext;
seeing Him, Gaurahari was immersed in dancing and singing.208

811Sri Mahaprabhu's supernatural rapture of prema —
on seeing it, no one kept even a trace of composure.

812At that time the service of Gopala was entrusted
to those two brahmanas whom Puri had made his disciples.

813By the mercy of Madhavendra the two brahmanas from Gauda
were strong in renunciation and full of the rasa of prema-bhakti.209

814What to say — after the departure of those two brahmanas,
for some time a certain fortunate person served.

815Sri Dasa Gosvami and others, after consulting together,
entrusted the service to Sri Vitthaleshvara.

816After the departure of his father, Sri Vallabha Bhatta,
he lived for some time in Mathura in seclusion.

817Utterly overwhelmed by the pastimes of Gaurachandra,
he is now always attentive in the service of Gopala.

818Having told of Gopala's qualities, Raghava Pandita,
filled with joy, goes on from Ganthuli.

819Going some distance, he says to Srinivasa:
look: this is the village named Rehej.

820Here Indra, deeming himself utterly low,
comes before Krishna, taking Surabhi as his helper.210

821And this place of pastimes is full of great splendor;
look: Devashirsha-sthana — the kunda shines beautifully.211

822Seeing Krishna herding the cows with His friends,
here the gods in great joy offered praises.

823Look: Munishirsha-sthana, the kunda full of sweetness;
here the sages, by performing austerities, attained Krishna.

824Look: in all these places Rama and Krishna,
herding the cows with Their friends, played various games.

825In this village of Pramodana, Krishna, playfully,
gave delight to all the beauties of Vraja.212

826For this reason the village bears the name Pramodana;
now all people call it Paramadana.

827This is Setu-kandara — a most charming place;213
look: [here is] the merciful Adi-Badri-narayana.

828Most wondrous is the service [of Him] deep in the forest;
on the charming hill Gandha-shila is set.214

829Here Krishna, bringing Nanda and the other cowherds,
dispelled their sorrow by showing them Narayana.215

830Here ahead, look, is a grove of kadambas alone;
here Radha-Krishna and the sakhis are immersed in happiness.

831Here they engage in many kinds of play;
in the month of Shravana, having made a swing, they swing joyfully.

832At this Indroli, Indra was absorbed in meditation on Krishna;
now everyone calls the village Idaroli.

833O Srinivasa, look: here nearby
is the village of Kanoyaro, the place of the sage Kanva's austerities.216

834Look: this is Kamyavana, the best of all forests;
whoever comes here is honored in Vishnu-loka.217

835Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The fourth is Kamyaka-vana, the best forest among forests;
having gone there, O goddess, a man is glorified in My world."

836Kamyavana grants the fruit of all desires;
wherever one bathes here, all sorrows are destroyed.

837Thus [it is said] in the Skanda Purana, in the Mathura-khanda:
"Next is Kamyavana, O king, where you stayed in childhood;
by mere bathing it grants everyone the fruit of all desires."

838In this Kamyavana Krishna's pastimes are enchanting;
you will see a great many places and kundas.

839O Srinivasa, look: Vishnu-simhasana;
[this is] Sri Charana-kunda: here [He] washed [His] feet.

840What can I say, oh, of the glory of this place!
Brahma and the others, describing it, find no end to it.

841Look: Shiva Kameshvara, full of great splendor;218
the place of Garuda's seat is most charming.

842This is Dharma-kunda: Narayana in the form of Dharma
sports here; [its] beauty cannot be described.

843This is the altar named Vishoka — everyone knows it;
look: here is the kunda of the five Pandavas.219

844This is Manikarnika, of which all people sing;
here are the power of Vishvanatha and much else.220

845Bathing in this Vimala-kunda destroys all sins;
one who gives up his life here attains Vishnu-loka.

846Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"In the kunda of Vimala one is freed from all sin;
whoever gives up his life there goes to My world."

847The account of Vimala-kunda cannot be told;
here Sri Vimala-devi always resides.

848Look: Yashoda-kunda, supremely pure;
here Krishna herds the cows, rapt beyond Himself.

849Look: Narada-kunda; here Narada
lost all composure singing Krishna's pastimes.

850This is Kamana-kunda, which everyone knows;
here all the desires of the heart are fulfilled.

851This is Setubandha-kunda — much is told about it:
here Krishna performed the pastime of bridging the ocean.221

852This is the place of Lukalukani and Michali;
here the play of Radha and Krishna is boundless.

853"Michali" means here "with the eyes closed";
in "Lukalukani" happiness grows by hiding.222

854Lukalukani-Michali-kunda is beautiful;
this very dense forest is full of darkness.

855Look: Kashi-kunda, Gaya, Prayaga, Pushkara,
Gomati, Dvaraka-kunda — secluded and beautiful.223

856This is Tapa-kunda, the place of the sages' austerities;
this is Dhyana-kunda: [here] Krishna meditated on Radha.

857Look: the marks of the holy feet on the hill;
in this Krida-kunda Krishna plays in the water.

858Charming are the kundas of the five cowherd boys — Shridama and the others;
this is Ghosharani-kunda, supremely beautiful.

859Ghosharani is the daughter of the cowherd Yashodhara;
the king of the cowherds gave [this] girl in marriage here.224

860Look: Vihvala-kunda; here Rai
was overwhelmed by the song of Krishna's flute.

861This is Shyama-kunda: here Shyama, full of rasa,
stays gazing at the path [by which] Radhika [will come].225

862This is Sri Lalita-kunda, and this one is named Vishakha-kunda;
here the two fulfilled the desire of Krishna's heart.

863Look: Mana-kunda — here Radha was sulking (mana);
Krishna broke her sulking with playful words.

864At this Mohini-kunda Krishna became Mohini —
that form of Mohini in which He distributed the nectar.226

865Look: this Dohani-kunda is the place of milking the cows;227
this is Balabhadra-kunda, made by Brahma.

866This is Surya-kunda, near Krishna-kunda;
Surya, staying here, offered praises to Krishna.

867On Chandrasena hill is this Pichhalini-shila;
here Krishna with His friends plays this game:228

868sitting gracefully on top of the low hill,
He slides down — so He does again and again.

869Look: Kama-sarovara — Gopika-ramana;
who could describe the enchanting play [that took place] here?

870Thus [it is said] in the Skanda Purana, in the Mathura-khanda:
"There, O king, is Kamasaras, the lake Gopika-ramana;
there are thousands of tirthas and lakes, each one apart."

871This Kama-sarovara is full of great happiness;
Kama-sarovara is called Kama-sagara.

872Look: Surabhi-kunda — its beauty is boundless;
Krishna with the cows and cowherds sports here.

873This is Chaturbhuja-kunda, supremely secluded;
the wonderful sports [that took place] here cannot be described.

874Look: Bhojana-sthali — here Krishna
made merry over a meal with His friends.

875Look: Bajana-shila, O Srinivasa;
here everyone rejoices to the sound of many instruments.229

876Behold the place where Parashurama stayed;
here Narayana sat on the throne.

877This is Santana-kunda, Veda-kunda, Damodara;
this is Gandharva-kunda, Prithudaka — an excellent kunda.230

878Look: Ayodhya-kunda, supremely secluded;
I cannot set out at length the account of this kunda.

879Look: Sri Nrisimha-kunda, and also Arghya-kunda;
this is Madhusudana-kunda — its glory is proclaimed.

880Rohini-kunda, Gopala-kunda, Godavari;
look at Devaki-kunda, full of wondrous sweetness.

881On this hill is the place of the stealing game; Vyomasura
Krishna playfully slew at the mouth of this cave.231

882Look: Prahlada-kunda, and also Lakshmi-kunda;
the tirthas in Kamyavana are beyond counting.

883This is the place of Krishna's play on top of the hill;
look from here — in all four directions [all is] enchanting.

884Look, Srinivasa, there is the village of Dhulauda;
there the dust from the cows' hooves covered the sky.232

885That village all people call by the name Udha;
staying there, Uddhava went to Nanda's home.233

886This is the village of Ator, charming and secluded; here
Krishna is absorbed in play through all eight praharas.234

887Look: Kadamkhandi, the village of Svarnahara,
Ratna-kunda, the incomparable place of Chaturmukha.235

888At the place of Svarnahara the play is boundless;
now it is called Sona-ar and Sonahera.236

889Look at the hill: here Krishna, herding the cows —
who could tell the joy He finds?

890This is Vrishabhanupura, called Varshana;
near the hill is Vrishabhanu's home.237

891A wondrous hill: here the son of the king of Vraja
performed the dana-lila, hidden from others.

892Here [He] broke Radhika's sulking (mana);
here Krishna was intoxicated with many kinds of play.

893Between the two hills, on this narrow path —
the sport [that took place] there, no one can tell.

894Now everyone calls this place Sankari-khor;
the hills of Dana, Mana and Vilasa — three garhs.238

895O Srinivasa, Sri Radhika with her sakhis
played many games here in a childlike mood.

896In the wondrous time when Radhika was at the junction of ages,
here, in great delight, she sports together with the sakhis.

897Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in [the chapter] on uddipana, [in the section] on vayah-sandhi, the sixth verse:239 "The junction of childhood and youth is called vayah-sandhi."

898The junction of childhood and youth is wondrous in this way:
as when another [king] takes possession of a kingdom.

899For example, [it is said] in the same work, the eleventh verse:
"The hips, girded with a cord, learning of their rise, bring music — the kinkini bells;
the waist, dwindling and seeing its own ruin, seeks alliance with the folds;
the bosom diligently gathers a pair of fruits fit to be a gift for the king —
when into the kingdom of Radha's body there enters the new lord of the earth, youth."240

900In this kunja the sakhis, having dressed Radhika,241
gaze their fill at the beauty of her fresh youth.

901Thus [it is said] in the same [work], in [the section] on uddipana, on the characteristics of fresh youth, the twelfth verse:
"The breasts have barely budded, the eyes are slightly restless, the smile is charming,
and feeling shows itself only a little — this is called fresh youth."

902In this kadamba grove Radha joyfully sports;
the sakhis behold the beauty of Her manifest youth.

903Thus [it is said] in the same [work], in [the section] on uddipana, on the characteristics of manifest youth:242
"The breasts have fully developed, the waist bears three beautiful folds,
and the limbs are radiant — when manifest youth unfolds."

904All is possible: She is always in manifest youth;
this Rai increases rasa with the art of Ananga.

905In this Madana-kunja, joyfully, together with the sakhis —
how wondrous is that beauty in full youth!

906Thus [it is said] in the same [work], in [the section] on uddipana, on the characteristics of full youth, the forty-first verse:
"The hips are broad, the waist slender, the body of splendid luster,
the breasts full, the thighs like plantain trunks — in full youth."

907What shall I say! In this kunja of tamalas the sakhis,
on a pretext, arranged the meeting of Radha and Krishna.

908The village of Chiksauli [was called] Chitrashali before;
here the sakhis, skilled in wondrous attire, [dressed] Rai.243

909Look: in the mountain gorge is a dense forest;
now people call it Gahvara-vana.244

910This is Shitala-kunda, surrounded on all sides by trees;
look at Dohani-kunda — here the cows were milked.

911This is the village of Dabhararo; here Krishna's
eyes filled with tears at the sight of Radhika.

912Dabhararo means "with eyes full of tears," so it is said;
now among the people it is known by the name Dabharo.

913Look: Mukta-kunda; here lovely Radhika,
contending with Krishna, made a field of pearls.245

914Look: east of Vrishabhanupura is Bhanukhora;
its water is very clear, its beauty has no limit.246

915Look: north of the village is Piyala-sarovara;
here the Beloved and the Lover — both — engage in many kinds of play.

916Here is a forest of jiyala trees, very extensive;
seeing [its] beauty, both rejoice together with the sakhis.247

917This is Pilukhora; here, on the pretext of [gathering] pilu fruits,
Rai with the sakhis merrily plays with Kanu.248

918Now people say "Bhanukhora," "Pilukhora";
formerly they were named Bhanu-sarovara and Pilu-sarovara.

919Near Varshana is this river, the Triveni;
how Krishna's pastimes [took place] here, I do not know how to tell.

920Look at Krishna's places of pastimes — they are beyond compare;
how many of the villages founded by Vajra have vanished!

921O Srinivasa, look: this is Prema-sarovara;
here the feeling of prema-vaichittya was manifested.249

922Look: Vihvala-kunda; here, on hearing
the name "Sri Krishna," Rai was overwhelmed.

923In this kunja of Sanketa the sakhis, giving a signal,
bring both Rai and Kanu with great care.250

924Unnoticed, at an auspicious moment, the first going [to the tryst] took place;
here, in the time of purva-raga, there was a brief meeting.251

925How wondrous the delights of purva-raga are cannot be told;
the characteristics of purva-raga are defined in the shastras.

926Thus [it is said] in the Ujjvala-nilamani, in the section on separation, the fifth verse: "The attraction (rati) that arises before meeting from seeing [each other], hearing [of each other] and so on, and blossoms in the two of them, is called purva-raga by the wise."

927Look at Krishna-kunda and other enchanting places;
in Sanketa are endless pastimes, beyond the sight of others.

928The people of the villages of Nandishvara and Varshana —
all of them come and go along this road.252

929Along this road Sri Radhika, from Her father's house,
goes to the village of Javata, to the house of Her father-in-law.

930This wondrous forest is always in cool shade;
birds sing in many voices, the bees hum.

931O Srinivasa, look: Nandishvara, the abode of Nanda;
here Rama and Krishna, hidden [in human form], enjoy Their pastimes.

932Thus [it is said] in the Tenth [Canto], in the forty-fourth chapter, the twelfth verse:253
"How pious are the lands of Vraja, where this Primeval Person, hidden in human form,
adorned with a colorful forest garland, tends the cows together with Bala, plays the flute,
and roams about in various play — He whose feet are worshipped by Giritra and Rama!"

933Look: this is the boundary of Nanda's settlement;
east of Nanda's house is a wondrous garden.

934From Javata Sri Radhika with the sakhis
comes along this road to Nanda's house.

935O Srinivasa, whoever, having bathed in this Pavana-sarovara,
sees Krishna on Nandishvara

936and has darshan of Sri Nanda and Sri Yashoda —
all his desires are fulfilled at that very moment.254

937Thus [it is said] in the Mathura-mahatmya:255
"Having bathed in the Pavana lake, [beholding] Krishna on Nandishvara hill,
and having seen Nanda and Yashoda, one obtains all that one desires."

938This Pavana-sarovara is very dear to Krishna;
who, seeing this wondrous beauty, can keep his composure?

939Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the fifty-ninth verse:
"Surrounded by multitudes of kadambas, charming with the humming of swarms of bees —
where the lotus-eyed [gopis], on the pretext of sweet play in the water and of fetching water,
again and again hasten to the son of the king of the cowherds
with merriment and love — may this Pavana lake protect [us]."

940Look: all around Nandishvara are kundas and forests,
places of Krishna's pastimes that purify the worlds.

941Look: on the hill, together with their son,
Sri Nanda and Yashoda shine in a wondrous cave.256

942O Srinivasa, here Sri Chaitanya-raya,
having come to receive darshan, enters the cave.

943Sri Nanda and Yashoda — two persons, one on each side,
and in the middle Krishnachandra; seeing [this], His eyes blossomed.

944Bowing at the feet of Sri Nanda and Sri Yashoda,
He touches all of Krishna's body, overflowing with joy.

945In the rapture of prema He began to dance and sing;
seeing this, all the people were amazed.

946Some say, "He is certainly not a human being;
is such beauty possible in a human?"

947Others say, "He is Narayana of Vaikuntha,
wandering in Vraja in human form."

948Someone says, "Oh, this is what comes to my mind:
has the son of Nanda appeared again?

949"Otherwise why would He act like this?
Again and again He falls at the feet of Nanda and Yashoda.

950"From His beautiful lotus eyes tears flow incessantly;
with joined palms He says something softly — I do not know what.

951"What shall I say, O brother! Seeing Him,
I have become certain in my heart: this is Krishna."

952Saying many such things, they float on the waves of prema;
crying "Hari bol!" they dance together with the Lord.

953Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the crest-jewel of sannyasis —
what prema He manifested here, I do not know how to tell.

954This is Tadaga-tirtha, renowned everywhere;
how beautifully trees and creepers adorn it on all sides!

955O Srinivasa, I will briefly tell one more account:
here was the dwelling of Parjanya, the son of Devamidha.257

956Out of mercy Narada came to Nandishvara
and gave Parjanya the Lakshmi-Narayana mantra.

957Parjanya performed austerities at Tadaga-tirtha;
his desire was fulfilled — five sons were born:

958Upananda, Abhinanda, the one named Nanda,
Sananda and Nandana — thus the five brothers are known.

959Look: this is that very pond, and it is dear to Krishna;
the devotees always pray for service to this pond.

960Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixtieth verse:
"Where grandfather Parjanya, giving up food, intently worshipped Narayana
when his own son, the lord of the pastures, was without a son,
and where a grandson was obtained — the slayer of the enemies of the gods, Giridhara, the sole mine of virtues —
that pond, renowned on earth as Kshunahara, is my refuge."258

961O Srinivasa, look at Kshunahara-sarovara;
what shall I say of what Krishna's pastimes are like here!

962This is Dhoyani-kunda, to the northeast of Nandishvara;
here remains the water with which the curd pots were washed.

963Look: by this Krishna-kunda is a forest of kadambas;
here the son of the lord of Vraja joyfully sports.

964Look: Lalita-kunda; here Lalita,
bringing Radhika on a pretext, unites [Her] with Krishna.

965Here is the most wondrous Surya-kunda;
Surya lost his composure on seeing Krishna.

966Look: this is Vishakha-kunda;
here, in great delight, Rai and Kanu met.

967Look: Paurnamasi-kunda in deep seclusion;
Paurnamasi lives here in a hut of leaves.259

968In the pastimes of Radha and Krishna her joy is unceasing;
who has the power to understand what her deeds are like?

969Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the twenty-fifth verse:
"She who in secret, through friends honored for their skill in this, arranges for Them —
with love, expertly, every day — the festival of mana and abhisara of the two connoisseurs of rasa,
and who herself again and again tastes the nectarean rasa of the happiness of Radha and Madhava —
to that Bhagavati Paurnamasi, who brings about good in Vraja, I offer worship."260

970Here is the charming abode of Nandimukhi,
who is always happy in the happiness of Radha and Krishna.261

971The beautiful character of Sri Nandimukhi
the great bhagavatas described with care in the past.

972Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the thirty-fourth verse:
"She who, her heart enchanted by abundant hearing of the glory [of Radha and Madhava], [left] Avanti
and in deep longing chose the land of Vraja [as her home],
and joyfully increases the happiness of Radha and Krishna's ujjvala-rasa — that
Nandimukhi I always greet with love."

973Look: everywhere are most delightful kunjas;
in these places there is no end to Krishna's pastimes.

974This is Sri Yashoda-kunda; here [dwells] Yashoda;
look: Rama and Krishna play with Their friends.

975O Srinivasa, Krishna, full of the bliss of prema,
here in His various ages enjoys pastimes beyond measure.

976Thus [it is said] in the Sri Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, in the Dakshina-vibhaga, in the first lahari, the hundred and fifty-eighth verse:
"Age — kaumara, pauganda and kaishora: thus it is threefold.
Kaumara lasts until the end of the fifth year, pauganda up to the tenth,
kaishora up to the sixteenth; after that comes youth."262

977Here, in the age of kaumara, Yashoda towards Krishna
shows such parental love — who could tell of it?

978Krishna, ever absorbed in the mood of the kaumara age,
increases His mother's happiness, which is beyond the reach of others.

979Thus [it is said] there, the hundred and fifty-ninth verse:
"As is fitting, in the rasa of parental love kaumara is to be described."

980Krishna in the pauganda age in this kadamba grove —
whatever merriment arises, His beloved ones see it.

981The pauganda age is threefold: the beginning, the middle and the last;
its games and the rest are full of supreme bliss.

982Thus [it is said] there, the hundred and fifty-ninth verse: "Likewise in the rasa of friendship, pauganda, in connection with the various games and the rest."

983There, in the Pashchima-vibhaga, in the third lahari, the twenty-third verse:
"Pauganda is of three kinds: the beginning, the middle and the last."263

984In early pauganda Krishna's body is exceedingly beautiful;
here are the herding of calves and other charming activities.

985Thus [it is said] there:264
"A deep redness of the lips and so on, slenderness of the waist,
the appearance of a conch-like neck and so on — when the first pauganda comes.

986Varied ornaments of flowers, designs drawn with mountain minerals,
yellow silk garments and so on — this is here called adornment.

987Herding the herds of fine cows while roaming through all the forests, the beginning of training in wrestling play, dancing and so on — such are the activities here."

988In middle pauganda, almost touching kaishora,
[He] sports here — His activities cannot be described.

989Thus [it is said] there, the twenty-fifth verse:
"The nose finely tipped and high; the cheeks round;
the sides and other limbs beautifully rounded — when middle pauganda comes.

990Here the turban, with a cord of silk threads gleaming like lightning;
the staff, dark, three cubits tall, tipped with gold — such is the adornment.

991Games at Bhandira, the lifting of the hill and so on — such are the activities."

992There, the twenty-seventh verse:
"Already in middle pauganda this Hari, playing, shines
as if partaking of the beginning of kaishora, for His form is wondrous with sweetness."

993In the last pauganda [His] body is supremely beautiful;
[His] activities are wondrous: here He sports with His friends.

994Thus [it is said] there, the twenty-eighth verse:
"The braid whose tip hangs down to the hips, the luster of dark curling locks,
the height of the shoulders and so on — when the last pauganda comes.265

995The tilt of the turban, a lotus for play in the hand,
a vertical tilaka of Kashmir saffron and so on — this is here called adornment."

996There, the twenty-ninth verse:
"Here: graceful turns of speech, the delight of whispering in the ear with the narma-sakhas,
praising to them the beauty of the girls of Gokula and so on — such are the activities."266

997Kaishora is threefold: the beginning, the middle and the last;
in these forest pastimes [He] attracts the hearts of all.

998Thus [it is said] there, in the Dakshina-vibhaga, in the first lahari, the hundred and fifty-ninth and hundred and sixtieth verses: "Although the pre-eminence of this kaishora is only in the ujjvala [rasa], nevertheless, since it is generally fitting for all the rasas, it is illustrated here in order. Kaishora is of three kinds: the beginning, the middle and the last."267

999In the first kaishora — a radiant complexion, lovely beauty;
[He] sports in this kunja, [showing] many activities that captivate the mind.

1000Thus [it is said] there:
"A certain [indescribable] brilliance of complexion, a reddish glow at the corners of the eyes,
the appearance of the line of hair — when the first kaishora comes."

1001There, the hundred and sixty-first verse:
"The vaijayanti garland, the peacock feather and so on, the dress of the best of dancers,
the sweetness of the flute, the beauty of the garments — such is the attire here."

1002There, the hundred and sixty-second verse:
"Here the sharpness of the tips of the nails, the bow-like play of the brows,
the coloring of the teeth with coloring powders and so on — such are the activities."

1003In middle kaishora [He] sports in these kunjas;
His activities, which enchant Kandarpa, cannot be described.268

1004Thus [it is said] there, the hundred and sixty-third verse:
"A certain [special] beauty of the thighs, the arms and also the chest,
the sweetness of the form and so on — when middle kaishora comes.

1005The face rich with the play of smiles, the eyes trembling with playfulness,
song that enchants the three worlds and so on — such is the sweetness here.

1006The unfolding of the very essence of artfulness, the great festival of play in the kunjas, the beginning of the rasa-lila and so on — such is the beauty of activities and so on here."

1007The last kaishora is new youth;
[He] is absorbed in play in these kunjas, His activities are delightful.269

1008Thus [it is said] there, the hundred and sixty-fourth verse:
"The limbs bear an excellence far greater even than before;
the appearance of the three folds and so on — when the last kaishora comes."

1009There, the hundred and sixty-fifth and hundred and sixty-sixth verses:
"This very [age] the wise call Hari's new youth.

1010Here: possession of the whole treasure of the feelings of the goddesses of Gokula,
unprecedented festivals of play according to the science of Kandarpa, and so on."

1011In these lovely places Krishna, full of rasa,
sports in the four kinds of the kaishora age.

1012Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in the section on uddipanas, the fifth verse:
"There, in madhura-rasa, age is said to be of four kinds:
the transitional, and also the new, the manifest and the full — in that order."270

1013Look: [here is] Karela-kunda, the forest of karil;
here Krishna, staying, gazes at the beauty.271

1014On Mount Nandishvara are the footprints of Krishna;
many see [their] power — so the elders say.

1015Here is Madhusudana-kunda amid the flower groves;
here is Krishna's great joy: the bees hum.272

1016Look: Panihari-kunda, supremely pure;
at mealtime Krishna drinks this water.273

1017And here, look, Srinivasa, is the kitchen:
here Radha joyfully cooks together with Rohini.274

1018Here Krishna takes His meal with His friends;
after walking a hundred steps, He comes here and lies down [to rest].275

1019Sri Radhika, having tasted the remnants of Krishna's food,
goes and sits in this pleasant garden within the homestead.

1020A friend, unnoticed by anyone, brings Krishna and unites [Them];
whatever merriment arises — who could find its end?

1021Here Sri Yashoda, having dressed Rama and Krishna,
sends [Them] off to the forest — and her heart breaks.

1022Amid Their friends, Rama and Krishna along this road
go to herd the cows — to what could that beauty be compared?

1023Here Yashoda, taking Radha on her lap
and sending [Her] off to Javata, is bathed in tears.

1024How much affection she has for Lalita and the other friends —
who could tell of it with a single mouth?

1025Yashoda and Rohini, having sent off Radhika with Her friends,
cannot become calm.

1026Look: here is the place where curd is churned;
and here, look — the boundless power of the goddess.276

1027Paurnamasi, having come and said much to Yashoda,
goes joyfully along this road to her own dwelling.

1028Here, a little way off, in this secluded place, Vrinda-devi
ponders in her mind how to unite the two of Them.

1029Having united the two of Them, she and her friends are bathed in happiness;
who would not proclaim such virtues of Vrinda?

1030Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the thirty-first verse:
"She who, filled with a flood of prema, having adorned one after another
the ever-new kunjas with abundant fragrant flowers —
ah! — arranges there the festival of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna,
surrounded by Their dear ones — in that Vrinda I take refuge."

1031Here is Sahasi-kunda: here a friend, having inspired Krishna
with boldness, unites [Him] with Rai.277

1032Here, having made a wondrous swing on the branch of a tree,
Rai and Kanu swing with Their friends, overwhelmed with happiness.

1033Here is Mukta-kunda: here the son of Nanda
made a field of pearls — and there was boundless merriment.278

1034O Srinivasa, this is Akrura's place;
when one tells of him, the heart breaks.279

1035Sent by Kamsa from Mathura, Akrura
was to take Rama and Krishna away to the city of Madhu.

1036For this reason, coming here, he reflects within himself
and sees here the footprints of Krishna.

1037Here Akrura was overwhelmed with prema;
this place of Akrura people call Krur.280

1038Look: [here is] Yogiya-sthana — here Uddhava
spoke of yoga in many ways.281

1039This is Udho-kriya-sthana: here Uddhava,
seeing the conduct of the gopis, considered himself blessed.282

1040Here Uddhava consoled Nanda and the others;
seeing [their] wondrous bhava, he lost his composure.

1041For some days Uddhava stayed here;
by seeing this place all aims are fulfilled.

1042Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-ninth verse:
"He who is always full of the rasa of prema, the servant and friend of the Enemy of Mura,
leaving His two feet, dearer to him than millions of his own lives,
lovingly lived here for ten months and with talk of Him again and again revived the cowherd settlement,
[saying,] 'Look, Krishna is coming!' — that Uddhava I carry on my head."

1043O Srinivasa, here Krishna with His friends
decides where they will go to herd the cows.

1044Look, Srinivasa, all these are the places of the cowsheds;
here are Krishna's pastimes with the cowherds.

1045Krishna with Subala and the others, with a joyful heart —
exceedingly beautiful [is He] going to this forest.

1046Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Dhanashri):
"Today Kanu comes to the forest — Kusumabana embodied;
[His] body lovely as a dense rain-cloud, the posture of the best of dancers enchanting.
His moon-face smiles slightly, His eyes are a snare for the eyes of young women;
on His lips, [red as] the bimba, the playing of the flute enchants the minds of the three worlds.283

1047His locks are entwined with flowers — all around the bees and she-bees hum;
a crown made of a mass of peacock feathers, makara earrings swaying.
His restless eyes — a pair of khanjana birds — again and again run toward His ears;
on His neck shine kingly jewels, a pearl necklace swings.

1048At His waist are yellow cloth and shining kinkini bells; His intoxicated gait surpasses the king of elephants;
a kadamba garland hangs to His knees, [over it] enraptured, intoxicated bees.
His lotus feet of reddish hue put to shame the rays of the young sun;
delighting the heart of Govindadasa, the lovely anklets sweetly ring."284

1049Look: the pegs to which the calves are tied —
the women of Vraja worship them with care even today.

1050At Nandishvara there are many places of Krishna's pastimes;
it is impossible to tell which pastime was where.

1051To the right and left of this parikrama path
there are many places of Krishna's pastimes — who can name them?

1052Having seen a few places on all four sides of Nandishvara,
we will again go on further by this path.

1053So saying, they set out from Nandagrama;
their joy grew as they looked on all four sides.

1054[Raghava] says to Srinivasa: "There is no end to this beauty;
to the northwest of Nandishvara, look — Gendukhora.285

1055Here at Gendukhora, joyfully taking a ball,
Rama and Krishna with Their friends are absorbed in the rasa of play.

1056Here, look, is the beautiful kadamba grove;
here Balarama sports in many delightful ways.

1057Here Baladeva lay down,
and Krishna massaged His feet.

1058Thus [it is said] in the Purva-gopala-champu, in the twelfth purana, the forty-eighth verse, a song:286
"Krishna plays around Rama, thirsting for the qualities of His friends' songs;
He sings after the song of the cuckoos and bees, chatters like the parrots and swans.

1059Likewise, with ringing laughter, He imitates the chakravakas, chakoras, cranes and other [birds]; to frighten the little ones, He produces as it were the cry of beasts terrified by a leopard's jaws.

1060Birds, beasts and others that make indistinct sounds — all of them He calls by names [He] has invented; and if some friend is wandering there, by laughter He draws out his affection too.

1061The animals that have strayed far He calls by name with a chant that delights the hearts of the cows and cowherds; when He called the cows, the cry of the peacocks arose, for that [call] was like the rumbling of a cloud.

1062Joining His hand with His brother's, He praises His friends' many good deeds and laughs; together with His friends, giving rest to the Elder, He performs the service of caressing His feet.

1063Having made a bed of tender shoots, resting His head firmly on a friend's thigh,
after the fatigue of play wishing to lie down — He whose body the most pious ones fan,

1064whose feet here some [of His friends] caress, whose service leaves us only thirst —287 He fell asleep to the songs and amusements of His loving [friends], delightful with melody.

1065For us who remember this, something in the heart can wait for its time, but cannot bear any other state; who are we here, only fancying ourselves thirsty, when the blessed ones headed by Shuka thirst for Him?"

1066Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Tenth Canto, in the fifteenth chapter, the fourteenth verse:288
"Sometimes, when the Elder, tired by play, laid His head in a cowherd boy's lap,
[Krishna] Himself gave Him rest by massaging His feet and serving Him in other ways."

1067This is Gupta-kunda: here, in secret, are various delights;
Krishna wanders in the forest with Subala and the others.289

1068Here, look, is the village of Meheran — everyone knows it;
here is the cowshed of the cowherd Abhinanda.290

1069O Srinivasa, and here is another lovely place:
look, this is Yaograma, called Javata.291

1070All the places of pastimes in the village of Javata
are most wondrous; who can tell how many there are?

1071Look, here is the dwelling of Abhimanyu;
here Rai enjoys Her pastimes with the sakhis.292

1072Abhimanyu, by the power of Sri Yogamaya,
cannot touch even Radhika's shadow — what to speak [of Her Herself].

1073Abhimanyu stays in his own company of cows and cowherds;
Jatila and Kutila are always busy with household work.

1074A clever sakhi, bringing Krishna here,
with delight in her heart beholds the pastimes of the Two.

1075Having tricked Jatila, Kutila and Abhimanyu,
Krishna, coming right here, playfully enjoys His pastimes.

1076Mukhara, seeing her granddaughter here, joyfully
speaks so many gentle words to Jatila.

1077Here Kutila, greatly pleased,
plots how to disgrace Radhika.

1078By this road Radhika goes to the temple of the Sun;
Krishna, staying in the kadamba grove, watches.

1079Coming out onto the road, He pulls at Radhika's garment;
great is the fun of Rai and Kanu, the Two of Them.

1080Thus [it is said] in the Gitavali of the Stavamala (raga Dhanashri):293
"Do not torment [me] here on the road,
seeing that I am a faithful wife, without protection.

1081Restless one, let go of the edge of my veil:
I must now perform the worship of the Sun. (Refrain.)

1082Do not delay, O hero of Gokula;
O moon-faced one, again and again I bow to you in entreaty.

1083Alone with you I am afraid, seeing you
with the corners of your eyes darting about, O Sanatana-deva."

1084This is Krishna-kunda, surrounded by banyans and other trees;
here Sri Krishna's pastimes are exceedingly charming.

1085This is Mukta-kunda: here in the hot season
a sakhi puts ornaments of pearls on Rai.

1086This is Pivana-kunda [and] the stream in the kadamba grove;
here Radha and Krishna happily sport with the sakhis.294

1087Supremely playful Krishna, receiving a sign from a sakhi,
intoxicated, drinks the nectar of Radhika's lips.

1088And this is Ladili-kunda: here Lalita
secretly arranges the meeting of Rai and Kanu.295

1089Look, O Srinivasa — Narada-kunda;
whoever bathes here has his desire fulfilled.

1090Here the sage gave Radhika a boon —
She became Amrita-hasta, as everyone knows.296

1091Here Sri Radhika, standing with the sakhis,
watches Sri Krishna when He goes to herd the cows.

1092With His friends, merrily playing the flute,
Krishna goes to herd the cows by this road.

1093Krishna, the enchanter of the worlds, amid the cows and cowherds
unnoticed gives His eyes to Rai's eyes.

1094Thus [it is said] in a song:
"The brightly shining cows of fierce majesty, honoured by the world — iya;
the restless dust from their hooves rose to the sky, delighting the hosts of gods — iya.297

1095He comes to the forest, delighting those who surrender [to Him]; [His] gait is lovely, putting the elephant to shame;
His softest body is like glossy collyrium; His eyes dance — young khanjana birds;
shattering the composure of beautiful women, He sports among the cowherds — iya.

1096His clear, shining face surpasses a forest of blossoming white lotuses;
His lovely locks, like bees, ripple in a dark wave — iya.

1097Ta ta thira mira kiti jhik jhik, jhankiti ta jhuk,
buddha jhik jhik jhik, tenati ai aiya.
Aiya! Shyamaghana, wondrously praised — iya. (Refrain.)298

1098The instruments sound, the singing is fine, the shrutis pure, the metre sweet in accord with the svaras; hearing the sound of the flute, Radhika leaves the house together with a host of sakhis.

1099She gazes at the charming attire of the best of dancers, Her unblinking eyes rejoicing; Manasija is strong, Her body trembles, from trembling Her gait is very slow.299

1100Ta ta takuta takuta nakuta, taku thai ta, thai thai diga ta, thaita,
ta ta kititak, tho di kiti tak,
thunna dramakata jha jha kitijhak, jhankana jhankana krina krina.

1101The corners of the eyes meet, the hearts of both are captured — who knows [this] wondrous attachment! Great is the merriment in the lanes of Vraja; [all is] immersed in Shyamaghana, the ocean of beauty; Shyamaghana sports — [all is] immersed [in Him].

1102Diga diga thai thai thai thai thaita, dhidhi kata dhidhi kata ti, ai aiya;
jha kina kina jha, kina kina kina jha, jha kina kina jha,
jhankana jhankana krina krina krina."

1103O Srinivasa, in this village of Javata
Krishna meets Radhika with great merriment.

1104Radha's sister-in-law Kutila and mother-in-law Jatila
cannot perceive Krishna's boundless cunning.

1105What to say — there is no end to all those joys;
the fortunate ones relish them in many ways.

1106Thus [it is said] in a song. Once (in any raga):300
The best of the best of nagaras, the stealer of Vraja's peace,
His heart joyful, full of the rasa [of love] for His beloved,
having made ready flowers, taking the guise of a malini,
enters the village of Javata.301

1107Looking at Himself again and again,
covering His face with the end of His cloth, smiling,
in a very sweet voice He calls at every house:
"Who will take a garland? Come, take one!"

1108Hearing a voice that surpasses the cuckoo,
Vinodini says to Her sakhi Vishakha:
"It must be a wondrous garland; lest someone else take it,
quickly bring the malini here."302

1109Vishakha, hearing these words, in the greatest joy
says to the malini: "Hey, come here!"
Turning the malini back, she leads [Him] into the house
and lovingly says: "Sit right here."

1110Looking at the malini, Radhika runs to meet [her]
and, delighted, thinks to Herself:
"Such a malini as this I have seen nowhere —
surely she must be a dweller of the city of the gods."

1111Thinking so in Her heart, sitting beside the malini,
[She] says: "Come, show me your garland."
Hearing this, [the malini] shows the garland, which has no comparison:
by its beauty it enchants everyone's mind.

1112Radhika, full of rasa, greatly
tormented by Madana, again thrills in Her heart.
Looking at the garland, She reflects in Her mind:
"Just so does my beloved string [garlands]."

1113The beautiful one cannot be calm and says to the malini:
"I feel like giving you my life!
What can I say of your skill? Blessed, blessed are you!
Tell me what the price is."

1114The malini says: "Listen, I will not say it again and again;
I never tell anyone an untruth.
I will put this garland on [you], and I will take that gaja-moti;
once [you] are adorned, whatever you give I will take afterwards."303

1115The young beauty speaks kind words to the malini:
"Whatever you wish — take it as you please."
Hearing this, [the malini], floating in rasa, with a slight smile, smiling,
puts the garland on Radhika's neck.

1116With great care arranging [the garland]
over the lovely hills of Her breasts, covers [them] with a hand;
at the malini's touch, with delight in Her heart,
the young beauty at once trembles all over.

1117Understanding [all], — [says] Narahari, — all the companions
stay at a distance, glad at heart.
In the secluded chamber, unable to remain calm,
the Two become intoxicated in the play of Ananga.

1118And once (raga Pauravi):
The best of nagaras, the moon of Vraja, taking a fine woman's attire, smiling,
full of rasa, enters Javata.
Surpassing a rain-laden cloud, the radiance of each graceful limb [of His body]
[and] the beauty of the clothes and ornaments He wears steal the life-breath.

1119Radhika, seeing Him from afar, cannot turn Her eyes away even for a moment
and says to Her sakhi, taking [her] by the hand:
"Where has this beautiful woman come from? Look, she has lit up everything with her beauty!
Bring her right here, with every courtesy."

1120Hearing Vinodini's agitated words, the sakhi, knowing [Her] heart,
hurries to where that beautiful woman is coming;
cleverly going near, speaking the sweetest words,
she joyfully brings Him and leads Him with honour into the house.

1121The beautiful woman joyfully comes near; the jewel among women, seating Him,
lovingly says: "I have never seen you.
Today I have found boundless happiness — I speak the truth, without guile.
On what business are you going alone, and where? Tell me."

1122Hearing words like nectar, the beautiful woman, plunged in still greater happiness,
like a poor man who has found the greatest jewel,
looking at the lovely moon-face, with cunning in mind says:
"Listen: since you have asked, I must tell you something.

1123With great eagerness, as my heart desired, I learned all the art of adornment;
I put endless effort into it, young though I am.
To display all this I wander through this town of Vraja,
but I find no expert who could judge such skill.

1124And then a woman said to me: 'In vain do you wander through the town:
here [lives] the wife of Abhimanyu, supremely skilful.
What is Rama [beside her] in beauty and virtues? In the world there is none equal to her;
by the touch of her feet the earth counts itself blessed.304

1125There are many heroines here — how much could I tell of them! —
who cannot keep Him in their power even for a moment.
But that moon Shyama, the best of the accomplished, above whom there is no one,
subdued by her prema, constantly roams [after her].

1126Go there, heed [my] word: there your skill will be honored.'
Hearing this, I was greatly delighted at heart.
Why should I repeat her words to you? I came, heeding what she said;
just as she told [me], so I have found [it]."

1127Hearing these words, beautiful Rai, feeling great joy at heart,
says: "Dress me, dear, regarding [me] as your own."
Having received [this] kindly permission, [the guest] eagerly rises and sits beside [Her];
a maidservant brings all the articles of adornment.

1128Carefully, keeping [her] composure, the lovely one, gazing at the sweet charm of [Rai's] back,
braids the plait — [like] a serpent, at the sight [of which] the sages lose their senses.
With a heart delighted by the rasa of touch, applying lovely kajal to [Her] eyes,
with the end of the sari [she] lovingly wipes [Her] face — [and it] shines all the more.

1129Placing lovely champaka [flowers] on [Her] ears, [the guest] deems herself blessed;
applying sindur in the parting of the hair, [she] paints designs on [Her] forehead.
Putting a beshar pendant in [Her] nose and swinging it, [she] speaks sweet words:
"There is no comparison [for You]: at this Madana will surely swoon."

1130As [she] places a lovely dot of musk on [Her] chin, an ocean of bliss surges up;
seeing this, [she] cannot turn away [her] unblinking eyes.
Touching the most lovely breasts, [she] puts on [Her] bodice — and [her] hands tremble:
the Holder of the mountain cannot keep even a trace of composure.

1131The incomparable body quivers again and again; tenderly [the guest] presses [her] face to that face;
seeing this, a sakhi, putting a finger to her chin, says:
"What an unheard-of wonder! Being a woman, with a woman
you do such a thing — how ever can you [do it]?

1132A wondrous attire you have made! What shall I say to my own friend?
Without discerning, she takes anyone at all as her own.
It is well that no one is here — otherwise this would be most shameful.
To whom shall I tell this sorrow? She never heeds any prohibition."

1133Hearing this, smiling Rai, abashed, looking at Shyama,
says: "Oh, you rogue! Who would not laugh at this?"
The Nagara says: "Do what is proper: quickly bind [me] in the noose of your arms —
then Ghanashyama will float in the ocean of happiness."305

1134And at another time — raga Gauri:306
Shyama, the best of handsome nagaras, the giver of joy, having devised a plan with Kundalata,307
takes on the wondrous guise of a woman, joyful in the hope of seeing Rai.
Virtuous Kundalata, sent by Yashoda, goes to Javata with incomparable gait;
with her goes the Beautiful One, carrying in lovely hands a plate with some articles.

1135Entering Javata, seeing Jatila, with a joyful heart [Kundalata] bows at her feet;
taking [her] by the hand, Abhimanyu's mother speaks so many sweet words of every kind.
Kundalata, showing her cleverness there, sitting close by, displays the articles,
conveys Yashomati's words and, having received permission, goes to where Rai is staying.

1136Rasavati, filled with great joy, smiling and looking at Kundalata,
in so many ways playfully, lovingly taking [her] by the hand, seats [her] beside [Her].
Having carefully asked about the beloved of [Her] life, Rai, glancing at that [guest], speaks again:
"Where did you find this new merry girl? And why has she come with you?"

1137Hearing, Kundalata, floating in bliss, says: "[She] lives in our neighborhood,
this young wife, very dear to me; [who she is], I will tell later.
Hearing from my lips the account of your virtues, every day she longs to come here;
seeing how she pines, I brought [her] today; regard [her] as your own.

1138With many virtues the Creator has fashioned her — to whom in the world could I compare her? She always keeps very much to herself, is skilled in her own work, of lovely conduct. What more shall I say of her cleverness: her touch drives away the pains of the body and the rest. O blissful one, among your sakhis no one has such soft hands."

1139Hearing, Vinodini, her heart delighted, wished [that one] to touch [Her] body; understanding [this], Kundalata, making a sign to the dark young wife,308 says with a slight smile: "The wish that was in your heart is fulfilled: Radha has accepted you as her own; so [now] with the lovely lotuses of your hands press [Her] feet and pour forth floods of nectar."

1140Hearing [these] words, feeling great happiness at heart, gazing to the full at the face as if smeared with nectar, [the guest], sitting beside the couch, smiles softly and, overflowing with rasa, touches [Her] feet. Startled, Rai's body trembles restlessly — like a golden creeper in the wind, like lightning; displaying incomparable skill, smiling, the moon Shyama cannot remain still.

1141Wondrous: each of the Two captivates the other's heart; in the play of prema the beauty of both grows manifold; there is no end to new embraces, frequent kisses; abundant thrills fill [Their] limbs. Far off, the sakhis, with great happiness at heart, smiling, keep their faces covered with their cloth; exchanging signs from the corners of their eyes, [they] tease Kundalata.

1142Choosing the moment, Kundalata again, smiling, coming there to Vinodini's side,
looking at Shyama, says to Rai: "What an unseemly thing you have done!
You embraced the young wife as if she were your sweetheart — I do not know what she will think.
Had I known you would act like this, I would not have brought her."

1143Rai playfully, with lowered face, says: "I understand: having bidden farewell to shame for good, dressing up your own brother-in-law like this, you take him along and enjoy yourself every day.309 For so many days this was a secret; be that as it may, now it has come to light." Thus the two say so much; hearing it, Ghanashyama's mind is utterly immersed [in bliss].

1144Again, raga Gauri:
Shyama, the handsome nagara, the ocean of rasa,
overwhelmed with the hope of seeing Rai,
seeing the moonrise, taking on the guise of a brahmana,
went to Javata, to Jatila.

1145Seeing the excellent brahmana, joining both palms,
bowing to Him, Jatila says:
"Today I deem myself blessed; [I wish to] hear your words —
tell [me], why have you come to a cowherd's house?"

1146Hearing, the Dvijaraja says: "I have a purpose:310
having worshiped the moon, today I have eaten nothing.
Knowing your daughter-in-law to be devoted to her husband,
I have come to receive something from her hand."

1147Hearing this, Jatila, delighted,
speaks sweet words to Vishakha:
"Take [him] to where Radha is;
whatever he asks, let her give it, deeming [it] a meritorious deed.

1148Tell her, joining her palms and clasping [his] feet,
to receive [his] blessing.
Misfortune will go, good fortune will come —
cows and wealth — by the boon of this brahmana."

1149Hearing this, taking the brahmana along,
[Vishakha] came to where the jewel of women [was];
she conveyed the words of the mother-in-law —
hearing them, [Rai] felt supreme joy.

1150Seating the brahmana on a wonderful seat,
bowing, speaking humble words,
curd, milk, ghee and all such things
[She] carefully brought before [Him].

1151The brahmana, looking again and again at Rai,
says to Vishakha: "Listen, sakhi!
The moon whom I worship every day in so many ways —
that moon I see in her face.

1152I have found [it] close at hand — how could I neglect [it]?
First I must drink the nectar."
Saying this, smiling, floating in the rasa of prema,
[He] kissed the moon of Rai's face.

1153Vinodini says: "What is this you are doing, hey!
You are a brahmana — why do you act like this?"
The brahmana says: "My hunger and the sorrow of my heart are gone —
I find happiness in drinking the nectar of [your] lips."

1154Rasavati in anger says to Vishakha:
"I do not understand this game of yours."
Vishakhika replies: "I have understood:
[this is] an unearthly pastime of mother-in-law and daughter-in-law!"

1155Hearing, the Moon-faced One laughs with lowered eyes;
seeing this, Ghanashyama, the Beloved, smiling,
taking Rai on His lap, trembles all over —
how He floats in that play of Ananga!

1156What shall I say, O Srinivasa, O Narottama!
Krishna's charming pastimes are hard to attain even for Brahma.

1157Krishna, the embodiment of rasa, knows all languages;
He is most skilled at imitating the calls of cuckoos and other [birds].

1158By means of agreed signals He meets [Radha] in Abhimanyu's house;
[but] by the will of fate on some days the meeting does not happen.

1159Thus [it is said] in the Padyavali:
"The enemy of Kamsa gave the agreed signal — the call of a cuckoo and other [birds] —
and again and again heard the jingling of the conch-shell bangles, trembling as the door was being opened;
[but] His heart was tormented by the words of the bold old woman, 'Who is it? Who is it?' —
and [so His] night passed in the shelter of the koli tree in the corner of Radha's courtyard."311

1160Krishna, the great jester, full of supreme bliss,
for the good fortune of the cuckoos meets [Her] by means of that call.

1161To the west of Javata is this charming forest;
hundreds of thousands of cuckoos call [here] without ceasing.

1162One day Krishna, coming to this forest,
joyfully makes a call like [that of] a cuckoo —

1163sweeter than [the voice of] all the cuckoos;
whoever hears it even once, his composure goes far away.

1164Jatila kindly says to Vishakha:
"Never have I heard such a cuckoo's call."

1165Vishakha says: "This is in the minds of all of us:
if you allow, we will go to the forest and see this cuckoo."

1166The old woman says, "Go." Hearing [this], with boundless joy
Rai entered the forest together with the sakhis.

1167There was great merriment, there was no limit to happiness;
all, coming, met in one place.

1168By the cuckoo's call Krishna unites with Radhika —
therefore this [place] is called Kokilavana.312

1169O Srinivasa, look: [here is] the village of Ajanak;
here the pastimes of Radha and Krishna are incomparable.313

1170Sri Radhika was dressing in seclusion;
She was adorned with many jewels and [other] ornaments.

1171Having arranged Her hair and the rest, [She was about] to apply anjana,
[when] suddenly the sound of the flute entered [Her] ears.

1172That very moment Sri Radhika, together with the sakhis,
coming here, met Krishna with great delight.

1173Going forward [and] leading [Her] in, Krishna was overwhelmed
[and] seated [Her] on a flower seat made by Vrinda.

1174He sees the beauty of [Her] limbs, [but] does not see anjana in [Her] eyes;
when He asked, the sakhis told what had happened.

1175Overcome by rasa, Krishna, taking anjana,
with great joy applied [it] to Radhika's eyes.

1176On the pretext of the anjana there was much joking;
therefore the name of this place became Ajanak.

1177This is the village of Vidyudvari; [people] call [it] Bijoari;
who would not melt on hearing the story of this village?314

1178O Srinivasa, when Akrura came to Vraja,
this cry arose: "He has come to take Rama and Krishna!"

1179Having joyfully spent the night in Nanda's house,
at dawn [Akrura] sets out for Mathura together with Nanda and the others.

1180Vraja became empty with the departure of Rama and Krishna;
what is there to say — whoever saw it, he [alone] knows.

1181The women of Vraja run to see Krishna;
tears stream from their eyes like the current of a river.

1182At the sight of that state wood and stone split apart;
no one could describe it even with hundreds of thousands of mouths.

1183On all sides Krishna's beloveds are distraught;
and here Krishna mounted the chariot.

1184The gopis fixed their eyes on the lotus of Krishna's face
and, crying, "Alas, alas, Lord of [our] life!", fell senseless.

1185As a mass of steady lightning falls from the sky,
so the gopis fall to the earth.

1186Everyone took [them] for a mass of lightning —
for this reason [the village] has the name Bijoari.

1187Look: ahead is the village named Parasho;
how it got the name Parasho, I will tell briefly.315

1188Mounting the chariot, Krishna set out for Mathura;
seeing the state of the gopis, He became distraught.
