1189Through a messenger He said, swearing an oath:
"Tomorrow or the day after I will come and meet [you]."

1190For this reason its name became Parasho;
I do not know how to tell what the gopis went through.

1191Near Parasho is this village named Shi;
I will tell briefly how the name Shi came about.316

1192Here Krishnachandra cannot keep His composure;
seeing the state of the gopis, He says again and again:

1193"From Mathura I will come [back] soon."
For this reason [from "shighra," "soon"] everyone calls [it] Shi.

1194Mounting the chariot, Krishnachandra goes to Mathura;
without Krishna the gopis became all but lifeless.

1195Together with the collyrium of the eyes of countless gopis,
the tears of their eyes, flowing down their breasts, fall to the earth.

1196Merging together, the water flows like a river;
all say: "This is a stream of the Yamuna."

1197This is the place full of the gopis' tears of prema;
O Srinivasa, the fortunate one sees it.

1198Look: here are two villages, Kamai and Karala;317
in the village of Kamai Vishakha was born.

1199Here in the village of Karala is Lalita's place;
it is known in Vraja that she also lived in the village of Ludhauni.

1200In this village of Karala resides Chandravali,
whose husband is Govardhana, the son of Karala.318

1201Her father is Chandrabhanu, her mother Indumati;
Chandravali is the elder sister of Radhika.319

1202Sri Chandravali's father is [one of] five brothers born of one mother;
the eldest of all is Vrishabhanu, the best of kings.

1203Chandrabhanu, Ratnabhanu, Subhanu, Shribhanu —
in order; the splendour of these five is as if like the sun's.

1204Govardhana Malla together with Chandravali
[lives] in the village of Sakhisthali, and sometimes stays in Karala.

1205Padma and the other group leaders live in this place;320
how they meet Krishna — there is no end to that fun.

1206There, in the village of Piyaso, Krishna became thirsty;321
Baladeva brought water and gave Krishna to drink.

1207In this village of Sahara is the dwelling of Upananda,322
advanced in years, very wise in counsel.

1208Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixteenth verse: "He whose face is beautiful with an abundance of white beard, dark, skilful, versed in counsel, who always has his place in the assembly of the lord of Vraja and is honoured, who would gladden the Slayer of Mura, his brother's son, at the cost of hundreds of millions of his own lives — dwelling in Sahara, he who is called Upananda, may he always protect the cowherd settlement."

1209Wonderful is the affection that the cowherd Upananda shows;
his son Subhadra is Krishna's elder brother.323

1210He is dear to Sri Nanda; his virtues cannot be told;
he is very learned, boundlessly affectionate to Krishna.

1211Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the seventeenth verse:
"Dark, of subtle mind, exceedingly sweet [in speech], foremost among the knowers of the heavenly bodies,324
who by his learning has surpassed the Lord of Speech, who has his place at the left hand of the lord of Vraja,
who here lovingly protects Krishna completely, even with hundreds of millions of lives,
and with counsel — him, the son of Upananda, Subhadra, we here praise with love."

1212The wife of Subhadra is named Kundalata;
Krishna is the life of her, Radhika's sakhi.325

1213Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the thirty-second verse:
"She who, most charming with abundant friendship adorned with jests,
by order of the queen of the lord of Vraja brings Radha for the cooking,
and, all along the way, constantly and lovingly delighting [Her] with news of Hari,
is herself supremely pleased — her, the Lata whose name begins with Kunda, I worship here."

1214The bliss that is in the village of Sahara day and night —
who has the power to tell of it in detail?

1215Look at this village named Sakhi: here326
Krishna Himself slew the wicked Shankhachuda.

1216The jewel that was on Shankhachuda's head [He] took,
and, coming to Baladeva, joyfully gave [it to him].

1217A little way from here, where Balarama was,
there is Rama-kunda; now its name is Rama-talao.327

1218Baladeva, through Madhumangala, gave the jewel
to Radhika — there was great fun in that.328

1219O Srinivasa, Narottama! Here
Rai with Her sakhis was overwhelmed with fun.

1220In Chhatravana the friends, having made Krishna king,
by the power of the king's command rule everywhere.

1221Madhumangala and all the others, with bold words,
roam from forest to forest, proclaiming Krishna's name:

1222"The great king, the Chhatrapati, is Nanda's son;329
in his kingdom no one else has any authority.

1223If anyone comes here to gather flowers,
we will punish him, taking him to the king."

1224Lalita and the other sakhis say angrily again and again:
"Who claims authority in Radhika's kingdom?"

1225Saying many such things, Lalita and the other sakhis
at that very moment made Radhika umrao.330

1226Sitting on a throne fit for an umrao, Rai,
looking in all four directions, says to the sakhis:

1227"Whoever claims authority in my kingdom —
defeat him and bring him here this very moment."

1228Hearing this, they arm themselves and go to fight,
taking in their hands flower staffs made by Vrinda.

1229Thousands upon thousands of sakhis go in all four directions;
Subala and the other friends see it from afar.

1230Without saying anything to Madhumangala, they ran away;331
some sakhi went and seized Madhumangala.

1231With a flower garland they bound his hands
and quickly brought him to the umrao.

1232Seeing Madhumangala, she says again and again:
"In whose kingdom are you establishing whose authority?

1233Together with all of you I will punish that king,
so that he never again does such a thing."

1234Hearing this, Madhu says, bowing his head:
"Punish me in such a way that my belly is filled."

1235The umrao says: "This brahmana who seeks only his belly —
release him; let him go into the king's presence."

1236The sakhis released Madhumangala;
still bound, Madhu ran off.

1237The king, sitting in great pride on the royal throne,
says to Madhumangala: "Why are you in such a state?"

1238Dejected, Madhu says again and again:
"I made You king — this is the fruit of it.

1239She is the umrao, Her power is boundless;
what authority will You establish in Her kingdom?

1240That Kandarpa who steals the world's treasure of composure —
that Kandarpa trembles at the play of Her eyes.

1241Therefore accept my counsel:
offering Yourself, take refuge in Her."

1242Krishna says: "Madhu, what you have said is above all;
that they bound you — that pain I cannot bear."

1243Madhu says: "I want only Your welfare;
even if I am dishonoured, there is no sorrow."

1244Saying this, pulling Krishna by the hand,
he comes that very moment to Radhika.

1245Seeing the coming of the Lord of Her life, Rai in happiness
lost Her composure — there is no limit to Her shyness.

1246Rai wants to take off the umrao's attire;
a sakhi says: "In this attire you will stay here."

1247Seeing Radhika in such attire from afar, Krishna
became agitated and cannot keep His composure.

1248Seeing Krishna's state, Madhu, with joy in his heart,
quickly brought Krishna to Radhika.

1249He seated Krishna at Radhika's right side;
Rai at Krishna's left — what wonderful beauty appeared!

1250Madhu says to Radhika again and again:
"Now take possession of the kingdom of Krishna's body.332

1251The jewel of an embrace that Krishna will give —
that is the tribute to you; accept it with care."

1252Hearing Madhu's words, Lalita, laughing happily,
put a sweet, a modaka, into Madhumangala's mouth.

1253Madhu says: "You committed an offence — you bound me;
feed me a hundred thousand such laddus, and the offence will go."

1254Saying this, he eats the modaka with comic gestures
and gazes at the beauty of the two of Them, surrounded by the sakhis.

1255Having eaten the modaka, in very sweet words
saying, "I have much to do," he goes off joyfully.

1256The umrao and the king — both entered
the nikunja house with very joyful hearts.

1257In the battle of love both became tired;
with various amusements the sakhis removed [Their] fatigue.

1258O Srinivasa, what more is there to say of this play?
For this reason this village is called Umrao.

1259Exceedingly dear to the daughter of Vrishabhanu
is this Kishori-kunda, always full of beauty.333

1260Seeing this wonderful forest, with great joy in his heart,
Lokanatha Gosvami lived here.

1261His renunciation — there is no end to telling of it;
Sri Radha-vinoda showed [him] mercy at this place.

1262Fruits, roots, greens, food — whatever was obtained at any time
he would carefully offer to Sri Radha-vinoda.

1263In the rains, the cold and so on, he lived under this tree;
with him a worn patched quilt and a very worn outer cloth.

1264He himself would get soaked by the water of heavy rains,
but he kept the Deity in the hollow of this tree.

1265At other times, placing [Him] in a worn bag,
he kept [Him] at his chest with a very joyful heart.

1266Remembering the pastimes of Sri Gaurachandra,
he would become distraught and weep here.

1267Having said many such things, he cannot hold himself back:
Raghava Pandita swims in the tears of his eyes.

1268Srinivasa and Narottama roll in the dust,
heave long sighs, float in streams of tears.

1269After some time Sri Pandita, becoming calm
and calming the two, goes on ahead, taking them both.

1270The Pandita says: this village is Nari-Semari;334
Shyamari-Kinnari is the former name of this village.

1271Seeing no way to break Radhika's sulking (mana),
here Sri Krishna became Shyama-sakhi.335

1272Playing the vina, [He] came here;
Sri Radhika says: "This is a kinnari in every way."336

1273Hearing the vina's playing, Rai was overwhelmed
and put Her own jewel necklace around her neck.

1274The kinnari says: "Give Me the jewel of your sulking;
be gracious and make Me your own."

1275Hearing these words, Rai smiles gently, gently;
Her mana vanished — She was immersed in delight.

1276In this way these two villages received their names;
here the power of this Devi is boundless.337

1277O Srinivasa, ahead, look — Chhatravana;
here the son of the lord of Vraja became king.338

1278When Krishna had become king, after some days Paurnamasi,
floating in happiness, performed Radhika's anointing [to the throne].

1279The anointing of Radha, queen of Vrindavana, at the place Radha-sthali —
who could tell what merriment [there was]?339

1280Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixty-first verse:
"Where, together with the hosts of rivers headed by Manasi-ganga, bearing an abundance of colors,
and with the hosts of goddesses headed by Savitri, at the heavenly voice of the Creator,
Sri Paurnamasi, for the supreme kingdom of Vrindavana, joyfully
abundantly sprinkled Radha — may that Radha-sthali sprinkle us with happiness."340

1281Look: Khadiravana, known to the world;
merely by coming here one attains Vishnu-loka.341

1282Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The seventh forest on earth is Khadira, renowned in the world;
having gone there, O auspicious one, a man goes to My world."

1283O Srinivasa, look: here Krishna
with His friends, while herding the cows, plays many games.

1284Look: Sangama-kunda, exceedingly charming;
here is the sweet meeting of the gopis with Krishna.342

1285Here it is supremely secluded; here Lokanatha
from time to time lived happily together with Bhugarbha.

1286Here is this Kadamba-khandi — enchanting is its beauty;
here the young son of the lord of Vraja performs wonderful pastimes.343

1287This is the village of Bakathara, near Javata;
here Krishna killed the demon Baka.344

1288This is the place Neochhak — look, Srinivasa;
here Sri Krishna enjoys His meal.

1289In Vraja, eatables are called by the word "chhak";
Krishna will eat — therefore Yashoda sends [them here].

1290And all the mothers of the cowherd boys,
all of them send eatables to this forest.

1291This is the village of Bhandagora — look, Srinivasa;
here are Sri Krishna's most wonderful pastimes.

1292Now people call this village Bhadali;
bathing and so on in this kunda grants all perfections.

1293Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Next there is My secret [place] known as Bhandagora;
people, O Earth, attain perfection there — of this there is no doubt.

1294There, O fortunate one, is a kunda surrounded by trees, shrubs and creepers;
the man who, having fasted day and night, bathes there,

1295having gone to the world of the Vidyadharas, rejoices — this is firmly established. There, O Earth, I shall tell of a wonder — My supreme secret:

1296on the twenty-four dvadashis devotion to Me is established [there];
at midnight [people] hear singing that delights the ear."345

1297Having said this and shown many other places,
he, full of joy, came back to Nandishvara.

1298Having told Srinivasa a little about the deeds of Nanda and others,
he stood beside Sri Pavana-sarovara.

1299Seeing the hut of Sanatana Gosvami,
he lost his composure: tears pour from his eyes.

1300Raghava Pandita says to Srinivasa:
"I shall tell a little of how the Gosvami lived here.

1301Coming from Vrindavana to this secluded forest,
he, always overwhelmed by prema, worshipped Krishna.

1302He lived in secret, with no concern for food;
no one knew who was living in this place.

1303Krishna, in the guise of a cowherd boy, taking milk,
stood before the Gosvami, full of joy.

1304In the dress of a herder of cows, a turban gracing His head,
holding a pot of milk in His hand, He says to the Gosvami:

1305'You live in seclusion, no one knows you;
I saw you when I came to herd the cows.

1306Drink this milk, as I tell you;
I will take the pot — leave it here.

1307If you live in a hut, all of us will be happy;
but you live like this — because of it the Vrajavasis will grieve.'

1308Having said this, Gopala went away;
Sanatana, enchanted, drank the milk.

1309As soon as he drank the milk, he lost his composure in prema;
drenched in tears, he lamented greatly.

1310The Lord, remaining unseen, consoled Sanatana
and through the Vrajavasis had a hut built.

1311Thus Sanatana came to have a dwelling;
from time to time Sri Rupa too stayed here.

1312One day Sri Rupa Gosvami
resolved to feed Sanatana milk-rice and other things.

1313Having resolved this, he again felt hesitant;
Radhika came to know what was in Sri Rupa's heart.

1314Taking ghee, milk, rice, sugar and other things,
She came in the guise of a cowherd girl, full of joy.

1315She says to Rupa: 'Svami, take all this;
quickly cook it, offer it to Krishna and eat.

1316My mother told me to say these words:
let there never be any hesitation in your heart.'

1317Having said this, Sri Radhika playfully went away;
Sri Rupa Gosvami happily and quickly cooked [the meal].

1318Having offered it to Krishna, he serves [the meal]
to Gosvami Sanatana with a heart full of supreme bliss.

1319Sanatana Gosvami, from the fragrance of the dishes,
does not know how much happiness arises in his heart.

1320Putting one or two mouthfuls into his mouth, Sanatana
lost his composure: his tears cannot be stopped.

1321Sanatana asked where the dishes had come from;
Sri Rupa told him everything in order.

1322Hearing it, the Gosvami forbids him again and again:
'Do not trouble like this over eatables any more.'

1323Having said this, he honored the Sri maha-prasada;
Sri Rupa Gosvami became deeply grieved.

1324Sri Radhika, giving [him] Her darshan in a dream,
consoled Sri Rupa; Sanatana came to know [of it].

1325O Srinivasa, what Sri Rupa's composure was like —
[this] wonder became manifest in the assembly of the Vaishnavas.

1326One day, during talk of the separation of Radha and Krishna,
the Vaishnavas weep, falling senseless to the ground.

1327Rupa's heart blazes like a tongue of flame,
and yet outwardly nothing shows.

1328Sri Rupa's breath touched someone's body —
and blisters rose on his body, as if burnt by fire.

1329Seeing this, everyone was astonished;
such are Sri Rupa's deeds — what more is there to say?

1330What can I say — how much happiness there is in this Nandishvara!"
Having said this, he goes to the Gosvami's holy hut.

1331There is the brahmana Sri Gopala Mishra, of noble conduct,
the son of Sanatana Gosvami's priest,

1332a disciple of Sri Sanatana, fine in every respect;
seeing them all, his heart rejoiced.

1333Sri Uddhava Dasa, Madhava and all who were there,
meeting one another, all became greatly joyful.346

1334The Vrajavasis, with jubilant hearts,
at once had eatables brought.

1335That day there was a great festival there;
all spent the night in nama-sankirtana.

1336Whoever hears such a wonderful account
will soon obtain the treasure of prema for Krishna.

1337Sri Gopala Dasa and all the other wise ones —
the hearts of all were filled with great joy.

1338Sri Raghava, taking the two, at daybreak,
having taken leave, goes along the path of the parikrama.

1339Sri Pandita says to Srinivasa and Narottama:
ahead, look — this is the village of Baithan.347

1340Whenever the cowherds hold counsel,
they all come here and sit down.

1341Here the cowherds sit — therefore this is Baithan;
now people call [it] by two names: Little and Big.

1342Bound by the love of the Vrajavasis, with a joyful heart
Sanatana Gosvami lived here.

1343How he lived here — of those beautiful deeds
I shall tell a little: by them the world is purified.

1344These Vrajavasis constantly
hold Sanatana Gosvami dearer than life.

1345When the Gosani makes the parikrama of Vraja,
he stays in village after village — there is no limit to that happiness.

1346When, having stayed in one village, he goes to another,
the people of the village run after the Gosvami.

1347Whether children or old people — no one can keep composure;
in separation from the Gosvami everyone weeps.

1348Sanatana Gosvami, weeping too,
consoles them and sends them back to their homes.

1349When all, restraining their weeping, have gone to their homes,
then Sanatana quickly goes on to another village.

1350Whatever village he was heading for, the people of that village
see from afar Sanatana coming.

1351Children, old people, young men, women and men —
all say, "Look, here is Rupa-Sanatana!"348

1352Wondrous is the love of the Vrajavasis:
even on seeing Rupa they say, "Rupa-Sanatana."

1353None of the village folk can stay still:
they go out ahead to bring Sanatana in.

1354As a poor man is happy on obtaining many jewels,
so is everyone happy on seeing Sanatana.

1355All the very old and the old, women and men,
cherish Sanatana as a son.

1356Someone says, "Ah, son, having forgotten us,
how have you lived? Where [were you]? We were dying with worry over it."

1357Speaking thus, all gaze at Sanatana's face,
perform nirmanchhana with their own selves and feel great happiness at heart.

1358Women, men and young people who were born in that village —
all of them, in the feeling of brothers, are overwhelmed with love.

1359Someone says, "Brother, how have you lived?
It seems you never once remembered us.

1360Why, brother, have you become so heartless towards us?"
So they say many things, and streams of tears flow from their eyes.

1361Girls and boys come up to touch his feet;
he holds them all back, but cannot hold them back.

1362The young wives of the village, staying a little way off,
all look at him, shyly.

1363O Srinivasa, at the sight of Sanatana
no one even remembers to offer obeisances and the like.

1364As he enters the village, all who come running to him
embrace him tightly and lead him along, holding his hand.

1365Beneath a beautiful tree all, with joy in their hearts,
seat Sanatana and sit around him on all four sides.

1366Curd, milk, fresh butter and other things from their homes
all bring with care to feed Sanatana.

1367Having finished the merry meal after a while,
everyone, settled and calm, sits happily.

1368Sanatana Gosvami, in deep affection,
asks everyone about their welfare in every respect:

1369how many daughters and sons each has, where they are married,
what each one's name is, how the elders are, whether they live free from fear;

1370how many cows, bulls and so on each has, how each one's farming goes,
how much grain is in whose house, how their affairs stand;

1371how each one's health is, what each one's state of mind.
When he asks thus, everyone becomes very glad.

1372One by one all tell the Gosvami everything;
hearing of anyone's sorrow, he himself becomes deeply sorrowful.

1373Sanatana's consolation destroys their sorrow;
in such talks the night turns to dawn.

1374In the morning Sanatana quickly performs his morning duties;
while he is bathing and so on, everyone comes.

1375All quickly bring curd, milk and so on
and ask Sanatana Gosvami to eat.

1376Sri Gosvami eats, having fed everyone,
and joyfully looks at how beautiful they all are.

1377As before, when he goes from the village,
the Vrajavasis weep in distress.

1378How they show their love — there is no end to telling it;
the Gosani consoles them all in many ways.

1379When all go along with him some distance,
he adjures them by himself to make them turn back.

1380Thus, going round from village to village,
Sanatana comes to the village of Baithan.

1381Seeing Sanatana, all the people of the village —
in what bliss they were immersed, who can tell, and how much?

1382Sanatana asks everyone about their welfare
and spends days and nights with joy in his heart.

1383To stay [in a village] one night — that is his rule, everyone knows it;
therefore, in distress, they say to Sanatana:

1384"If you stay a few days, it will be good for everyone.
Heed our words, do not be heartless.

1385In the morning you will leave — that is your rule.
Give up this rule, save everyone's life."

1386Thus the villagers say many things, weeping,
and for this reason he stayed here, giving happiness to all.

1387The people of Baithan village and all [the villages] nearby —
all are constantly immersed in Sanatana's virtues.

1388O Srinivasa, here there is great bliss.
Look at Nipavana: it enchants the mind with its beauty.349

1389Here is Krishna-kunda — here the pastimes are endless;
at this Kuntala-kunda Krishna dressed His hair.350

1390Here is the Bedokhor kunja: inside its little house
the Two delight, having shut the door of the kunja.351

1391Charana-pahari is the name of this hill;
here are the incomparable pastimes of Krishnachandra.352

1392Krishna, surrounded by His friends, climbed the hill;
far off the cows graze — He looks in all four directions.

1393In a form that enchants the world, taking the flute in His hand,
He stood beneath a tree, bent in three places.

1394The moment He began to play the flute, the world went mad;
all, wherever they were, came running [here].

1395Hearing the song of the flute, all became motionless;
what can compare with that song? — this hill melted.

1396Those who came here on hearing the sound of the flute —
look at their footprints on the stone.

1397Here the marks of Sri Krishna's lotus feet remained;
for this reason the name Charana-pahari arose.

1398Look: here is Krishna-kunda, the village of Haroyal;
here Rai and Ghanashyama joyfully delight.353

1399Playing at dice, Rai defeated Krishna;
having lost the game, Krishna was greatly ashamed.

1400Lalita says, "Rai, in the game of dice
you easily defeated the Lord of your life.

1401Your victory is in many ways.
We shall see who wins and who loses in Kandarpa's battle."

1402Having said this, the sakhis left the Two in the nikunja temple
and, themselves unseen, watch Their play.

1403Supreme bliss arose — what more is there to say?
In this Haroyal there are wondrous pastimes.

1404Look: the village named Satoha shines in its beauty;
here the sage Sri Shantanu worshipped Krishna.354

1405Surya-kunda, Nandana-kupa, Vadya-shila, and also
a wondrous hill — here are Krishna's pastimes.355

1406Look at the village of Pai: Rai with Her friends,
searching for Krishna, found [Him] here.356

1407Look at this Chalana-shila: here Shyama-raya
cannot walk for prema and sits down on the stone.357

1408Look at the village of Kamari: here Krishna,
tormented by desire, gazes at the path by which Rai [is to come].358

1409Look at this village of Bichhor: here the Moon-faced One
meets with Krishna, with Her dear friends beside Her.359

1410When the play is over, the Two go to Their homes;
because of the separation [this place] is called Bichhor.

1411Look at Kadamba-khandi and the village of Tiloyar:
here, absorbed in play, [They] know not a moment's rest.360

1412And here is Shringaravata: here Krishna
adorned Radhika in many different ways.361

1413Look: here is a wondrous place of Krishna's pastimes;
now it has become the village named Lalapura.

1414And here is the village of Vasoni: from the fragrance of Krishna's body
will only the bees go mad? — it destroys the composure of the world.362

1415Here Radha and Krishna with Their dear friends
are ever immersed in the games of Holi and other play.

1416O, look at the village of Paya: here Sri Krishna
drank milk together with all His friends.363

1417This is Kotaravana; everyone calls it Kotavana;
here Krishna happily sports with His friends.364

1418In this Dadhigrama Krishna plundered the curd;
with the gopis great merriment arose.

1419Here is Sheshashayi — here is Kshira-samudra;
playfully Krishna lay down on the bed of Ananta.365

1420Sri Radhika serves His lotus feet;
what bliss arose — it cannot be described.

1421Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-first verse:
"He whose beautiful, tender lotus feet, though She Herself is tender,
Sri Radha for Her own happiness raises high to the tips of Her breasts,
quite close, but then, afraid of their hardness, does not place [them there] —
may that Sheshashayi ever establish our dwelling in Sri Goshtha."366

1422To see this Deity of Sheshashayi,
Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra came here.

1423When He saw [Him], great delight arose;
in that absorption in prema the Lord lost His composure.

1424Seeing the Lord's radiance, the fortunate people
went mad with bliss — streams [of tears] flow ceaselessly from their eyes.

1425They said to one another: "This is not a human being at all;
He wears the dress of a sannyasi, but truly this is the Lord."

1426Someone said: "O brother, it cannot be otherwise:
this sannyasi is the Lord Sheshashayi."

1427So many spoke, and no one could keep calm;
again and again they gaze at the Lord's moon-like face.

1428O Srinivasa, the Lord's deeds are boundless;
one can know them only if the Lord [Himself] makes them known.

1429Here, look at the charming kadamba grove;
here the crown of rasikas sports in merriment.

1430This is the border of Vraja — Khamba, Hare, the village of Khami;367
here Krishna and Balarama merrily herd the cows.

1431In the villages of Banachari and others — wondrous pastimes;
all these are the border of Vraja, O Srinivasa.368

1432The village near the Yamuna — here is Khararo;
here Balarama asks His friends about their welfare.369

1433Look at the place Ujani: here the Yamuna
flows upstream at the song of Sri Krishna's flute.370

1434Look at Khelanavana: here the two brothers
play with Their friends — and have no thought of eating.

1435[Only] by their mother's efforts do Krishna and Balarama eat;
the name of this Khelana-vata is Sri Khela-tirtha.371

1436O Srinivasa, this is Rama-ghat;
here the son of Rohini performs the rasa-lila.372

1437Where Krishna with His beloveds enjoyed the rasa sport —
far from there is this rasa place of Rama.

1438What is there to say — He is deep as millions of oceans,
Krishna's second body, supremely steadfast.

1439Full of longing, He came from Dvaraka to Vraja
and stayed [here] two months — Chaitra and Vaishakha.373

1440He consoled everyone — Sri Nanda, Yashoda and the others —
and gladdened His friends in various ways.

1441The son of Rohini, skilled in many kinds of entreaty,
calmed Krishna's beloveds in various ways.

1442He pleased the hearts of His own beloved gopis,
with whom He had sported before in the spring.

1443Who can describe that boundless merriment?
At that time Krishna slew Shankhachuda.

1444With Baladeva's beloveds together with Krishna's beloveds
the play of Holi went on, and the merriment grew as was fitting.

1445How Rama and Krishna, both, with Their own beloveds
enjoy Their pastimes — of that the knowing ones tell.

1446Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, [composed by] Sri Murari Gupta, in the fourth prakrama: "And then look: here Sri Rama and Krishna in spring attire, the two knowers of rasa, adorned with gold, played with the beauties of Vraja — each with His own group leaders.374

1447Dancing and singing with the gopis, filled with rasa,
They shone [amid] the lovely women who sang and danced."

1448Supremely wondrous are Baladeva's pastimes;
Baladeva's beloveds are beyond count.

1449The girls not yet born at the time of Krishna's pastimes —
all of them are counted among Baladeva's beloveds.

1450How Balai, who increases the love of all these gopis,
was absorbed in play — there is no end to telling it.

1451Boundless is the good fortune of the months Chaitra and Vaishakha,
in which the son of Rohini sports in Vraja.

1452Thus [it is said] in the Tenth [Canto], in the sixty-fifth chapter, the eleventh verse:
"For two months — Madhu and Madhava — Lord Rama
stayed there, bringing delight to the gopis at night."375

1453O Srinivasa, "Baladeva with His beloveds
will perform the rasa play" — with this joy in His heart

1454(who can understand the deeds of Balarama?)
in great merriment He came here.

1455Here is the lovely grove on the sandy bank of the Yamuna;
here a fragrant breeze always blows gently, gently.

1456The night is bright with the rays of the full moon;
masses of blossoming flowers — a wondrous beauty.

1457Bees with their mates hum charmingly;
various birds ceaselessly make various sounds.

1458Hundreds of thousands of peacocks and peahens dance;
deer and does playfully roam in all four directions.

1459Staying beneath a tree, the son of Rohini watches [this];
what an unprecedented pose [He has], enchanting the worlds!

1460Seeing Sri Rama's beauty, with joy in their hearts,
the gods in heaven cry out: "Glory, glory!"

1461Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Velavali):
Glory to the son of Rohini, the mighty Bala!
His luster steals the pride of the conch, the kunda jasmine, camphor and the Silver Mountain; lovely is [His] body. (Refrain.)376

1462Lovely hair, curling locks swaying, tilaka glittering — the thief of young women's hearts; lotus eyes wide, bee-like brows trembling, earrings brightening the ears.

1463The nose — [like] the beak of the king of birds, the face surpassing the moon ceaselessly rains nectar; the arms rounded and gracefully curved, bracelets on the wrists, on the broad chest a jewel necklace shines.377

1464The waist, crushing the weight of the lion's pride, is clad in blue garments — incomparable; the shapely knees delight people; to the cluster of nails on [His] feet Ghanashyama offers himself in sacrifice.378

1465O Srinivasa, on seeing Baladeva,
who in the three worlds could keep his composure?

1466Here Rama shines on a throne of jewels;
extraordinary is the beauty of His attire for the rasa festival.

1467Baladeva's beauty surpasses millions of Kandarpas;
the graceful curves of every limb enchant the best of sages.

1468The radiance of His body illuminates the three worlds;
it steals the pride of the rays of millions of moons.

1469On His head a charming mass of curly, glossy hair,
a crown of jewels encircled by a flower garland.

1470The forehead shines, the brows are a row of bees;
the eyes, reaching to the ears, have the splendor of red lotuses.

1471The nose, surpassing the beak of the king of birds, is beautiful;
incomparable and charming is [His] beautiful face.

1472The luster of the lips surpasses the ripe bimba fruit;
the beauty of the lovely teeth destroys the pride of pearls.

1473The pair of cheeks surpasses a silver mirror;
in the ear a single earring glitters.379

1474How sweet the chin — no comparison can be found;
with the bend of His neck He steals the lion's pride.

1475The neck with three folds, the shapely sides;
young women cannot hold back their hearts, seeing the broad chest.380

1476What is an elephant's trunk before [His] beautiful arms!
Who, with great longing, does not beg for the rasa of their touch?

1477He is adorned with armlets, bracelets and various ornaments;
in His left hand is a horn studded with various jewels.

1478The vaijayanti garland on His neck sways ceaselessly;
bees roam over it and hum.

1479The belly is charming, [charming] the navel, the waist very slender;
the bluish garment He wears clings to His body.

1480The thighs — [like] inverted plantain trunks, the abode of rasa;
the soles of the feet defeat the pride of the dawn.

1481The sweet charm of the feet increases everyone's joy;
on them the restless ankle-bells ceaselessly ring.

1482With the radiance of His nails He dispels darkness;
what comparison to give — there is none in the universe.

1483Such a dhyana (meditation) on Baladeva is proclaimed in the Puranas;
fortunate people see [Him] ceaselessly.

1484The Lord who enchants the worlds, the son of Rohini,
whose horn-playing steals the minds of Brahma and the others.

1485Here Baladeva, standing in a threefold bend,
with a joyful heart plays the enchanting horn.

1486Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Malakosha):
Today is the sweet spring night, the full moon shines.
Gazing at the forest and the bank of the Yamuna, His heart maddened again and again, Baladeva sounds the horn — the sound enchants the world. (Refrain.)381

1487The sound draws the beloveds; touching [their] ears, leaving their homes,
[they] come — their hearts brimming with joy, their beauty delighting the mind.
The belts of little bells ring "rini-jhinin-jhanan", the sound of the ankle-bells steals composure;
the lovely tread of their lotus feet puts to shame the gait of the khanjana bird.

1488Many beloveds on all sides — women in spotless attire,
flashing brighter than lightning, display their merriment.
The Lord, absorbed in supreme play, speaks so many [words] softly, softly, softly;
[His] clever, charming words destroy the pride of nectar.382

1489The host of lotus-faced women, with restless eyes like pairs of bees,
drinks the honey of [His] sweetness in rapture and flocks [to Him] with a dense humming.
Abundant thrills rise on the body, incomparable, ever-charming love;
how could Narahari understand this? — [all] are maddened by the supreme rasa of touch.383

1490Here are Sri Balai's most wondrous pastimes —
what can I say with one mouth, O Srinivasa!

1491[Here] a breeze with the fragrance of night lotuses blows ceaselessly,
and how bright, how charming is the moonlight!

1492Balarama, absorbed in play in the grove by the Yamuna,
incomparable, is surrounded by hundreds of thousands of beloveds.

1493Thus [it is said] in the Tenth [Canto], in the sixty-fifth chapter, the twelfth verse: "In the grove by the Yamuna, bathed in the rays of the full moon and fanned by a breeze with the fragrance of night lotuses, He enjoyed, surrounded by hosts of women."384

1494With His beloveds He drank varuni — great merriment;
this story of Varuni is known everywhere.

1495Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the thirteenth verse:
"Sent by Varuna, the goddess Varuni, flowing from the hollow of a tree,
filled that whole forest with fragrance.

1496Bala, smelling the fragrance of that stream of honey carried by the wind,
came there and drank together with the women."385

1497The goddess presiding over intoxicating drink, born together with the nectar,
told Rama: "I am the daughter of Varuna."386

1498Thus [it is said] in the Harivamsha:
"My father Varuna has sent [me] to You, O sinless one."

1499Here the son of Rohini with His beloveds
was ceaselessly enraptured at the beginning of the rasa.

1500On mridanga, pinaka, vina and other instruments
many play in various styles.387

1501The skilled beloveds perform the alapa of various ragas,
displaying shrutis, svaras, murchhanas, gramas and the rest.

1502The gopis sing of the deeds of the Lord of their life;
Brahma and the others, hearing that song, are enchanted.

1503In the Sri rasa-mandala there is no limit to that happiness;
with song, music and dance Balai is in great rapture.

1504Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Shankarabharana):
Baladeva dances, every limb [of His body] thrilling with abundant ecstasy.
Da drimi drimi drimi kata, dha drinda drindadha vidhuddhata,
taka takadhikitaka thori, kuku — softly sounds the mridanga. (Refrain.)388

1505He sways His head very sweetly; His chest is mighty, exceedingly broad;
the lovely, incomparable forest garland swings, [and with it] the bees.
His cheeks outshine silver mirrors, the fine earrings in His ears sway;
His sidelong glance is a khanjana bird, His brows [are curved]; merriment with the lovely women.

1506The gestures of His hands are gracefully made; on His head is a crown of jewels and peacock [feathers];
His curling locks glitter so — [He] shatters the pride of Manmatha.
His soles are lovely land-lotuses; stepping here and there, [He] keeps various talas,
calling out: "Taka thai thai thai, titaka dhilanga."

1507Jhunu jhunu jhunu jhunu — the sound of the ankle bells; hearing it, no one keeps composure;
the bells of the girdle jingle, rani rani they sound, and rapture arises in the heart.
The moon-faced beloveds [He] kisses, smiling ever so gently —
so sings Ghanashyama this heart-delighting wave of rasa.389

1508Again, raga Kedara:
It sounds: "Jhig jhig jhig jhendrang, drinda drinda drimi dig-drang";
the triputa tala is manifest, soft strokes, a swift tempo.
Taka thai thai tathai ta, thodi thunna thong kana
kana jhini na na na — [so it sounds]; the mind of Ratipati is enraptured.390

1509The beautiful, composed hero Bala dances on the bank of the Daughter of the Sun;
the beloveds, in the joyous ardor of the rasa, sport all around [Him].
The restless steps go jhinini; the jeweled bells of the girdle jingle;
jhunu jhunu jhunu — the sound of the ankle bells steals the minds of the sages.

1510The jeweled earrings flash on His cheeks, the lovely forest garland sways;
drawn by the wealth of fragrance, the bees hum in swarms.391
With a touch full of rasa [He] smiles gently; the splendid moon of His face shines;
the nectar-rasa [of it] the eyes of Ghanashyama drink — chakora birds.

1511All the beloveds, with great bliss in their hearts,
surrounding Baladeva, dance wondrously.

1512Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kedara):
Today it is the full moon, the moon is full, the spring night is pure.
Dha dha dhigi tagadhilanga, drimi drimi drimi — the mridanga sounds;
Baladeva dances, and, surrounding [Him], all the lovely women sport. (Refrain.)

1513The bells of the girdle, the soft sound of the ankle bells, the incomparable movement, the sweet singing,
the many gestures of the hands, the restless eyes, the curving poses — charming [women].
He sways His head ever so gently, He smiles — His rows of teeth shine.
What will Ghanashyama say? The fair-bodied [women] flash like lightning.

1514Again, raga Bhupali:
How sweet is the spring night today!
The moon has lit up all the directions.

1515On the expanse of the Yamuna's bank
Balai sports with His beloveds.

1516What beauty the rasa-mandala has!
On all four sides are the charming gopis.

1517Eagerly they play various instruments,
they sing songs in waves of rasa.

1518Surrounding the Lord of their life they dance;
with their beauty they steal the mind of the world.

1519Balarama, the crown of rasikas,
dances, surpassing millions of Kamas.

1520Again and again He blows the lovely horn;
with that very sound He intoxicates the world.

1521How many clever tricks He displays!
On His beloved's arm He places His arm.

1522Bringing the moon of His face to [her] face,
in delight He cannot restrain His heart.

1523He fulfils the desires of all;
this Narahari Dasa offers himself [for Him].392

1524O Srinivasa! The rasa-lila of Sri Rama
the Lord's devotees have described in many ways.

1525Playfully drawing the Yamuna and bringing her here,
Baladeva held water sports with His beloveds.393

1526Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Bhupali):
The hero Bala, who delights in the Sri rasa,
is in rapture at every moment and cannot be steady.

1527Who can understand this lila of Balai?
Without effort He drew the Yamuna with His plough.

1528Settling with the host of lovely women,
He sports in the waters of the Yamuna in many ways.394

1529Having fought in the water, He comes up onto the bank;
then with the beauty of His garments and ornaments He steals [all] hearts.

1530Balarama is the embodiment of rasa;
He drinks madhu and the rest, intoxicated with the intoxication of Madana.

1531With His beloveds in the bower-house
He lies down on a bed of flowers; how much rises in His heart!

1532Seeing that the night has ended, the beloveds
cannot leave the Lord of their life and go home.

1533Balai, caressing [them] so much,
bids [them] farewell, and His heart breaks.

1534All went each to her own home.
Narahari offers himself for this pastime of Balai.

1535Here [there were] various sports with the beloveds;
at the end of the night all returned home.

1536Here the Yamuna, seized with great fear,
fell at Baladeva's lotus feet and bowed down.

1537Considering herself lowly, with an anguished heart,
joining both palms, she offered many prayers.

1538Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Deshapala):
O Rama, son of Rohini, lotus-eyed,
ornament of the Yadu dynasty, Baladeva, friend of the surrendered!
Affectionate to Your devotees, Halayudha, abode of joy,
home of virtues, remover of fear, sole ocean of mercy!395

1539O You who are honoured by the world, moon-faced, beautiful,
unsurpassed in playing the horn — dhiki dhikata dheya!
Sa ri ga, sa ri ga ma, pa ma ga ri ma pa dha ni ti —
ah, show mercy to me, O Lord of Nrihari — tenna!396

1540With jubilation in her heart the Yamuna bows down [to Him] again.
What to say — she is skilled in caring for the welfare of others.

1541Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Shri):
Glory, glory to the beloved of Revati, the abode of rasa,
who delights the people of all the worlds — re!
His eyes are petals of a spotless lotus; He frees from the burden of composure,
He puts to shame the gait of the elephant — re!397

1542Moon-faced, master of new tandava dances,
Haladhara, ornament of the Yadu dynasty — re!
Like a conch and the kunda flower, clad in blue,
He shatters the pride of Makaradhvaja — re!

1543Protector of those who take refuge, [Lord of] Narahari,
jha jha jha jha, trigadatiya!
Ei ai ai ai, ai ati ainava,
tenna tenna ti ati ai iya!398

1544What shall I say, O Srinivasa, of that very story:
here Balai became gracious to the Yamuna.

1545Various amusements [took place] in this rasa pastime;
this Rasa-sthali of Rama is famous in the world.

1546What shall I say — beautiful is the region of Rama-ghat;
the communities of devotees constantly worship it.

1547Thus [it is said] in the Sri Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-fourth verse:
"That Krishna who, composed, was flowing to the salt ocean, devoid of connection with Krishna,
was drawn by the tip of the plough of the angry Plough-bearer;
even today all people see her so in this place.
Oh! With devotion I worship this wondrous region of Rama-ghatta."399

1548Whoever has the wish to hear about Rama-ghat,
from him these worldly fetters fall away without effort.

1549Rama, who delights in the Sri rasa — Nityananda-raya —
stayed here during His pilgrimage to the tirthas.400

1550With the cowherd boys He was always absorbed in play;
when hungry, He ate yogurt, milk, roots and fruits.

1551In the mood of Baladeva He could not remain steady;
He hides Himself — [but] cannot stay hidden.

1552All say: "This is that very son of Rohini
who wanders through Vraja in the guise of an avadhuta."

1553O Srinivasa, seeing Nitai's ways,
all — whether children, old men or youths — were enchanted.

1554Here are Nitaichand's wondrous pastimes.
This shakata tree here is His tooth-stick.401

1555Here at Rama-ghat a fortunate brahmana
could not sustain his life without Baladeva.

1556Nityananda-Rama, to protect His devotee,
appeared to the brahmana in the form of Baladeva.

1557Seeing here Nityananda-Balarama, who delights in the Sri rasa,
the Kalindi offered [Him] prayers.

1558Here, seeing Nityananda's play, the gods
were overwhelmed — their tears could not be checked.

1559Beneath this tree, on a raised platform of dust,
Nityananda-Haladhara lay in rapture.

1560Lying there, Prabhu says again and again:
"In how many days will the deliverance of the faithless come?

1561In how many days will the Lord of Navadvipa in Navadvipa
manifest Himself? [When] shall I go and see [Him] with my own eyes?"402

1562So much He speaks thus — no one can understand;
Nitai's wondrous lila is known throughout the world.

1563Look: near Rama-ghat is Kachchhavana;
here the boys played [imitating] turtles.403

1564Look at Bhushanavana — this is a very secluded [place];
[here] the friends adorned Krishna with flower ornaments.404

1565And here as well — look at the place of Krishna's pastimes;
whose heart is not soothed on seeing all this?

1566Having said this, Pandita walks slowly, slowly;
seeing the beauty of the forest, he cannot keep his composure.

1567With jubilation in his heart he goes along the path to Bhandira;
now people call this [place] Akshayavata.

1568Approaching Bhandira, with very sweet words,
with great affection Pandita says to Srinivasa:

1569Look at the incomparable place of Bhandiravata;
here Krishna and Balarama sport delightfully.405

1570When [They] were playing games with Their friends in the guise of wrestlers,
the asura Pralamba came and mingled among them.

1571Balarama playfully slew Pralamba.
At Bhandira are Krishna's various pastimes with His friends.

1572One day Krishna, alone at the foot of Bhandira,
played the flute — by which the world is intoxicated.

1573Hearing the sound of the flute, Radha lost Her patience;
coming quickly with Her sakhis, She met Krishna.

1574Supreme bliss arose in the hearts of the Two;
with Their friends They sport in many playful ways.

1575Sri Radhika says to Krishna in gentle words,
"What games do You play with Your friends in this region?"

1576Sri Krishna says, "Here, dressing as wrestlers,
I happily wrestle with My friends.

1577No one knows wrestling as I do;
without effort I defeat other wrestlers."

1578Laughing, Lalita says to Krishna again and again,
"Today we shall see You fight in a wrestler's dress."

1579Having said this, they all dressed as wrestlers;
Krishna, in a wrestler's dress, boasts without end.

1580Looking at Krishna, Rai smiles softly, softly;
for the wrestling She enters the place of the contest.

1581In the great wrestling there was neither victory nor defeat;
Kandarpa's joy became boundless.

1582Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-third verse:
"Where my Mistress, full of rasa, the most beloved Radha, filled with pride,
having made wrestlers of Her own friends and eagerly becoming a wrestler Herself,
joyfully wrestled with the Slayer of Baka, who had fully taken on the role of a wrestler,
and gave delight to Madana — that Bhandiraka I worship."406

1583Thus at Bhandira [They] were absorbed in all kinds of amusements;
who can describe the pastimes that took place at Bhandira?

1584Near Bhandira, look at this village of Ara;
this is Munjatavi, also named Ishikatavi.407

1585Here Krishnachandra, having drunk the forest fire,
saved the cows, the cowherds and all the rest — there was great bliss.

1586This here is the village of Bhandari on the bank of the Yamuna;
that is Munjatavi, as all people proclaim.408

1587O Srinivasa, look at this Tapovana:
here the daughters of the cowherds performed austerities.409

1588Look at Gopi-ghat: here the gopis came;
bathing in the Yamuna, they were filled with great delight.

1589This is Chir-ghat: here the daughters of the cowherds
worshipped Katyayani, and the hearts of all rejoiced.410

1590Leaving their garments on the bank of the Yamuna,
all entered the water to bathe.

1591Unnoticed, stealing everyone's clothes,
Hari watches the fun from up in a nipa tree.

1592The daughters of the cowherds, greatly ashamed,
remaining in the water, beg Krishna for their clothes.

1593Krishna, revealing what was in His own heart,
joyfully gave everyone their clothes.

1594The daughters of the cowherds joyfully put on their clothes,
having surrendered their very selves to Krishna.

1595Look at this Nanda-ghat: here Nanda and the others
bathed in the Yamuna — there is much to tell about this.

1596Having fasted on ekadashi, on dvadashi
he enters the waters of the Kalindi to bathe.

1597A messenger of Varuna seized Nanda and carried him off;
Krishna playfully brought Nanda back from there.411

1598O Srinivasa, here Nanda became afraid;
therefore Vajra founded a village named Bhaya.412

1599Having said this, they set out from the village of Bhaya
to see all the places that [lie] along the parikrama.

1600He says to Srinivasa: look at this Vatsavana;
here the Four-faced One stole the calves.413

1601Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-sixth verse:
"When the Creator, eager to see with his own eyes the boundless greatness of his Lord,
swiftly stole the herd of calves and the crowd of boys who tended the calves,
Hari, becoming each of them, there gave joy to their mothers
and even ate [their] food — that place of the stealing of the calves I worship."

1602This here is the village of Unai: here with His friends
Krishna eats all sorts of foods in many playful ways.

1603This is the village named Balihara: here
the Four-faced One, with a glad heart, steals the boys and the rest.414

1604Look here at the place named Parikham:
the Four-faced One stayed [here] to test Krishna.415

1605All people know this place by the name of Sei;
here Brahma was bewildered by Krishna's maya.416

1606Having stolen the boys and calves and hidden [them] in secret, Brahma
sees those same boys and calves beside Krishna.

1607"Those are these, these are those," he says again and again;
for this reason [this place] received the name Sei.

1608In this village of Chomuha Brahma, coming to Krishna,
offered praise to Krishna in countless ways.417

1609Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-seventh verse:
"Where Brahma, in great fear because of the offence committed by stealing the calves and the calf-herds,
fell to the ground in tears and with unprecedented verses praised
Mukunda, the son of the lord of Vraja, the wondrous herder of calves, faintly smiling —
that place named Bhiru-chaturmukha, together with [its] Lord, we ceaselessly praise."418

1610[Here] Krishna killed Aghasura — this is Sarpa-sthali;
[its] name is Aghavana, and people call [it] Sapoli.419

1611Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninety-fifth verse:
"Where the Conqueror of Mura, seeing that His friends, dear to Him as life, had entered before Him
the belly of the most sinful Aghasura, foul with poisons burning like the fire at the edge of the aranis,
and were in distress, in anger at once entered [it], and, mighty, killed that villain
and saved His own [friends] — may that Sarpa-sthali protect [us]."420

1612Here the gods shower flowers and cry out, "Victory!" —
for this reason this [place] is called the village of Jayet.421

1613All say, "In killing Aghasura He [showed Himself] clever (siyān)";
therefore this is the village of Seyano, [also] called Sehona.422

1614Look at these two villages, Taroli and Baroli;
all say [that they are] villages founded by the cowherds in ancient times.423

1615O Srinivasa, look also at a delightful place:
here the son of Nanda, Bhagavan, sports.

1616Having said this, he climbed the hill by Krishna-kunda
and looks in all four directions, filled with joy.424

1617He says to Srinivasa: look, this is the village of Maghera;
formerly it was known by the name Maghahera.425

1618O, look here at the tamala grove:
at the meeting of Radha and Krishna great merriment grows [here].

1619Having said this, he joyfully came down from the hill
and speaks to Srinivasa with the greatest affection:

1620In this village of Atas a great wonder took place:
the sage Ashtavakra performed austerities here.426

1621This is Shakra-sthana, now [people] call [it] Shakaroya;
having poured rain upon Vraja, Shakra became afraid here.427

1622In this village of Varahar, in the form of a boar,
Krishna played with His dear friends.428

1623Look at the village of Harasali, O Srinivasa:
this is Rasa-sthali — here Krishna performed the rasa dance.429

1624Thus [it is said] in the same place, in the Vraja-vilasa, the sixty-third verse:
"Where the Conqueror of Mura, dancing with the throng of lovely young cowherd women, radiant with skill,
leaves them and in seclusion, with love, adorns Sri Radhika
with a wealth of flower ornaments and delights [with Her] in an abundance of joys —
may that Rasa-sthali, filled with a sweetness wondrous to the three worlds, protect [us]."430

1625Having said this, he, together with Srinivasa and Narottama,
came again to Nanda-ghat, filled with great joy.

1626He says to Srinivasa: here, in this solitary place,
Sri Jiva lived, entirely unrecognized.

1627I shall tell that story. One day in Vrindavana
Sri Rupa, sitting in solitude, was writing a book.

1628It was the hot season, sweat covered [his] body;
Sri Jiva, standing to one side, was fanning [him].

1629As boundless as the beauty of Rupa Gosvami was,
so [beautiful] was the appearance of Sri Jiva — [it was] the time of [his] youth.

1630Who would not long to see Sri Rupa?
Sri Vallabha Bhatta came and met [him] in private.

1631Seeing the mangalacharana of the book Bhakti-rasamrita,
the Bhatta says, "I will correct this."431

1632Having said this, he went to bathe on the bank of the Yamuna;
Sri Jiva went [there too], on the pretext of fetching water.

1633[He] had no acquaintance with Sri Vallabha Bhatta;
he asks, "What doubt [do you have] about the mangalacharana?"

1634Having listened, whatever Sri Vallabha Bhatta said,
Sri Jiva quickly refuted all of it.

1635In the course of the talk a debate on many shastras arose;
the Bhatta could not refute Sri Jiva's words.

1636Having discussed for some time and brought the discussion to a close,
the Bhatta went again [to Rupa] and says to Sri Rupa,

1637"That young man who was beside you —
I have joyfully come to learn who he is."

1638Sri Rupa says, "What shall I tell [you about him]?
[His] name is Jiva; he is my disciple, my brother's son.

1639It is only a few days since he came from [our] homeland."
Hearing [this], the Bhatta praised [him] in every way.

1640Honoured by Rupa, the Bhatta departed;
at that very moment Sri Jiva came back from the Yamuna.

1641Sri Rupa says to Sri Jiva in gentle words,
"Out of kindness to me the Bhatta came to me.

1642For my own good he said he would correct the book —
and you could not bear even such small words.

1643Therefore go quickly to the eastern country;
when your mind becomes calm, come [back] to Vrindavana."432

1644At the Gosvami's order he set out eastward;
having gone some distance, he carefully calmed his mind.

1645There was no order of the Gosvami to come near [him];
for this reason he came here, to this solitary forest.

1646Living in a hut of leaves, in the greatest grief,
he sometimes eats a little, sometimes fasts.

1647"Quickly separating my life from my body,
I shall attain the lotus feet of [my] master" — such was the thought in his heart.

1648Unexpectedly Sanatana Gosvami came;
the villagers went out to meet [him] and took [him] to the village.

1649Seating the Gosvami in great joy
and asking about his welfare, they then say slowly:

1650"A handsome young ascetic
has been living in this forest for some days now.

1651We try in many ways to feed him;
sometimes he eats fruits and roots, sometimes he goes without food.

1652Only after much effort does he take a little wheat flour
and eat it, mixing it with water."

1653Hearing this, he understood that Jiva was there;
melting with parental affection, he went to that place.

1654Sri Jiva was sitting in his hut of leaves;
at the sight of the Gosvami he could not hold back his heart.

1655Rolling on the ground, he falls at the Gosvami's feet;
seeing Sri Jiva's behaviour, everyone is amazed.

1656Whatever Sanatana, overcome with affection, asked,
Sri Jiva related it all to him briefly and in order.

1657Having heard, Sri Gosvami left Jiva right there
and, reassuring the villagers, went to Vrindavana.

1658Hearing of the Gosvami's arrival, Sri Rupa at once
went to see the Gosvami.

1659The Gosvami asks Sri Rupa for news:
"What still remains [to be done] in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu?"

1660Sri Rupa says, "The writing is nearly finished;
if Jiva were here, the revision would be done quickly."

1661The Gosvami says, "Jiva is barely alive.
I saw his body swaying in the wind."

1662Saying this, he told what had happened to Jiva;
Sri Rupa at once had Sri Jiva brought.

1663Seeing Sri Jiva's condition, Sri Rupa Gosani
nursed him — there was no limit to his mercy.

1664When Sri Jiva recovered, everyone's heart was glad;
Rupa-Sanatana entrusted [him] with all the work.

1665By the grace of Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana
the power of Sri Jiva's learning spread through the world.

1666A digvijayi came to Vrindavana
with many people, expert in all the shastras.

1667He said, "If you are unable to debate,
then quickly send me a certificate of my victory."433

1668Hearing this, Sri Jiva at once sent a letter;
on reading the letter, the digvijayi was defeated.

1669All the digvijayis who come like this, full of pride,
are defeated and flee to their own lands.

1670The power of Sri Jiva cannot be described.
O Srinivasa, this is his hut.

1671Telling many such things, they crossed the Yamuna
and, coming to the village of Surukhuru, stayed [there] that day.434

1672How Sri Krishna showed favour to the gods there —
that he made known to Srinivasa and Narottama.

1673From there he showed them distant villages too;
which pastimes took place where — of that he spoke briefly.

1674Setting out from Surukhuru in the morning,
he says to Srinivasa: look, here is Bhadravana.

1675By going to Bhadravana one becomes dear to Krishna;
by the power of this forest one attains the world of heaven.

1676Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"There is a forest named Bhadravana, the sixth forest, excellent.
Going there, O Vasudha, My devotee, for whom I am the supreme refuge,435
by the power of that forest goes to the world of heaven."

1677Look: utterly secluded is this Bhandiravana;
here Rama and Krishna play various games with Their friends.

1678This Bhandiravana is dear to the yogis;
merely seeing it removes the torment of [dwelling in] the womb.

1679This Bhandira is the best of all forests, the shastras say;
whoever sees Vasudeva here is not born again.436

1680Whoever regularly bathes and so on in Bhandira
is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Indra.

1681Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The eleventh is Bhandira, excellent, dear to the yogis;
by merely seeing it a man does not enter a womb.

1682Having reached Bhandira, the best of forests,
and having then seen Vasudeva, [one] is not born again.

1683Whoever, self-controlled and restrained in eating, bathes in this Bhandira
is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Indra."

1684Having played with His friends in Bhandira, Sri Krishna
eats various foods, sitting in this shade.

1685Therefore this village is called Chhaheri.
Look at this beautiful place near the Yamuna.437

1686This is Mathgrama — here there is great bliss;
here Rama and Krishna engage in various games with Their friends.438

1687A large vessel made of clay is called a math;
[this place] is famed for making maths — therefore [it is] Mathgrama.

1688For churning yogurt and so on, the residents of Vraja
take countless maths [from here] — so everyone says.

1689In this Bilvavana Rama and Krishna with Their friends
eat ripe bilva fruits with great merriment.

1690The beautiful Bilvavana is worshipped by the gods;
whoever goes to this forest is honoured in Brahma-loka.

1691Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The forest named Bilvavana is the tenth, worshipped by the gods;
going there, a man is glorified in Brahma-loka."

1692Whoever bathes in Sri Krishna-kunda in Bilvavana
is freed from all sins; he is supremely fortunate.

1693Look: in very ancient times the course of the Yamuna was here,
and Mana-sarovara was on the far side of the Yamuna.439

1694Now the Yamuna has become two streams,
and in the middle is the most beautiful Mana-sarovara.

1695Look also at the many villages in this region —
all of them are incomparable places of Krishna's pastimes.

1696O Srinivasa, look: here is Lohavana;
in Lohavana Krishna wondrously herded the cows.

1697This charming place is pervaded by the fragrance of various flowers;
here Bhagavan slew the demon Lohajangha.

1698Its name is Lohajanghavana;
it delivers from all sins.

1699Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The forest named Lohajanghavana, guarded by Lohajangha —
the ninth forest, O Devi — destroys all sins."440

1700Look at the many enchanting places in this region:
everywhere the son of Nanda always sports.

1701Saying this, [they] had darshan everywhere
of the Deities of Krishna, Balarama, Nrisimha and others.

1702Going near the Yamuna, he says to Srinivasa:
at this ghat Krishna begins the boat pastime.

1703It is a great frolic: Rai with Her friends,
taking milk and other things, comes to cross over.

1704Seeing that unprecedented beauty, Krishna, enchanted,
stays to one side with a very old boat.

1705Sri Radhika with Her friends says again and again,
"Take [us] across, boatman — we must quickly get to the other side!"

1706Thus [it is said] in the Padyavali, in [the section on] the boat pastime, verse 269:
"Glory to Hari, whom crowds of gopis call again and again, 'Take [us] across the Yamuna!' —
while He, pretending to lie down on the bank by the boat, becomes twice as lazy."

1707At last Krishna, seating [them] in that boat,
moves off a little way with great joy in His heart.

1708What frolic arose I am unable to tell;
the poets have described this sport at length.

1709Thus [it is said] in the Padyavali, in the same place, verses 272 and 274–276:
"The boat is old, the river's waters are very deep,
we are young girls: thus everything [portends] disaster.
But this alone is the seed of rescue for us slender-waisted ones:
that You, O Madhava, are now the helmsman.

1710At Your word alone, O Yadunandana, I at once threw into the water
the load of milk products and even my necklace;
I have also removed the silk cloth from these breasts —
and still the bank of the daughter of Kalinda is not near.

1711Filled with floods of water and spun about by the winds,
this boat is about to sink into the deep waters of the Kalindi.
Alas, my ill fate! And Hari, His heart seized with great amusement,
still claps His hands again and again.

1712My hands never rest from bailing out the water,
and still You go on with Your mocking words.
If I live, then never again,
O Krishna, will I set foot in Your boat."

1713Coming to Mahavana, Sri Pandita, absorbed in prema,
gently says to Srinivasa and Narottama:

1714Look at the home of Nanda and Yashoda in Mahavana;
what sports took place here — who knows how to describe them?

1715Look: here is the birthplace of Sri Krishnachandra;
seeing the face of the son here, Nanda and the others were overwhelmed.441

1716The cowherd men and women of Vraja come running into this courtyard;
here the festival of the son's birth took place.

1717For the son's welfare Nanda gave many gifts;
supreme, wondrous happiness pervaded the world.

1718Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the eighty-ninth verse:
"Where, at the great festival of the appearance of the Enemy of Mura, the lord of Vraja joyfully
gave the brahmanas twice nine lakhs of cows adorned with the splendour
of strings of large pearls set in gold, and also, with respect, divine ornaments,
mountains of jewels, prasthas of sesame and more — to that Brihat-kanana I bow."442

1719In the Gitavali of the Stavamala, the first [song] on Nanda's festival (raga Bhairava):
Yashoda gave birth to a wondrous son —
the throng of cowherds became exceedingly joyful. (Refrain.)

1720Someone brings various gifts,
someone dances again and again.

1721Someone sweetly sings a song,
someone scatters fresh butter with yogurt.

1722Someone fulfils [others'] desires,
someone beholds the eternal form.443

1723Again in the same [work] (raga Ashavari):
The host of brahmanas is amply endowed with ornaments and cows;
now quickly satisfy singers like me as well, O lord of Vraja!

1724O King Nanda, this wondrously beautiful son has been born to you!
Give the people of the goshtha what they desire — gifts befitting the festival. (Refrain.)

1725The heart of people like me, rejoicing in the festival of beholding your son,
desires that wealth which none of the petitioners has received.

1726In the blue swan sporting in the Manasa lake of Sri Sanatana's heart —
in this child of yours may the love of people like us always abide.444

1727O Srinivasa, here is the limit of happiness:
here all the customary rites for Krishna's birth were performed.

1728Look, here is the place of Nanda's cowshed;
here Nanda told Gargacharya what was in his heart.

1729Out of fear of Kamsa, Garga secretly,
right here, with a joyful heart, performed the name-giving ceremony of Rama and Krishna.445

1730Here the prince of Vraja slew Putana;
right here the cremation of Putana['s body] took place.

1731O Srinivasa, Krishna, while lying on His bed,
broke the cart right here.

1732Lying on His back, Krishna is exceedingly beautiful;
seeing the wondrous pastime of [His] infancy, one is amazed.

1733Thus [it is said] in the Sri Padyavali, [in the description of] Sri Krishna's infancy, the hundred and thirtieth verse:
"Whose hands and feet are deep red, whose tilaka of lovely gorochana shines,
who forcibly overturned the cart — the enemy of Mura, lying on His back, I worship."446

1734Here Krishnachandra, climbing into His mother's lap,
drinks her breast milk in a most wondrous manner.

1735Yashoda, gazing at Krishna's face,
overwhelmed with joy, nurses Him at her breast.

1736Thus [it is said] in the Padyavali, in the same place, the hundred and thirty-first verse: "When with half-opened eyes He drinks His fill at one breast, and with His hand strokes the other, wet with milk that has just flowed, and His mother caresses Him with her fingers, and His face again and again breaks into a smile — may the luster of Vishnu's teeth, white with the bright gleam of drops of milk, protect you."

1737Here Yashoda in great happiness coaxes Krishna to her;
He crawls on all fours — what a sweet smile on His face!

1738Thus [it is said] in the Sri Padyavali, in the same place, the hundred and thirty-second verse:
"Him whose eyes dart about at the sounds the mistress of the cowherd settlement makes with her lips,
who crawls over the ground on His two knees,
whose lips shine sweet with the nectar of a slight, fresh smile —
that child, dark as a tamala leaf, I worship."

1739Here, whatever the gopis ask Krishna about,
Krishna shows by pointing with His finger.

1740Thus [it is said] in the same place, the hundred and thirty-third verse:
"'Where is the face? Where are the eyes? Where is the nose?
Where is the ear, and where the topknot?' — asked in this way,
the Lord, placing the petal of His finger here and there,
delighted the crowd of cowherd women."

1741Here Krishna, grey with dust, laughs;
seeing [this], the mother says so much to her son in a soft voice.

1742Thus [it is said] in the same place, the hundred and thirty-fourth verse:
"Only just now [Your] body was washed and anointed with ointment —
and already, Krishna, Your body is grey with dust."

1743Supremely beautiful Krishna, sitting right here,
looks at His mother, wanting to drink milk.

1744Here the wicked Trinavarta, seizing Krishna,
rose up into the sky, greatly elated.

1745In great playfulness Krishna, looking about in all four directions,
slays here Trinavarta from Kamsa's abode.447

1746Here Krishna happily ate earth;
the queen of Vraja saw the universe in Krishna's mouth.

1747For this reason this place is called Brahmanda-ghat.448
Look at the wonderful beauty of the bank of the Yamuna.

1748Yashoda, joyfully sitting together with the gopis,
watches the charming beauty of her son in this courtyard.

1749Thus [it is said] in the same place, the hundred and thirty-fifth verse:
"Five years old, very playful, running about the courtyard,
His eyes covered by His locks,
adorned with little bells, bracelets, a necklace and anklets —
bow down to the son of Nanda."

1750How Krishna in infancy displays youth —
poets joyfully describe this wondrous matter.

1751Thus [it is said] in the same place, [on] youth even in infancy, the hundred and thirty-sixth verse:
"Having placed lips to lips, neck to neck, tenderly eyes to eyes,
forehead to forehead, a gopi in agitation
laid the crying Krishna on her bosom, [thinking,] 'He is a child'; and He, for a long time
hiding His thrill, smiling, His body languid with love — may He protect [you]."

1752In the same place, the hundred and thirty-eighth to the hundred and fortieth verses:
"When the Wearer of the forest garland performs childlike antics on His father's lap,
a row of smiles of the ever-new young wives of the cowherds blossoms forth."

1753"'How much fresh butter did You take?' — so Yashoda asked Krishna; 'This much,' [He showed] before the elders, taking hold of Dhanishtha's breast. May He protect [you]."449

1754"'Where are you going, thief? Your delight is plain to see.
You are carrying here in your bodice a second ball of mine —
drop it!' — [so saying,] forcibly pressing the breasts of a young gopi,
Keshava, all aglow with thrills, is victorious in Gokula."

1755Here Krishna ponders in His mind [His] fear of His mother;
in stealing fresh butter He is exceedingly skilled.

1756In the same place, the hundred and forty-first verse: "[The childhood] in which the pot of fresh butter is spotted from afar, in which one hurries crawling on the knees, in which the face is turned away for fear of the mother — that indescribable childhood of Keshava I worship."

1757Here Krishna in a dream addresses the gods;
hearing those words, the mother is anxious at heart.

1758In the same place, the hundred and forty-seventh verse:
"'Shambhu, welcome! Sit here, here. Lotus-born, on the left.
Enemy of Krauncha, is all well? Lord of the gods, are you happy? Lord of wealth, you are not to be seen' —
hearing such words of the sleeping enemy of Kaitabha, His mother [said],
'What, what improper things are You babbling, child?' — may her 'thoo-thoo' protect you."450

1759Here Nanda and Yashoda, to put Krishna to sleep,
tell [Him] in various ways the story of Sri Rama and others.

1760In the same place, the hundred and fifty-first and hundred and fifty-second verses: "'There was [a king] named Rama.' — 'Mm.' — 'His wife was Sita.' — 'Mm.' — 'While he, at his father's word, was living in the Panchavati forest, Ravana carried her off' — hearing from His mother this ancient story about Himself, Krishna [cried out], 'Saumitri, where is the bow, the bow, the bow?!' — may those agitated words protect you."451

1761"'It is night, the moon is high — You are not asleep, child?' — 'Mother, sleep does not come to me.' —
'To fall asleep, listen, son, to an extraordinary story.' — 'Tell it.' —
'From a pillar Narahari appeared, to tear apart a Danava' —
when this was said, a smile arose on the son of Devaki."452

1762Here Yashoda tied Krishna to the mortar;
Krishna playfully accepted being bound.

1763This is the holy place, Yamalarjuna-bhanjana-tirtha;453
wondrous is the beauty of the kunda, and [its] water is perfectly clear.

1764Bathing and fasting [here] bring endless fruit;
by coming to Mahavana [one] becomes honoured in the world of Indra.

1765Look at Gopishvara, the destroyer of great sins;454
Mahavana, dear to Krishna, is full of Krishna's pastimes.

1766Look, here is the Sapta-samudrika well;455
the fruits of offering pinda and so on [here] are declared in that Purana.

1767Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The eighth [forest] is Mahavana; it is always dear to Me.
Going there, a man becomes honoured in the world of Indra.456

1768There too is Yamalarjuna-tirtha and a kunda,
where the cart was overturned and its pots and jars broken.

1769By bathing and fasting there one obtains endless fruit.
There too [abides] Gopishvara, the destroyer of great sins."

1770O Srinivasa, Krishna Chaitanya here,
seeing how [the songs of] the birth festival were sung, rejoiced at heart.457

1771In a rapture of feeling the Lord became absorbed in dancing and singing;
by His mercy He drew all hearts.

1772Seeing the Lord, people come running from all four directions;
losing their composure, they cry out, "Hari! Hari!"

1773From everyone's eyes tears flow ceaselessly;
all say, "This is no sannyasi — this is certainly Krishna."

1774Maddened by prema for the Lord, all the people
say so much and fall rolling on the ground.

1775Who has the power to understand the ways of Sri Gaurachandra?
In Mahavana a great ocean of bliss arose.

1776Seeing Madana-gopala, [the Lord] lost His composure;458
who could describe this unearthly pastime of the Lord?

1777O Srinivasa, look at this place:
right here lived Sanatana Gosvami.

1778All the fortunate residents of Mahavana,
just by seeing Sanatana, would come to life.

1779Sanatana, receiving great happiness
from the darshan of Madana-gopala, lived in Mahavana.

1780This is Ramanaka-valu, on the bank of the Yamuna;459
here Madana-gopala plays merrily.

1781One day, with the children of the residents of Mahavana,
He came to this divine sandbank in the form of a cowherd boy.

1782They play many games; seeing this, Sanatana
thinks, "This is no ordinary child."

1783When, having finished playing, the boy went off [home],
Sanatana followed behind Him.

1784The boy enters the temple, and there too goes Sanatana;
not seeing the boy, he sees Madanamohana.

1785Bowing down to Madana-gopala, Sanatana
returned to his lodging without saying anything.

1786Madana-gopala is subject to the Gosvami's prema;
His pastimes, full of rasa, spread throughout the world.

1787Look at this well — everyone calls it Gopa-kupa.460
Sri Gokula and Mahavana — the two are one.

1788This Sri Gokula-Mahavana is exceedingly beautiful;
one after another [here] are the dwellings of Upananda and the other cowherds.

1789In Gokula are Krishna's surpassing childhood pastimes,
by which the hearts of the cowherd men and gopis rejoice.

1790O Srinivasa, this tree is ancient;
look at the beauty of this tree: it cannot be described.

1791The residents of Gokula find refreshment here;
Gauranga, coming to Gokula, sat right here.

1792How the Lord came here —
who could describe it in detail?

1793From Prayaga, gradually reaching Agravana,
He soon arrived at the ashrama of Jamadagni.461

1794His wife was Renuka; the village is named Renuka —
[the place] where Sri Parashurama took birth.462

1795From Renuka, quickly, by way of Rajagrama,
coming to Gokula, He stayed under this tree.463

1796Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the fourth prakrama, in the second sarga:464
"Then, coming to Prayaga and seeing the Lord Sri Madhava,
filled with the nectar of the bliss of prema, He danced together with His companions.

1797Seeing the glorious Akshaya-vata and bathing at the Triveni,
plunging into the Yamuna with the playfulness of an intoxicated elephant,465

1798with deep, thunderous roars of hunkara, covered with tears of prema and thrills,
proceeding [onward], He gradually crossed it and saw Agravana.

1799There too is the village named Renuka, where the lord of warriors
and the great-souled Jamadagni descended upon this holy land.466

1800There, seeing the Yamuna, which ever flows toward Vrindavana,
and then going to Rajagrama and beholding Gokula, He was beside Himself."

1801Here, in great rapture in nama-sankirtana,
[the Lord] went with many people to the birthplace of Krishna.

1802O Srinivasa, here, at the height of happiness,
all the rites customary at Krishna's birth were performed.

1803Here all the elderly gopis with great joy
merrily sing auspicious songs about Krishna.

1804Here sit Nanda and the other cowherds,
skilled in all kinds of counsel among themselves.

1805Here, seeing various calamities from time to time,
all resolved: "Let us go and live in Vrindavana."

1806The cowherds from Gokula, Raval and other [villages] —
look, by this path they all went to Vrindavana.

1807On the way, in great merriment, beside Bhandiravana
they crossed the Yamuna in supreme joy.

1808The calves and the rest were all gathered in one place;
therefore there [it] is called the village of Sakarauri.467

1809O Srinivasa, look at this village of Raval:
here is the incomparable dwelling of Vrishabhanu.

1810Here Sri Radhika appeared,
and with her appearance happiness spread through the worlds.

1811Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the ninetieth verse:
"Where in the mine of Kirtida's womb, praised by gods, sages and men eager for bliss,
there appeared the jewel — the birth of Gandharva — here, in the chief city of Vrishabhanu,
called Raval, surrounded by gopis, gopas and herds of cows,
may my flood of love abide."468

1812Thus [it is said] in a song:
What bliss today in the house of Vrishabhanu!
From the womb of Krittika Radhika-devi is born.469

1813With the radiance of her beauty she lights up the ten directions;
whoever sees [her] even once, his sorrows go far away.

1814Her most tender body surpasses golden fresh butter;
ah, I die! How graceful the curve of every limb!

1815Mother and father cannot keep their composure;
with what tender longing they gaze again and again at the moon-like face!

1816The joyful cries of "Glory, glory!" have filled the world;
the wives of the cowherds sing auspicious songs.

1817All kinds of instruments sound, full of sweetness;
all the people dance and say, "Wonderful, wonderful!"

1818Scattering curd, milk and turmeric about the courtyard,
they laugh and make [others] laugh, displaying so many antics.

1819To the brahmanas and the bards gifts of every kind are given;
seeing this merriment, Ghanashyama is drunk with happiness.

1820Again:
What bliss today fills Vraja!
Putting on new garments and ornaments, the wives of the cowherds run —
they cannot hold on to their composure. (Refrain.)

1821In what wondrous attire they enter the house,
the cowherds, carrying loads on their shoulders!
Vrishabhanu, the jewel among kings, considers himself rich,
gazing at the moon of the little girl's face.

1822Subhanu and Suchandrabhanu cannot keep their bodies steady;470
all the cowherds dance, surrounding them.
Instruments of many kinds sound, they sing songs, drunk with prema,
waving their cloths, whirling round and round.

1823One [pours] ghee, curd and milk, another turmeric water
on someone's head, slyly catching the moment.
How great is Mukhara's longing, how many auspicious rites she performs!
Narahari watches this fun.

1824Mother and father, seeing [their daughter's] beauty at the hour of her appearance,
are beside themselves with joy — they cannot turn their eyes away.

1825For their daughter's welfare they give many gifts;
