who can describe it? [Only] the fortunate see it.

1826Here Sri Radhika, together with many little girls,
wanders about, and seeing this, her mother rejoices.

1827Here Vrishabhanu sits with his people;
there is no end to telling of the merriment in Raval.

1828O Srinivasa, Gaurachandra with His associates,
coming from Gokula, stayed here.

1829How deep was [His] absorption in ecstasy on seeing the village of Raval —
what to speak of others, even Shesha cannot describe it.

1830From all four sides people come running and raise the name of Hari;
all say, "Look, brother — the Crest-jewel of sannyasis!"

1831Drunk with drinking the nectar of the moon of the Lord's face,
someone, rejoicing, says to someone else:

1832"I have concluded in my mind: this is surely Krishna;
in this guise He wanders in Vraja by His own will."

1833Someone says, "On seeing this golden form,
what is in [my] heart does not come to my lips."

1834Saying so much, the people, by Chaitanya's mercy,
cannot keep the strength of composure — streams pour from their eyes.

1835Having manifested a wondrous pastime here, the Lord
went to Mathura with that Sanodiya brahmana.

1836O Srinivasa, this place is utterly secluded;
here are Radhika's charming childhood pastimes.

1837Speaking so much, [they] stayed the night in Raval;
in the rasa of talks about Krishna the night turned to dawn.

1838In what prema Sri Raghava was immersed
together with Srinivasa and Narottama — who will describe it?

1839Whoever hears all these narrations with care
attains the feet of Radha-Krishna and Chaitanya.

1840In the morning [they] set out from Raval
and, crossing the Yamuna, came to Mathura.

1841[There are] the dwellings of Ugrasena, Vasudeva and Kamsa;
[the place] where Kamsa seized Yashoda's daughter;

1842where Kamsa raised his hand to kill the goddess;
the place where Vasudeva was in prison;

1843the stone on which Vasudeva passed urine;471
the path by which Vasudeva went, carrying Krishna;

1844[the place] where Vasudeva crossed the Yamuna;
the path by which, leaving his son in Gokula, he returned home.

1845Showing Srinivasa all those places,
Raghava Pandita tells so much in detail.

1846Having bathed at Vishrama-tirtha with a joyful heart,
[they] came to the bank of the Krishna-ganga, to Ambika-kanana.472

1847Seeing Sri Ambika-devi and the Shiva called Gokarna,
Srinivasa and Narottama became filled with great happiness.

1848Raghava Pandita says to both, softly, softly:
look at the wondrous place on the bank of the Krishna-ganga.

1849Here the cowherds headed by Nanda, finely equipped,
came to see the festival of the deva-yatra.473

1850Mahadeva called Gokarna and Ambika — both of them —
Nanda-raya worshipped in every manner.

1851In this lovely place Nanda lay asleep,
[and] suddenly he was seized by a huge black serpent.

1852Seeing His father seized by the serpent, Krishna at that very moment,
smiling gently, touched the serpent with His foot.

1853By the touch of the Lord's lotus feet [the serpent] rejoiced at heart;
the serpent's body was gone, [he] gained a divine form.

1854Formerly [he] had been a Vidyadhara named Sudarshana,
and the serpent's body was from a brahmana's curse; [this he] told the Lord.474

1855Having offered praise to the Lord's lovely feet,
Sudarshana went to his own abode.

1856Nanda and the other cowherds, in their love, became greatly joyful;
taking Rama and Krishna with [Their] friends, they returned home.

1857Look: Sri Akrura-tirtha is the best of tirthas;475
it is known everywhere as exceedingly dear to Krishna.

1858What shall I say of the fruit of bathing [here] at the full moon:
[one] is freed from samsara — especially in [the month of] Kartika.

1859The fruit that is gained by bathing in all the tirthas
is gained by bathing at Akrura-tirtha.

1860Whoever bathes at this tirtha during a solar eclipse
gains the fruit of the Rajasuya and the Ashvamedha.

1861Thus [it is said] in the Saura Purana:
"Next is the most excellent Akrura-tirtha,
destroying all sins; it is exceedingly dear to Hari.

1862A man who bathes at that best of tirthas on the full-moon day
is truly freed from samsara — especially at the full moon of Kartika."

1863And in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Akrura is indeed the king of tirthas, the supreme secret among secrets;
[here] one gains that fruit [which comes] from bathing in all the tirthas.

1864And again, having bathed at Akrura when the sun is seized by Rahu,
a person gains the fruit of the Rajasuya and the Ashvamedha."

1865O Srinivasa, in this Akrura-grama
Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu lived in seclusion.

1866In Vrindavana [there were] crowds of people; for this reason He
would come here and, with a joyful heart, take His meal.476

1867Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu, the purifier of the worlds —
who will understand the workings of His mind?

1868Look, Srinivasa: in this most lovely place
the sages headed by Angira performed a sacrifice.477

1869For food Krishna sent His friends here;
at the words of the cowherd boys the brahmanas grew angry.

1870The friends went and reported everything to Krishna;
then Krishna sent [them] to the sages' wives.

1871The sages' wives, with great joy of heart,
brought food here and gave it to Krishnachandra.

1872Together with His companions Krishna eats the food right here;
there is no end to the merriment at the meal.

1873Everyone's heart was filled with great bliss;
all know [this place] by the name Bhojana-sthala.478

1874Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the eighty-sixth verse:
"Ah! Here the glorious company of the beautiful wives of the learned sacrificers themselves, with joy
and devotion, fed to His heart's content Achyuta, surrounded by loving friends, together with Rama,
with four kinds of food, rich in qualities, putting nectar to shame —
to this place and to that [company] we bow."479

1875O Srinivasa, behold the beauty of Vrindavana: what can compare with it? — it captivates the minds of the kings of yogis and the kings of sages.

1876Vrindavana, served by Vrinda, dear to Krishna,
destroys all sins; this [forest] is hard to attain and beautiful.

1877Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"The twelfth [forest] is Vrindavana, protected by Vrinda;480
O Earth, it is dear to Me and destroys all sins.

1878There I shall play together with the gopis and the cowherd boys;
[this place] is delightful, renowned, and hard to attain for the gods and the Danavas."

1879Brahma, Rudra and others are devoted to the service of Vrindavana;
the sages meditate on Vrindavana unceasingly.

1880As Lakshmi, devoted to bhakti, is most beloved,
so Vrindavana is dear to Govinda.

1881There, where Mount Govardhana shines in its splendour,
Rama and Krishna with Their friends are engaged in herding the cows.

1882Containing all the tirthas, it gives liberation to every living being;
Vrindavana, the abode of bliss, destroys all sorrows.

1883Thus [it is said] in the Skanda Purana, in the Mathura-khanda:
"Then [comes] holy Vrindavana, which has taken shelter of Vrinda-devi;
Hari presides in it, and Brahma, Rudra and others serve it.

1884Vrindavana is dense, vast, spreading far and wide,
full of the ashramas of sages, with forest thickets of tulasi.

1885As Lakshmi, ever devoted to bhakti, is the most beloved,
so Vrindavana on earth is Govinda's most beloved [place].

1886Together with the calves and heifers Madhava plays,
dwelling within Vrindavana, with Rama, surrounded by the boys.

1887Oh, delightful is Vrindavana, where Mount Govardhana [stands];
there are many tirthas there, made by the god Vishnu."

1888Thus [it is said] in the Padma Purana, in the Nirvana-khanda:
"The forest called the root of bliss destroys great sins,
removes all sorrows and gives liberation to every living being."

1889Vrindavana is a forest ever new;
the gopis are enchanted by the beauty of Vrindavana.

1890Thus [it is said] in the Sri Tenth [Canto], in the eleventh chapter, the twenty-eighth verse:481 "The forest named Vrindavana, good for the cattle, with fresh groves, is fit for the cowherd men, the gopis and the cows; [there are] holy hills, grasses and creepers."

1891Thus [it is said] there, in the twenty-first chapter, the tenth verse:482
"O friend, Vrindavana spreads the glory of the earth,
for it has gained its beauty from the lotus feet of the son of Devaki.
At Govinda's flute the intoxicated peacocks dance;
seeing this, all the other creatures on the mountain slopes stand still."

1892O Srinivasa, it is established in all the shastras:
Vrindavana is Krishna's most beloved abode.

1893Animals, birds, trees, insects, humans and others —
whoever lives here attains Krishna's abode in the end.

1894This forest of five yojanas is the form of Krishna's body;
in subtle form the gods and others always remain here.

1895Krishna, who contains all the gods, never leaves it;
appearance and disappearance take place [here] age after age.

1896Radiant Vrindavana is exceedingly beautiful;
without eyes of prema it is beyond the reach of physical eyes.

1897Thus [it is said] in the Gautamiya[-tantra] — the words of Sri Krishna to Narada:
"This delightful Vrindavana is wholly My abode.

1898The animals, birds, trees, insects, humans and gods
who live here, in My dwelling place, go to My abode when they die.

1899The daughters of the cowherds who live here, in My dwelling place,
are yoginis, eternally [abiding] with Me, devoted to My service.

1900This forest of five yojanas is indeed My body;
this Kalindi, called the Sushumna, carries the supreme nectar.483

1901Here the gods and [all] beings remain in subtle form;
and I, who contain all the gods, never leave this forest.

1902Here, age after age, [My] appearance and disappearance take place.
This radiant, delightful [abode] is invisible to the physical eye."

1903O Srinivasa, the greatness of Vrindavana —
each describes it in his own way, but no one finds its limit.

1904Vrindavana is sixteen kroshas: so people say;
but it is renowned in the shastras that it extends over five yojanas.484

1905What people say is not false:
the inconceivable potency of the abode reconciles everything.

1906The fortunate one who sees Govinda in Vrindavana
does not go to the city of Yama — [for this] there is evidence everywhere.

1907Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"O Vasundhara, those who see Govinda in Vrindavana
do not go to the city of Yama; they go to the destination of the doers of good."

1908In Vrindavana is the abode of Sri Govinda-deva,
always surrounded by servants, exceedingly beautiful.

1909O Srinivasa, what more can be said of it?
Whoever sees it even once has attained the goal [of life] on earth.

1910Thus [it is said] in the Skanda Purana, in the Mathura-khanda, in the words of Narada:
"In that Vrindavana is the holy abode of Govinda,
filled with His servants; there indeed I dwell.

1911On earth, in that Vrindavana, O king, is Govinda's Vaikuntha;
there are Vrinda and the other servants, longing for Govinda.

1912Those best of men, O lord of the earth, who have seen in Vrindavana
the great house of Govinda, have attained the goal [of life] on earth."

1913Sri Govinda-deva is the son of the king of Vraja Himself;
by His own will He plays as though He were a Deity.

1914Worldly people see the form of a pratima;485
His own people see Sri Govinda face to face.

1915Taking upon Himself the mauna-mudra and the rest,486
He gives His associates waves of the rasa of happiness.

1916In Vrindavana, in the whorl of an eight-petalled lotus,
He delights with His Beloved — in what wondrous splendour!

1917Thus [it is said] in the Atharva-veda:487 "In [the place] called Gokula, in Mathura-mandala, in the midst of Vrindavana, in a thousand-petalled lotus, in the middle of the sixteen petals, on the filaments of the eight petals, Govinda shines: dark, in yellow garments, two-armed, with a peacock feather on His head, with flute and staff in His hands, without qualities and with qualities, formless and with form, without activity and active.488 On His two sides are Chandravali and Radha," and so on.

1918Thus [it is said] in a statement of the Sammohana-tantra:
"To Radha, the mistress of the Yogapitha, [abiding] together with Govinda,
full of abundant havas and bhavas, I bow unceasingly."489

1919The Yogapitha in Vrindavana is the greatest wonder;490
on the Yogapitha is Govinda's wondrous beauty.

1920Thus [it is said] in the Padma Purana, in the Vrindavana-mahatmya. Parvati said:
"What is the wonderful, amazing nectar of Govinda's beauty?
I wish to hear of it — tell me, O ocean of mercy."

1921Ishvara said:
"In the middle of delightful Vrindavana, adorned with lovely mandara trees,
adorned with the branches and shoots of those trees rising a yojana high,

1922in [that] shelter of the rasa of great bliss, is a great place, a great abode,
served by swarms of bees intoxicated by the fragrance of shoots and flowers.

1923There, below, on the Siddha-pitha, is Govinda's imperishable place,
a place with seven enclosures, ever sought by the Shrutis.

1924There, on a pure golden seat adorned with a jewelled pavilion —
in its midst is the brilliant Yogapitha of beautiful workmanship.

1925It is built with eight corners, charming with manifold radiance,
and above it shines a throne of rubies and gold.

1926On it is an eight-petalled lotus; in its whorl, the abode of happiness,
is Govinda's beloved place: what can be said of its glory?

1927Here abides beautiful Govinda, served by multitudes of gopis —
Krishna, the lord of Vrindavana, with the divine form and age of Vraja,491

1928the lord of Vraja, ever full of majesty, the sole beloved of the beauties of Vraja, bearing a wondrous form in the age of budding youth."

1929The lord of Vrindavana, Sri Govinda, the abode of prema,
always delights on the throne together with Radha.

1930At the eight corners of the Yogapitha [He] is surrounded by the prakritis;492
the throne, the jewelled pavilion and the rest are incomparable.

1931Thus [it is said] in the Varaha-tantra, in the fifth patala. Sri Varaha said:
"The whorl [of the lotus] is that great abode, Govinda's imperishable place;
above it is a golden seat adorned with a jewelled pavilion."

1932Thus [it is said]:
"In the whorl is the great lila; on the mountain full of the rasa of that lila,
where Krishna is the eternal lord of the forest of Vrinda,

1933Krishna became Govinda — what need of many other words?
The third petal is delightful — the best of all, the highest of the highest."

1934Thus [it is said]:
"Govinda's beloved place — what can be said of its glory?
There abides Govinda, the beloved of the multitudes of gopis,

1935with the divine form and age of Vraja, increasing the love of the gopis,
the lord of Vraja, holding back His majesty, the sole beloved of the children of Vraja."

1936Thus [it is said]. The Earth said:
"Krishna is the supreme cause, called Govinda, higher than the highest,
the eternal lord of Vrindavana, the sole cause of the attributeless."

1937Varaha said:
"Govinda together with Radha is seated on a golden throne —
with the beauty of form described before, with divine ornaments, most beautiful,

1938bending in three places, lovely, most tender, the pupil of the gopis' eyes.
There, on the Yogapitha adorned with the golden throne, —

1939absorbed in ardour in every limb, the principal beloveds of Krishna —
are the prakritis headed by Lalita, and the original prakriti, Radhika.

1940In front is the goddess Lalita, and in the north-west Shyamala;
in the north Sri Madhumati, in the north-east Dhanya; Hari's beloved493

1941Vishakha is likewise in the east; after her, Shaibya in the south-east;
Padma in the south, Bhadra in the south-west: so they are placed in order.

1942At the tips of the corners of the Yogapitha is the charming beloved Chandravali;
and the eight prakritis other than her are principal beloveds of Krishna.

1943The principal and original prakriti is Radhika, surpassing all;494
Chitravesha, Vrinda, Chandra, Madana-sundari,

1944Supriya, Madhumati, Shashirekha, Haripriya — in order, beginning from the front, are likewise placed in the cardinal and intermediate directions.

1945Sixteen years old, the best of the prakritis, the principal beloved of Krishna —495 is Radha, the Queen of Vrindavana; likewise Lalita too is dear [to Him]."

1947Thus [it is said] in the Gautamiya-tantra:496
"[Him who sits] on a jewelled throne joined to a jewel mountain,
in a golden pavilion amid the wish-fulfilling trees."

1948Govinda's sweetness intoxicates the world:
whoever sees Him even once finds nothing [else] pleasing.

1949Thus [it is said] in the Sri Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, in the Purva-vibhaga, in the second lahari, the hundred and eleventh verse:497
"Smiling, bending in three places, casting wide sidelong glances,
with lips soft as shoots placed on the flute, resplendent with a peacock feather —
this form of Hari called Govinda, here near Keshi-tirtha,
do not look at, O friend, if you [still] delight in the company of your kin."

1950Govinda, whose form is eternity, knowledge and bliss, is beautiful;
with the mauna-mudra, two-armed, exceedingly enchanting.498

1951Thus [it is said] in the Gopala-tapani, in the Purva-vibhaga, the eleventh verse:499
"With beautiful lotus eyes, like a cloud, clad in a garment the colour of lightning,
two-armed, with the mauna-mudra, the Lord wearing the forest garland,

1952surrounded by cowherds, gopis and cows, sheltered beneath the tree of the gods,
adorned with divine ornaments, abiding in the middle of a jewelled lotus,

1953fanned by the breeze that touches the waves of the Kalindi's waters —
meditating in the heart on such a Krishna, a person is freed from the cycle of births."

1954In the same place, the thirty-fifth verse:
"That one Govinda, whose form is eternity, knowledge and bliss," and so on.

1955O Srinivasa! In sweet Sri Vrindavana,
who does not bow down at the feet of these three?

1956Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana —
the feet of these three are everyone's all in all.

1957Madana-gopala is called Madanamohana;
this name is renowned — everyone knows it.

1958In the Gopala-tapani, in the Purva-vibhaga, the thirty-seventh, forty-first and forty-third verses: "To Gopala, to Govardhana, to Gopinatha, to Govinda — obeisance, obeisance!"500

1960O Srinivasa! There is no end to telling of this;501
all this is proclaimed in the Urdhvamnaya-tantra.502

1961Thus [it is said]:
Sri Parvati said:
"Who is this Govinda-deva whom you mentioned before?
What is His glory like, and what is His nature, O Shankara?"

1962Sri Mahadeva said:
"Gopala is Govinda Himself; He is ever both manifest and unmanifest.
In Vrindavana, on the Yogapitha, He abides perpetually.

1963In all four yugas He is the lord of Sri Vrindavana;
worshipped by Nanda-gopa and others, He is deeply worshipped even by Krishna.503

1964The stealer of the garments of the maidens of Vraja, the fulfiller of their vow,
whose form is a stone full of consciousness and bliss, He pervades the Vraja-mandala.504

1965Having passed beyond kaishora, He abides [so] day after day;
His mouth is honoured with tambula; He is the lord of Radhika's life.

1966With four banks inlaid with jewels, full of swans, lotuses and so on,
[there is] a pond named Brahma-kunda; to its south

1967shines a jewelled pavilion surrounded by mandara trees;
in its midst is the supreme seat of sovereignty called the Yogapitha.

1968Here Krishna, coloured by the abundant rasa of sovereignty of the Queen of Vrindavana, was conquered by Radha with Her bold laughter.

1969Ever [here] are Vrinda — His bodily splendour — and Vira, who accomplishes everything; to the east of the Yogapitha stands [she] who is called Lilavati.505

1970In the south stands Shyama, who delights in Krishna's play;
in the west there always abides the goddess named Bhagini.506

1971In the north there ever stands the goddess named Siddheshi.
In the east stands the Five-faced, and in the south the Ten-faced;507

1972in the west, the Four-faced; in the north, the Thousand-faced.
And she who holds a golden cane in her hand, appointed to command everywhere,

1973named Madanonmadini, the dear friend of Radhika,
leads to the tree Govinda, who is distraught with mana.508

1974Even she who heightens the pride of the husband of Rati himself, here, in the abode of the form of the Pair, in the stronghold of Kama's pride, with the sweetnesses of the fresh blue of the sapphire Hari builds up at every step the palace of Manmatha.509

1975First the twofold [syllable] of Manmatha, then the word 'shri-krishnaya',
after it 'govindaya', and then 'svaha': this twelve-syllable
great mantra of Govinda in time brings one to share in purva-anuraga.510

1976Next I shall tell [the mantra] of Govinda as the Pair:
after [the syllables] of Lakshmi and Manmatha, the words 'radha-govindabhyam namah'.

1977Merely by knowing it, Radha and Krishna become gracious.
The rishi of these two [mantras] is Kama; the metre is declared to be virat;

1978the devata is the eternal Govinda, and also Radha and Govinda; the shakti is the Mistress of the Yogapitha; the six limbs [of nyasa] are with the kama-bijas.511

1979Let [one] meditate on Govinda-deva, sweet as a fresh cloud, dancing divine pastimes, with a gleaming wrestler's tuck, holding in both hands the flute and a jewelled staff, charming with the tassels of the broad ends of the spotless yellow cloth laid over His shoulders, complete, Sri Mohanendra, whose right shin is crossed by His other foot.

1980Having meditated thus, let him chant the mantra up to four lakhs [of times]; at the end of a homa with sesame and ghee, let him worship the Lord and the Lady of the Yogapitha512

1981with flowers of champaka, ashoka, tulasi, kahlara, and also with lotuses —
[and] he sees directly with his own eyes the Pair, Radha and Govinda.

1982Here too the beautiful Madana-gopala is firmly established.
Gopala is in the form of kaishora, Govinda in a mature form.

1983Compared with these two, Gopinatha is the most beautiful.
Gopala, then, is dhiroddhata; as dhirodatta is described513

1984Govinda; Gopikanatha is he whose form is dhira-lalita.
Gopala has the waist of a lion; graceful in three bends is

1985Govinda; Gopikanatha is broad-chested, a connoisseur of love.
Three times a day there is now one sweetness, now another, in the Lord of the cowherds514

1986in the ravine of Govardhana, variegated with young shoots and so on.
Having passed beyond childhood, having gone beyond kaishora,

1987immersed in Kandarpa, Sri Govinda shines
on this Yogapitha, captivating with many jewels.

1988Such is its innate power: [Govinda] is soon pleased.
The perfection [attained] at other siddha-pithas over many years

1989arises in a single day at the Yogapitha in Vrindavana.
In the early morning [it] is like the young sun, at sangava of auspicious radiance,515

1990at midday like the full-grown sun, in the afternoon like a lotus petal,
in the evening like a heap of vermilion, and at night pure as the moon;

1991on dark nights of a dusky radiance, like the rays of a sapphire,
and in the rains it always shines with the green light of grass and emerald;

1992in autumn like the disc of the moon, in late autumn like a ruby,
in winter like a diamond, in spring rosy as young shoots;

1993in summer like a flood of nectar: [thus] the Yogapitha shines.
Ever covered with sweetnesses, surrounded by ashoka creepers,

1994enveloped on all sides, below and above, by the rays of great jewels —
"Unassailable for Chandravali," "Temple of Radha's Good Fortune" —

1995[it] is named "Sri Ratna-mandapa," and also "Shringara-mandapa,"
is named "Saubhagya-mandapa," "Maha-madhurya-mandapa,"516

1996is named "Samrajya-mandapa," and also "Surata-mandapa,"
is named "Ananda-mandapa," and also "Surata-mandapa" —
these are the eight names of the Yogapitha; listen, O Parvati.517

1997Whoever recites at dawn the eightfold names
of the most great Sri Yogapitha
thereby brings Govinda-deva under his sway
and attains prema for the Supreme Person."
Thus [ends] in the Urdhvamnaya the nineteenth patala, called "The Revelation of the Yogapitha."518

1998Having said this, Sri Pandita, with jubilation in his heart,
slowly walks on from Bhojana-tila.519

1999Going a little way, he speaks sweet words:
here the sage Saubhari performed austerities.520

2000Look: on the bank of the Yamuna is a secluded place;
everyone knows the village called Gonarakha.521

2001This here is Kaliya-hrada — look, Srinivasa;522
here took place Sri Krishna's most wondrous pastime.

2002Climbing the kadamba of play on the bank of the Kalindi,
He leapt with a plunge into the waters of the Kalindi.

2003He subdues Kaliya in the waters of the Kalindi;
He dances on the hoods of the serpent Kaliya — everyone sees [it].

2004Krishna bestowed His mercy on the serpent Kaliya;
from here He sent him away to Ramanaka-dvipa.523

2005Whoever bathes and so on in this Kaliya-hrada
is freed from all sins without effort.

2006Leaving the body here, [one] goes to Vishnu-loka;
the Puranas say that many other fruits too are obtained [here].

2007Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Coming to the pool of Kaliya and engaging in play [there], O Vasundhara,
merely by bathing there [one] is freed from all sins.

2008And whoever gives up his life here goes to My world."

2009In the Tenth Canto [of the Bhagavatam], in the sixteenth chapter, the sixty-second verse:524
"Whoever, bathing in this place of My play, satisfies the gods and others with its waters,
and, having fasted, remembering Me, performs worship, is freed from all sins."

2010That kadamba, climbing which Krishna leapt into the pool —
the beauty of that huge tree the shastras have revealed.

2011Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Even now learned men see a great wonder:
to the east of Kaliya-hrada [stands] a revered kadamba tree —

2012hundred-branched, O wide-eyed one, holy and fragrant;
in all twelve months it, charming, auspicious and cool,
blossoms, O wide-eyed one, [and] the ten directions shine."

2013This Kaliya-tirtha destroys sins committed at holy places;525
bathing at Kali-tirtha brings the fulfilment of many aims.

2014Thus [it is said] in the Saura Purana:
"Then comes the tirtha called Kaliya-tirtha, the destroyer of sin,
where the Lord, as a child, danced on Kaliya's head.

2015Whoever bathes there and worships Vasudeva
attains sayujya with Krishna, unattainable for the unfortunate."526

2016Look: here is the Dvadashaditya-tirtha;527
[here] one obtains the desired fruit — this is known from the Puranas.

2017Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"A man who has bathed in Surya-tirtha and seen the Adityas, O Vasundhara,
reaches the world of Aditya and, having done what was to be done, rejoices.

2018On the day of the Sun, at sankranti, at this tirtha, O Vasundhara,
[people] obtain what the heart desires — of this there is no doubt."528

2019In the Saura Purana:
"Then comes the purifying tirtha called the Dvadashaditya-tirtha;
merely by the sight of it, people's sin perishes."

2020O Srinivasa, Krishna, having subdued Kali[ya],
came from Kali-hrada onto this hill.

2021The Suns, knowing that Krishna was badly chilled,
drove away the cold by displaying fierce heat.

2022Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the eighty-second verse:
"Where the enemy of Mura, chilled, by the twelve suns with their fierce heat,
full of the weight of bhakti and prema — He of generous deeds, the beautiful one — was joyfully and especially served,
where He shines, lovingly surrounded by women and men and by herds of lowing cattle —
in this tirtha named Dvadasha-surya I always take refuge."

2023O Srinivasa, by Mahaprabhu's command
Sanatana, having come to Vraja, settled here.

2024Sanatana had been told that the Lord would come;
for Him he made a place — look — in this solitude.529

2025Seeing Sanatana anxious, Gaurahari
mercifully showed Himself to him here in the guise of a dream.

2026Gaurachandra is seated on a divine throne;
Sanatana, prostrating himself, fell at [His] feet.

2027The Lord, firmly embracing Sanatana
and consoling him in every way, vanished from sight.

2028Wondrous are the Lord's pastimes — who can understand them?
He always sports in Vrindavana as He wishes.

2029Look at the holy place Praskandana: by bathing [here] sin departs;530
and one who gives up life [here] attains Vishnu-loka.

2030Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"I shall tell of yet another [place] — hear it, O Vasundhara:
[there is] an auspicious holy place named Praskandana, which takes away all sins.

2031A man who bathes there is freed from all sins;
and if he gives up life here, he goes to My world."

2032O Srinivasa, from the heat of the suns
the cold went away, and sweat appeared on [His] body.

2033That sweat-water mingled with the daughter of the Sun [the Yamuna];
for this reason the tirtha received the name "Praskandana".

2034Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the eighty-third verse:
"From the abundant sweat that arose all over from long exposure to the burning sun
and flowed from Govinda's body, an exalted tirtha came into being.
Captivating with fragrances flowing from those tender, dense, most beautiful and splendid limbs [of His body],
with pure water and brilliant radiance — that Praskandana I honour with praises."531

2035Having shown Srinivasa the Praskandana-ghat,
[Raghava], absorbed in prema, speaks in most sweet words:

2036Besides Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Lord Advaita
[too] lived for some days in this forest.532

2037Under this banyan He worshipped Krishna;
who can understand His unfathomable intent?

2038How this Lord was born and so on, and how He came here —
listen, Srinivasa, I shall tell of that briefly.

2039Together with the master Madhavendra Puri,533 Shachi and Jagannatha,
Lord Advaita appeared [in the world].

2040Advaita's mercy towards living beings is boundless:
under the guise of birth He blessed Bengal.

2041In Bengal, near Shrihatta, is Navagrama;
there [lived] Kuvera Pandita, a descendant of Nrisimha.534

2042Kuvera Pandita was greatly blessed on the path of bhakti;
apart from Krishna's lotus feet, he knew nothing else.

2043Such too was his wife Nabha Devi, devoted to her husband,
worshipped by the world — she is Advaita's mother.

2044The two of them, coming to Shantipura, to the Ganga,535
were ceaselessly immersed in conversation about Krishna.

2045One day Sri Kuvera, together with Nabha,
hearing the blasphemy of Vaishnavas, wished to die.

2046A certain fortunate person, seeing them both all but dead,
by Krishna's will calmed them.

2047Even so, sorrowful, they lay down;
when a little sleep came, he sees a wondrous dream.

2048A beautiful Purusha, full of great effulgence,
whose body surpasses a mountain of molten gold;536

2049this Purusha, to another beautiful Purusha,
holding [His] two hands, speaks most sweet words:

2050"To dispel this suffering of beings stricken by Kali,
quickly descend You upon the earth.

2051When You draw [Me], I shall not be able to stay [away];
with [My] elder brother I shall soon appear [in the world]."

2052Hearing these words, with a heart full of joy,
at an auspicious moment He entered Nabha's womb.

2053Seeing this, the brahmana's joy was boundless;
when his sleep broke, his heart was stirred.

2054The brahmana, a great knower of the scriptures, reflected in his mind:
in Kali the Lord appears hidden.537

2055Thinking much in this way, he was overwhelmed;
together with his wife he could not stop his tears.

2056From that day Nabha was with child;
[they] went again to Navagrama and settled [there].

2057There Lord Advaita appeared;
great jubilation arose in the hearts of [all] the world.

2058Suddenly this voice arose: "Through Him
Sri Krishna Chaitanya will appear on earth.

2059He will soon bring Nityananda-Rama;
with hosts of associates [the Lord] will joyfully sport.

2060He will destroy the sufferings of living beings — there is no more cause for worry;
in every home prema-bhakti will be preached.

2061The ocean of the bliss of sankirtana will surge;
blessed is this [age of] Kali! — no one will be left deprived."

2062Hearing such various voices, all rejoiced;
Kuvera's house became an abode of all that is auspicious.

2063Day by day Lord Advaita grows;
the fortunate see [Him] with jubilant hearts.

2064Advaita always keeps Himself hidden;
at times, by Sri Chaitanya's will, He becomes manifest.

2065Having obtained Advaita, the people of Navagrama
float in bliss, forgetting sorrow and grief.

2066"Kamalaksha" and "Advaita" are the Lord's two names;538
"Advaita" — so all call [Him] ceaselessly.

2067Advaita's childhood pastimes are exceedingly wondrous;
the fortunate see them — who has the power to describe them?

2068Sri Advaita is to everyone like the pupil of the eye;
lying down and in their dreams [people] sing of Advaita's virtues.

2069Blessed are all these people, I say again and again;
blessed is Bengal, where the Lord appeared.

2070Sri Kuvera, full of prema-bhakti, most steadfast,
said to all: "I shall go to the bank of the Ganga."

2071Together with his fellow villagers and beloved friends
he came from Navagrama to Shantipura.

2072He settled in Shantipura with a contented heart;
at times he met his friends in Navadvipa.

2073He carefully had Advaita study the shastras;
the Lord, the purifier of the fallen, became a pandita.

2074Although the father and mother knew the true nature of their son,
out of parental love they kept none of it in memory.

2075All the great panditas living in Shantipura
were amazed to see Advaita's acts.

2076Some said: "Advaita is by no means a human being:
can a human so attract everyone's heart?

2077Blessed is this brahmana Kuvera, who has such a son!
Through Him, it seems, good fortune will come to all."

2078Thus everyone said many things;
Advaitachandra became the life of all.

2079Who can understand the will of Advaita Prabhu?
He gives joy to His mother and father in many ways.

2080After some time His father and mother passed from sight;
the Lord set out to perform [the rites at] Gaya.

2081On the pretext of Gaya He travelled to all the tirthas;
from Madhavendra Puri He received the mantra of initiation.

2082Thus it was said by the ancients:539
"I worship Sri Advaita Prabhu, the giver of prema-bhakti,
dear to Sriman Madhavendra Puri, belonging to the Sri Madhva-sampradaya."

2083Who has the power to understand Advaita's acts?
Intoxicated with prema, He wanders ceaselessly.

2084Wandering on and on, He came to Mathura-mandala;
seeing the beauty of Vraja, bliss welled up [in Him].

2085Having seen everything, He came to Vrindavana;
here the Vrajavasis lovingly sheltered [Him].

2086He eats a little — fruits, roots, milk;
seeing Advaita's radiance, people marvel.

2087Intoxicated with prema, He roars thunderous hunkaras;
"Shall I see Krishna?" — saying this, He weeps.

2088Thus moment by moment various bhavas arise [in Him];
He worships Krishna here, near the Yamuna.

2089Knowing [that] the time of Krishna Chaitanya's appearance [had come],
He departed from here for the land of Gauda.

2090Advaitachandra's pastimes are like nectar;
O Srinivasa, the fortunate relish them.

2091The banyan under which Advaita stayed
became famed everywhere as Advaita-vata.540

2092By the sight of this Advaita-vata all sins are destroyed,
and most rare prema-bhakti becomes attainable.

2093Look at the trees and creepers on the bank of the Kalindi:
ever fresh, exceedingly beautiful.

2094This tamarind tree is very old;
here Radha and Krishna sport together with the sakhis.541

2095Remembering the past, Krishna Chaitanya Gosani
came here and sat down — there was no limit to His happiness.

2096Saying this, the Pandita was overwhelmed with prema;
he tells Srinivasa of the deeds of Gorachand.

2097Sri Gaurasundara is the complete Brahman, the eternal,
the Lord of Navadvipa, Krishna, the son of the king of Vraja.

2098In Navadvipa, in the house of Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra,
the Lord descended at Advaita's hunkaras.542

2099The wondrous pastimes of Gauranga in Navadvipa
cannot be described even with a thousand mouths.

2100Some time after His father's departure,
He came to Gaya, as if following worldly custom, to perform [the rites].

2101There Sri Ishvara Puri, most fortunate,
on seeing Gaurachandra felt as if he had found his life.

2102The life of the devotees, the Lord Sri Gaurasundara,
showed Ishvara Puri the highest respect.

2103When he spoke his own initiation mantra into His ear,
He received the mantra, falling to the ground and bowing down.

2104Having made Ishvara Puri His guru, Gaura-raya
constantly floats in the streams from both His eyes.

2105Having made Vishvambhara, the purifier of the worlds, his disciple,
Sri Ishvara Puri became intoxicated with the bliss of prema.

2106If you say, "Gaurachandra is the guru of the world;
to hear that He has another guru is puzzling,"

2107to this I reply: for the instruction of the people
He Himself, by practising dharma, establishes it.

2108Who can know this unearthly pastime of the Lord?
He Himself glorified the Madhva sampradaya.

2109When one enters a sampradaya, one's purpose is accomplished;
a mantra received in initiation elsewhere is certainly fruitless.

2110The four sampradayas — Sri, Madhva, Rudra and Sanaka —
are known in [the age of] Kali: the Puranas tell [of this] in detail.543

2111Thus [it is said] in the Sri Padma Purana:
Mantras that are without a sampradaya are considered fruitless.
Therefore in Kali four [founders of] sampradayas will appear.544

2112Sri, Madhva, Rudra and Sanaka — Vaishnavas who purify the earth —
these four will be the founders of sampradayas in Kali.

2113These four sampradayas hold the right to bhakti;
I shall tell briefly how the names of the sampradayas [arose].

2114Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu, the tree of desires,
in the form of Narayana is the guru of them all.

2115Sri is the beloved of Narayana and also His disciple;
her wondrous deeds are described at length in all the scriptures.

2116The word "Sri" means Lakshmi; her branches and sub-branches
became many — who could write them down?

2117In that circle Ramanuja became the acharya;
from him the Ramanuja sampradaya went forth.

2118Formerly his name was Sri Lakshmanacharya;
with great reverence everyone calls [him] Ramanujacharya.545

2119He composed the Ramanuja-bhashya, [named] after himself;
his branches and sub-branches covered the world.

2120O Srinivasa! About the Madhva sampradaya
I shall say a little now, and further on I shall tell what [is due].

2121The disciple of Sri Narayana is the merciful Brahma;
his disciples, their disciples and others filled the world.

2122In that circle Sri Madhva became a disciple;
first of all he composed a commentary on the Brahma-sutra.

2123For this reason he received the name Madhvacharya;
from then on the Madhvacharya sampradaya spread.546

2123aSri Anandatirtha is another name of his;
he is known everywhere and is peerless in all virtues.547

2123bThere is no end to his disciples and their disciples;
spreading bhakti, they filled every place.

2124The disciple of Sri Narayana is the compassionate Rudra;
there is no end to his disciples and their disciples.

2125In that circle Vishnusvami became a disciple;
he was intoxicated with the rasa of bhakti together with his disciples.548

2126Supreme power, learning in all the scriptures —
from him came the name "Vishnusvami sampradaya".

2127Hear, Srinivasa, how the Sanaka sampradaya is:
from Narayana — the manifestation of the form of Hamsa.549

2128His disciples are the four great souls, Sanaka and the others;
their disciples and their disciples' disciples cannot be written down.

2129In that circle Nimbaditya became a disciple;
from him the Nimbaditya sampradaya went forth.550

2130Nimbaditya's power is supremely astonishing;
his disciples and their disciples filled the world.

2131In the sampradayas of Sri, Madhva, Rudra and Sanaka
many sampradayas arose by virtue of [their] power.

2132Thus, among the followers of Ramanujacharya,
Ramanandacharya became venerable in every respect.551

2133His disciples, their disciples and others are many;
that sampradaya became known as "Ramanandi".

2134In the Vishnusvami sampradaya Sri Vallabhacharya,
noble in every respect, composed the Anubhashya.

2135He became known as [the founder of] the "Vallabhi";
what shall I say — such is the way of the other sampradayas as well.552

2136The Lord glorified the Madhva sampradaya in Kali;
I shall name the Lord's guru and the others, from the very first.

2137The origin of all is the Lord of Paravyoma, Narayana;
His disciple is Brahma, the ornament of Brahma-loka.553

2138His disciple is Sri Narada Muni, full of prema;
Vyasa, the guru of Sri Shuka, is his disciple.

2139The magnanimous Sri Madhva became Vyasa's disciple;
he composed a commentary under his own name — [his] glory is boundless.

2140From then on the Madhvacharya sampradaya went forth;
Srimat Padmanabhacharya became his disciple.

2141His disciple is Narahari, his [disciple] is Sri Madhava,
Sri Akshobhya is his disciple, renowned everywhere.554

2142Jayatirtha is his disciple, his [disciple] is Jnanasindhu;
his disciple is Mahanidhi, the friend of the poor and lowly.

2143His [disciple] is Vidyanidhi, his is the renowned Rajendra,
his is Jayadharma Muni, wondrous in his deeds.

2144In his circle Vishnu Puri became a disciple;
he brought forth the book Bhakti-ratnavali.555

2145Jayadharma Muni's disciple, pure in conduct,
is known by the name Sri Purushottama Brahmanya.

2146His disciple is Vyasatirtha, a man of great learning;
it was he who wrote the book Sri Vishnu-samhita.556

2147His disciple is Lakshmipati, the abode of virtues;
his disciple is Madhavendra, the rising moon of bhakti.

2148His disciple is Ishvara Puri, the treasury of mercy;
his disciple is the Lord Gaurachandra, Bhagavan.

2149Thus [it is said] in the Srimad Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, [composed] by Sri Kavi Karnapura:
In the Kali-yuga there appeared four [founders of] sampradayas,
called Sri, Madhva, Rudra and Sanaka, as is stated in the Padma [Purana]:557

2150"Therefore in Kali four [founders of] sampradayas will appear —
Sri, Madhva, Rudra and Sanaka, Vaishnavas who purify the earth."

2151Of these, the Madhva sampradaya is described here as the occasion requires.
Brahma, the lord of the universe, became the disciple of the Lord of Paravyoma.

2152His disciple was Narada, and Vyasa became his disciple;
Shuka became Vyasa's disciple by restraining knowledge.558

2153His disciples and their disciples abide on earth in great numbers.
From Vyasa the renowned Madhvacharya received initiation into [the mantra of] Krishna.

2154Having analysed the Vedas, he composed the samhita Shata-dushani,
in which Brahman with qualities is established over Brahman without qualities.559

2155His disciple was the noble Padmanabhacharya;
his disciple was Narahari, and his disciple the brahmana Madhava.

2156His disciple was Akshobhya, and his disciple Jayatirtha;
his disciple was Jnanasindhu, his disciple Mahanidhi.

2157His disciple was Vidyanidhi, his servant Rajendra,
his disciple Jayadharma Muni, in whose circle [was]

2158Srimat Vishnu Puri, whose work is the Bhakti-ratnavali.
The disciple of Jayadharma was Brahmanya Purushottama.

2159His disciple was Vyasatirtha, who composed the Vishnu-samhita;
his disciple was Srimat Lakshmipati, the shelter of the rasa of bhakti.

2160His disciple was Madhavendra, by whom this dharma was set going —
the descent of the wish-fulfilling tree that stands in Vraja-dhama

2161and bears the fruits called prita, preyas, vatsala and ujjvala.560
His disciple was the illustrious renunciant, the Puri named Ishvara.

2162Gaura, respectfully accepting Ishvara Puri [as His guru],
flooded the world — both the material and the non-material.

2163The disciple of Ishvara Puri is the Lord Gaura-raya;
the Lord sings Puri's glory with His own mouth.

2164Who can understand the Lord's wondrous bhakti?
From the Lord the Nimananda sampradaya went forth.

2165Among the Lord's names the chief is Nimai Pandita;
Nityananda Prabhu is very fond of this name.

2166Seeing the Lord's Vaishnavas in Nadia,
people to this day extol them as "the Nimai sampradaya".

2167Nimai bestowed bliss upon the world —
for this reason [He] is famed on earth as Nimananda.561

2168As I told earlier how the other sampradayas are,
so, by the Lord's power, is the Madhva sampradaya.

2169Thus [it is said] in a verse composed by Sri Gopala-guru Gosvami, disciple of Srimat Vakreshvara Pandita:
Sriman Narayana, Brahma, Narada and Vyasa,
Srila Madhva, Padmanabha, Nrihari and Madhava,562

2170Akshobhya, Jayatirtha, Jnanasindhu, Mahanidhi,
Vidyanidhi, Rajendra and Jayadharma Muni,

2171Purushottama Brahmanya and Vyasatirtha Muni,
Srimat Lakshmipati, Sriman Madhavendra Puri, Ishvara [Puri].

2172Then Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the tree of prema on earth,
He who is famed throughout the circle of the earth by the name Nimananda.

2173O Srinivasa, Gaurahari, having bestowed His mercy on Ishvara Puri,
set out from Gaya.

2174Formerly in Navadvipa He kept Himself hidden from the devotees;
again He wishes to hide — but He cannot hide.

2175Shortly, Gaurachandra, having come to Nadia,
revealed Himself by the wish of His dear devotees.

2176All the devotees of the Lord — Advaita and the others —
were filled with great joy at heart.

2177The happiness that grew at the meeting with Nityananda —
who could describe it, even with a hundred thousand mouths?

2178With Nityananda, Advaita and the others, Gaura-raya
is ceaselessly intoxicated with sankirtana in Nadia.

2179Performing supremely wondrous deeds day after day,
He resolved to give up the life of a householder.

2180The Lord of the world, Gora, the enchanter of the universe,
out of mercy for living beings accepted sannyasa.

2181Having accepted sannyasa, the Lord was overwhelmed [with love];
Nityananda took [Him] to Advaita's house.

2182To see the Lord Gorachand, the crest-jewel of sannyasis,
people came running, unable to restrain themselves.

2183Gods and men gathered together as one:
hundreds of thousands of people surrounded Advaita's house.

2184All ceaselessly called out, "Hari, Hari!" —
heaven, earth and Patala were struck with wonder.

2185The crest-jewel of sannyasis, Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
granting His darshan, blessed all people.

2186Gaurahari dances in the sankirtana;
His body is adorned with sandal — a wondrous sweetness.

2187On all sides all the devotees of the Lord
together sing the sweetest kirtana.

2188Nityananda, Advaita, Srivasa and Gadadhara
do not leave the Lord's side, their hearts jubilant.

2189Raising His arms, the Lord calls, "Hari, Hari!" —
and in the bliss of sankirtana floats in His tears.

2190At the sight of such a Lord, Chaitanyachand,
the people were overwhelmed [with love], forgetting themselves.

2191Some, stepping aside, said to one another,
"The Vedas describe this Ishvara in the form of a brahmana."

2192Thus [it is said] in the Sama-veda:563
Om. When the seer sees the Golden One, the Creator, the Lord, the Purusha, the source of Brahman,
then the wise one, shaking off virtue and sin, stainless, attains the supreme equality.

2193Someone said, "Mishra Vishvambhara is in the form of a devotee,
endowed with all the marks; He is above all."

2194Thus [it is said]:
Hence I, having accepted sannyasa, shall descend — endowed with qualities, detached, without desires, a god on earth, dwelling on the bank of the Alakananda, in Kali, after four thousand years have passed, within five thousand — golden in complexion, long-limbed, endowed with all the marks, entreated by Ishvara, tasting My own rasa, in the form of a devotee, by the name of Mishra, versed in yoga — upon her.
So in the third kanda of the Atharvana, after the Brahma-vibhaga.564

2195Someone said, "In this Kali, in its first sandhya,
the Vedas sing of the oneness with His own shakti in this Gaurachandra."

2196Thus [it is said] in the Atharva-veda, in the Purusha-bodhini: In the seventh — "of the golden Vishnu": by this — having attained oneness with His own shakti, at the end, at dawn, having descended together with His own, He teaches His own mantra.565

2196aIts explanation: In the seventh — in the seventh manvantara, [the manvantara] of Vaivasvata Manu, the golden Bhagavan, with His own shakti — the hladini shakti — having attained oneness, at the end — in the Kali-yuga, at dawn — in the first sandhya, having descended, together with His own — with His associates, His own mantra — "Hare Krishna" and the rest — teaches, instructs the people.566

2197Someone said, "Look: a golden body, smooth and glossy!
Ah, how wondrous are the ornaments of sandal!"

2198Thus [it is said] in the Sahasra-nama-stotra:567 Of golden colour, with a golden body, with beautiful limbs, [adorned] with sandal and armlets.

2199Someone said, "Gora is the thief of everyone's life;
the three worlds are intoxicated with His deeds.

2200The yellow colour He assumes in this blessed Kali;
white, red and black — in Satya, Treta and Dvapara."

2201Thus [it is said] in the Tenth Canto, in the eighth chapter, the thirteenth verse:568
Indeed, He had three colours, assuming bodies in each yuga:
white, red and likewise yellow; now He has become black.

2202Someone said, "Within He is black in colour;
without, a captivating golden lustre is manifest.

2203With Nityananda, Advaita and the others He sports;
by the worship of sankirtana He is attained."

2204Thus [it is said] there too, in the Eleventh Canto, in the fifth chapter, the thirty-second verse:569 Black in colour, yet not black in lustre, with [His] angas, upangas, weapons and associates — Him the intelligent worship with sacrifices consisting chiefly of sankirtana.

2205Someone said, "This Lord is the saviour of all;
there will never again be one so merciful.

2206The dharma of the Kali-yuga is nama-sankirtana;
having descended, He joyfully established dharma."

2207Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gita, in the fourth chapter, the eighth verse:
For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the wicked
and for the establishment of dharma I appear from yuga to yuga.

2208Someone said, "Who can understand the pastimes of the Lord?570
By accepting sannyasa He has made the Kali-yuga blessed."

2209Thus [it is said] in the Sahasra-nama-stotra:
He who accepts sannyasa, self-restrained, serene, devoted to steadfastness and peace.

2210Someone said, "In Kali the fortune of living beings is great:
having accepted sannyasa, the Lord destroys [their] evil-mindedness."

2211Thus [it is said] in the Upapurana — the words of Sri Krishna [addressed] to Vyasa:
I Myself, O brahmana, at times, having taken the ashrama of sannyasa,
make the people of Kali, struck down by sin, accept hari-bhakti.

2212Someone said, "By the gift of the great mantra of harinama
He Himself destroys the grievous sufferings of living beings."

2213Thus [it is said]:
Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare
Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare.

2214Someone said, "The syllables of the names Hari, Krishna and Rama
give birth to a wondrous meaning — the best of the wise relish it."

2215Thus [it is said] in the verses composed by Sri Gopala-guru Gosvami:
Having made known the truth of Bhagavan — the form full of consciousness and bliss —
He removes ignorance and its effects; therefore He is called Hari.

2216She, the embodiment of Krishna's bliss, steals the mind of Sri Krishna;
therefore by this very [word] "Hara" Sri Radha is glorified.

2217The master of the one happiness — bliss, dark, lotus-eyed,
the delight of Gokula, the son of Nanda — He is called Krishna.

2218The essence and whole wealth of artfulness, the presiding deity of embodied pastimes, ever giving delight to Radhika — He is named Rama.

2219Thus, speaking of many things, all the people
surrendered themselves at the feet of Sri Chaitanya.

2220The crest-jewel of sannyasis, the Lord Gaura-raya,
thus passes [His days] in bliss in Advaita's house.

2221All who had come from Navadvipa to Shantipura
He comforted at heart in various ways.

2222Having consoled mother Sri Shachi in every way,
He placed the dust of her lotus feet on His head.

2223Shachi Thakurani, overwhelmed with affection,
gave this order: "Stay in Nilachala."

2224By His mother's order the Lord set out;
who can describe how the devotees became?

2225In the feigned guise of a sannyasi, wandering through all lands,
He entered the Mathura-mandala.

2226Taking with Him the Sanodiya brahmana of Mathura,
absorbed in bhakti, He roams Vraja in great joy.

2227Wherever He Himself had formerly performed whatever pastimes —
as though not knowing, He asks everyone about them.

2228To hear [of them] from the mouths of others is boundless joy for Him;
with such sport the son of Shachi is intoxicated.

2229Gradually wandering through the groves and forests,
He came to Vrindavana by way of Mathura.

2230What transformations of feeling [He had] on the bank of the Yamuna —
even with a hundred thousand mouths I could not describe.

2231Countless, countless people come running from all sides,
and, greatly intoxicated with prema, sing of Gaura's qualities.

2232For fear of the crowds the Lord, going to Akrura,
takes His alms there, finding solitude.571

2233From time to time, sitting beneath the tamarind tree,
the Lord in His own bliss floats in His tears.

2234Beneath this tamarind (amli) a great wonder took place:
He showed great mercy to Krishnadasa Rajput.572

2235O Srinivasa, from this Amli-tala
the Lord went to Nilachala, by the wish of the devotees.

2236Whoever beholds this tamarind tree
will surely have his desire fulfilled.

2237Look at this wondrous banyan on the bank of the Yamuna:
everyone calls it Shringaravata.

2238Here Sri Krishna, in various pastimes of dressing and the like,
increased the joy of Subala and His other friends.

2239Some also call it "Nityananda-vata";
whatever anyone says, all of it is true.

2240How Nityananda came here
I shall tell in brief; listen.

2241Nityananda-Rama is one body with Chaitanya;
His birthplace is in Rarh, the village of Ekachakra.573

2242His father was Hadai Pandita, His mother Padmavati;
their life was in their son — what power [have I] to describe their love?

2243The son of Padmavati, in supreme bliss,
manifested various pastimes in the village of Ekachakra.

2244The pastimes [He] had performed in various avataras —
in that mood He showed them all to the people.

2245The people living in the land of Ekachakra are fortunate:
Nityananda-chandra is their wealth and life.

2246Nityananda, increasing everyone's love,
stayed at home for twelve years.

2247Who can understand Nityananda's heart?
Without Sri Krishna Chaitanya He finds no rest.

2248One day Prabhu reflected within Himself:
"If I go there now, it is not fitting.

2249Sri Krishna Chaitanya, having appeared in Navadvipa,
abides in the mood of childhood, keeping Himself hidden.

2250When He reveals Himself and sports with the devotees,
then, going to Navadvipa, I will meet Him.

2251But now I will quickly set out on a pilgrimage to the tirthas."
Reflecting thus, the Lord smiles within Himself.

2252At that time a worthy sannyasi came to the village;
he asks the people where the house of Hado Pandita is.574

2253Learning from the people, he went to the house of Hado Ojha;
seeing the sannyasi, Ojha was filled with great joy.

2254At once Ojha, preparing various dishes,
offered them to the sannyasi for him to eat.

2255The sannyasi says, "Brahmana, I will ask for something;
if you can promise it, then I will eat."

2256Having given his promise, he fed the sannyasi;
on departing, the sannyasi asked for Nityananda and took [Him] away.

2257Nityanandachand, steadying His heart,
goes with the sannyasi, having consoled His father and mother.

2258In this way He left home;
what wise man can understand this most wondrous pastime?

2259Fresh youth, beauty that enchants the worlds —
whoever sees [Him] even once, his eyes are refreshed.

2260In whatever direction Nityananda, full of prema, walks,
in that direction people run with impatient hearts.

2261The Lord, showing mercy to all people,
walks alone with the gait of a great king of elephants.

2262As He made a pilgrimage to the tirthas in Dvapara,
in the same way He [now] wanders through all the tirthas.575

2263Wandering, He went south to Pandurpura;
there the Lord saw Sri Vitthalanatha.576

2264In that village lives a gentle brahmana;
he is a fellow disciple of Sri Madhava Puri.577

2265The brahmana, bringing Nityananda to his own home,
carefully feeds [Him] fruits, roots, milk and so on.

2266The people of Pandurpura are most fortunate:
seeing Nityananda, all of them find solace for their souls.

2267What the Lord's state of mind is — who knows?
Having seen Sri Vitthalanatha, He stays in solitude.

2268Suddenly, in answer to that brahmana's longing,
his guru Lakshmipati came to the village from afar.

2269[He came] with many disciples, learned in all the shastras;
who can describe his affection for his disciples?

2270He is very old, [his] deeds are indescribable;
he is known everywhere — a great noble one on the path of bhakti.

2271Who can tell the glory of Lakshmipati,
whose disciple is Madhavendra Puri? That says it all.

2272Madhavendra Puri is full of the rasa of prema-bhakti;
by remembering his name every perfection is attained.

2273Sri Ishvara Puri, Ranga Puri and the others —
all are disciples of Madhava, intoxicated with the rasa of bhakti.578

2274In Gauda, Utkala and other lands are Madhava's followers;
all are devotees of Krishna, wholly devoted to prema-bhakti.579

2275In the Madhva sampradaya his fame is supreme;
an ocean of virtues, he is very dear to Lakshmipati.

2276Lakshmipati, in the house of that brahmana, his disciple,
took his meal while conversing about Krishna.

2277Lakshmipati says to him again and again,
"What auspiciousness I see in your home today!

2278How many times I have come to your house,
yet such happiness never arose in my heart.

2279From this I understand that some devotee is present here."
The brahmana says, "Your mercy is powerful."

2280By the Lord's will [this] did not come to the brahmana's mind;
thus the day passed in many conversations.580

2281At night, sitting in solitude, the best of sannyasis
sings of the charming deeds of Baladeva.

2282He has unalloyed devotion to Lord Baladeva;
weeping, he speaks, addressing Baladeva:

2283"O Baladeva, show mercy to me, lowly and wicked —
let [Your] fame resound throughout the world!"

2284Saying many such things, he cannot keep his composure:
he rolls on the ground, tears stream from his eyes.

2285He is very old as it is, and on top of that his grief is boundless —
he grew so faint that it cannot be told.

2286In extreme distress the sannyasi cannot calm himself;
suddenly, by the Lord's will, sleep overcomes him.

2287In the form of Balarama, Nityananda, playfully,
appeared to Sri Lakshmipati in a dream.

2288What beauty! It dispels the pride of Kandarpa;
[His] sweet body puts a silver mountain to shame.

2289Arms reaching to the knees, a broad chest;
the enchanting sweep of the eyes reaches to the ears.

2290In [His] ear is a single earring that charms the mind of the world;
tucked under His left arm is a sweet-sounding horn — it looks splendid.581

2291[His] body is adorned with various ornaments;
there is nothing in all the world to compare [Him] with.

2292[His] face surpasses the full moon;
in the guise of speech He pours out an ocean of nectar.

2293To dear Lakshmipati He speaks softly:
"Hearing of your grief, I feel My heart break.

2294O Lakshmipati! Krishna is the Lord of My life;
birth after birth be His servant."

2295Lakshmipati, clasping the Lord's feet, says,
"May such a sense of difference never be in me!"582

2296Hearing these words of Sri Lakshmipati,
Lord Baladeva, smiling, says something:

2297"To this village has come the son of a brahmana;
in the guise of an avadhuta he will become your disciple.

2298With this mantra you will make him your disciple."
Saying this, He speaks the mantra into his ear.

2299Receiving that mantra, Lakshmipati rejoiced;
the Lord, having shown His mercy, vanished.

2300Waking at dawn, the sannyasi ponders within himself;
at that time Nityananda came to that very place.

2301Seeing Nityananda's radiance, the sannyasi reflects:
"What wondrous radiance! This is by no means a human being."

2302Reflecting thus in many ways, the wisest of sannyasis
gazes with unblinking eyes at the beautiful holy face.

2303The Lord bows down, prostrating Himself on the ground;
in haste the sannyasi lifted [Him] up and took [Him] in his arms.

2304Nityananda says to the sannyasi again and again,
"Give Me initiation into the mantra and deliver Me."

2305At these sweet words of Lord Nityananda
the sannyasi is awash in tears and cannot calm himself.

2306Not daring to transgress the command of Sri Baladeva,
that very day he gave Nityananda the mantra of initiation.583

2307Having given the mantra of initiation, embracing Nityananda,
he was overwhelmed; his heart overflows with bliss.

2308Nityananda, dear to Lakshmipati, the merciful —
what can He not do, He who acts by His own will?

2309He increased the great joy of the Madhva sampradaya —
the Lord, affectionate to His devotees, the source of the bliss of prema.

2310Thus it was said by the ancients:584
"I worship Lord Nityananda, dear to Sriman Lakshmipati,
who increases the bliss of the Sri Madhva sampradaya, who is affectionate to His devotees."

2311Having become Lakshmipati's disciple, Nityananda
increased his most wondrous bliss.

2312Very soon He went away from there to another place;
others cannot understand this pastime of the Lord.

2313The sannyasi, left without Nityananda, became distraught;
he says nothing to anyone, pondering within himself.

2314At the end of the night a light sleep overcame him;
Lord Nityananda appeared to him in a dream.

2315Seeing Nityananda, Lakshmipati, for all his great steadiness,
cannot hold back the tears of both his eyes.

2316At that very moment the Lord took the form of Baladeva;
seeing this, Lakshmipati falls at [His] holy feet.

2317Bathed in tears, he says again and again,
"This incarnation of Yours is to deceive me!

2318Brahma and the others do not know [You], others cannot know;
only one whom You Yourself grant knowledge can know.

2319Why did You make such a mockery of me, a wretched fool?
Show mercy, Lord — I have taken shelter."

2320Hearing such words of Sri Lakshmipati,
He at that very moment took the form of Nityananda.

2321The sweetness of [His] form surpasses a mass of lightning;
beholding that beauty, Lakshmipati lost his composure.

2322Nityananda-Rama shows mercy:
He fulfilled Sri Lakshmipati's desire.

2323Forbidding [him] to tell others of all this,
the Lord, consoling [him] once more, vanished.

2324No longer seeing the Lord, Lakshmipati grew sorrowful;
sleep went far away — he sees that the night has passed.

2325He says nothing to anyone and cannot keep his composure;
from that day his state became wondrous.

2326Seeing this, the disciples grew anxious;
suddenly Lakshmipati disappeared.

2327What do I know to tell of the life of Lakshmipati,
who is known in the world as dear to Nityananda?

2328The devotion of the people of Pandura cannot be described;
even today, by Nitai's mercy, their devotion is strong.585

2329Meanwhile Nityananda Prabhu, by His own will,
travels to the holy places with joy in His heart.

2330After some days He met
with Madhavendra near Pratichi-tirtha.586

2331The prema that was revealed when the two met —
who could describe it? Only one who saw it knows.

2332Madhavendra regards Nityananda as a friend;
Nityananda regards Madhavendra as his guru.

2333Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, in the Adi-khanda — the words of Madhavendra:
"I have understood that Krishna loves me:
now I have found such a friend as Nityananda."587

2334In the same place — the words of the poet:
"Toward Madhavendra, Nityananda Mahashaya
holds no attitude other than that toward a guru."

2335Sri Ishvara Puri and the others were amazed to see this;
in all of them deep affection for Nityananda arose.

2336For some days the two were immersed in Krishna-rasa;
in the joy of their hearts they passed days and nights.

2337Nityananda, taking leave of Puri,
went to Setubandha for the darshan of Rameshvara.588

2338Sri Madhava Puri, taking his disciples, Ishvara and the others,
took leave and set out for Sarayu-tirtha.589

2339Both were as if lifeless in separation from each other;
only their absorption in Krishna-prema preserved them both.

2340Although Sri Nityananda is supremely steady,
He wandered everywhere, unable to be at rest.

2341After some days, coming to the city of Mathura, the Lord,
absorbed in a childlike mood, plays with the boys.

2342Whoever sees Nityananda-chand even once
cannot leave His company even for half a moment.

2343Supremely sweet is the form of Nityananda-raya;
countless people run to see Nityananda.

2344Nityananda does not stay in one place:
He wanders through Vraja, finding great bliss.

2345From time to time He goes to Sri Gokula-Mahavana
and, seeing Madana-gopala, stays there.

2346Seeing Nanda's home, how much rises in His heart!
Weeping, He goes on with His pilgrimage.

2347Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, in the Adi-khanda:
"Seeing in Gokula the house and dwelling of Nanda,
the Lord sat down and wept profusely."590

2348Then the Lord, bowing to Madana-gopala,
went to Hastinapura, the city of the Pandavas.591

2349Having seen all the forests and come to Vrindavana,
He plays wonderful games on the bank of the Yamuna.

2350Beneath this wondrous banyan
He now sits, now rises, now rolls in the dust.592

2351Now He adorns Himself with various flowers,
now He says, "Where is My life, My Kanai?"593

2352Nityananda, in ecstatic mood, staggers;
His long eyes are full of tears.

2353Thus Nityananda sports in Vrindavana;
who has the power to understand Nityananda's ways?

2354He came to know that Sri Gaurasundara in Navadvipa,
who had sported in a hidden form, now sports in a manifest form.

2355Smiling to Himself, Nityananda-Haladhara,
His body constantly thrilled with horripilation,

2356lost His composure, drawn by the Lord,
and went from here to Navadvipa.

2357For twenty years He travelled to the holy places;
who could describe the pastimes He had in each place?

2358This is the place of the play of Prabhu Sri Nityananda;
whoever sees it is supremely fortunate.

2359O Srinivasa, this is Chir-ghat;
some call it Chayana-ghat.594

2360One day Radha and Krishna with the sakhis,
after the rasa and other pastimes, came here to bathe.

2361Leaving their garments and other things beneath this kadamba tree,
they entered the water wearing fine, short garments.

2362They had grown weary from various pastimes;
their weariness was relieved by the cool touch of the Yamuna.

2363In the water-play great merriment arose;
all of them went and entered the lotus thicket.

2364Krishna, on some pretext, came to the tree,
hid the garments, and entered the water again.

2365After sporting in the water for some time, they come up onto the bank;
not seeing their garments, all grow anxious at heart.

2366Krishna, beholding at that time a wondrous beauty,
gave everyone their garments, joking.

2367The relief of weariness, the theft of the garments and so on took place here;
and in this place, too, Krishna performed various pastimes.

2368O Srinivasa, Radha and Krishna with the sakhis
are absorbed in the play of nidhuvana here in Nidhuvana.595

2369See, O Srinivasa, this Keshi-tirtha;
its glory is proclaimed in many Puranas.

2370Thus [it is said] in the Adi-varaha Purana:
"Where Keshi was felled, the merit is a hundred times that of the Ganga;
and even there, O Earth, there is a special [greatness] at Keshi-tirtha.

2371By offering pinda there one obtains the fruit of offering pinda at Gaya."

2372Krishna slew Keshi with great sport
and in great joy washed His hands in the Yamuna.

2373Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the eighty-fifth verse:
"He who with his neighing, in great intoxication of pride, shook the three worlds,
and with the rolling of his wide-open eyes burned the whole world on every side —
that hostile Keshi the Destroyer of Baka then tore apart like a blade of grass;
where He washed His blood-stained hands, that Keshi-tirtha I worship."596

2374O Srinivasa, here at Sri Dhira-samira
are Krishna's kunja-lilas in countless ways.597

2375Here is the wondrous meeting of Sri Radha and Krishna;
in great happiness Their dear ones relish it.

2376Thus [it is said] in the Gita-govinda, in the fifth canto, in the second song — the words of the messenger to Sri Radhika:
"There where before, together with you, He attained the perfections of the husband of Rati —
in that very kunja, the great tirtha of Manmatha, Madhava now again,
meditating on you incessantly and even repeating the mantra-syllables of your words,
longs once more for the nectar of the close embrace of your pitcher-like breasts."598

2377In the same place — the song: "He has gone to the tryst, the essence of the bliss of love, in attire as enchanting as Madana's. O you of lovely hips, do not delay your going — follow that lord of your heart. At Dhira-samira, on the bank of the Yamuna, in the forest the Wearer of the forest garland waits."599

2378See: here is the appeasing of Sri Radhika's mana;
this is Manikarnika: Krishna sports in this forest.600

2379O Srinivasa, here near the Yamuna
is Vamshivata, full of supremely wondrous beauty.601

2380The shade of Vamshivata removes the sorrows of the world;
here Gopinatha always sports in bliss.

2381In an attire that enchants the worlds, in charming poses,
He draws the gopis with the sound of His flute.

2382Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, in the Adi-lila, in the first chapter, the seventeenth verse: "The glorious Gopinatha, who begins the rapture of the rasa dance, standing on the bank by Vamshivata, drawing the gopis with the sounds of His flute — may He bestow blessing upon us."

2383This place of Vamshivata has been flooded by the Yamuna:
Vamshivata disappeared into the Yamuna.

2384Bringing one of its branches, the Gosvami himself
planted it near the former [place].602

2385See, Srinivasa, this supremely charming place:
here a cool breeze always blows softly, softly.

2386At the sound of the flute, leaving everything, with impatient hearts,
the gopis come and meet Krishna here.

2387The gopis swim in the ocean of Krishna's beauty;
Krishna, seeing the gopis, cannot remain still.

2388Taking hold of His composure, with joy in His heart —
who understands the inner meaning? — how He asks after their welfare.603

2389Here Krishna tested the prema of the gopis
and gave them much instruction to go back home.

2390Seeing, at the beginning of the rasa, inequality (asamata) among the gopis,
He resolved to vanish together with Radha.604

2391Here Krishnachandra, having vanished,
listened with delight to the lament of the gopis.

2392Without Krishna the gopis, here, of the trees and creepers
ask about Krishna with anxious hearts.

2393The gopis, imitating Krishna's lilas,
here described Radhika's good fortune.

2394Here Krishna did what pleased Radhika's heart,
and at this very place, leaving Her, He vanished.

2395Here the other gopis, seeing Radhika,
said many things with hearts in the utmost turmoil.

2396All together, longing for Krishna's darshan,
they sang of Krishna's qualities in countless particulars.

2397Here Sri Krishna gave them His darshan;
the gopis were immersed in supreme bliss.

2398The gopis carefully seated Krishna here;
here there was much conversation between them.

2399See, Srinivasa, the bank of the Sri Yamuna:
here Krishna began the great rasa dance.605

2400Surrounded by hundreds of millions of lovely women, joyfully
Krishnachandra sports in the Sri rasa-mandala.

2401In the Sri rasa play the night became like a kalpa;
Vyasa and other poets have described it in many ways.606

2402Surrounded by the jewels among women, Krishna, the crown of rasikas,
is intent on the rasa sport that draws all hearts.

2403Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Tenth Canto, in the thirty-third chapter:607
"There Govinda began the rasa sport together with the jewels among women,
devoted [to Him], pleased, their arms linked with one another.

2404The festival of the rasa began, adorned with the circle of the gopis —
[begun] by Krishna, the master of yoga, who between each two of them

2405took His place and held them by the neck, so that each woman thought He was beside her. Then the sky
was crowded with hundreds of aerial chariots
of the dwellers of heaven with their wives, their hearts stolen by eagerness.

2406Then kettledrums resounded, showers of flowers fell;
the lords of the Gandharvas with their wives sang His spotless glory.

2407The sound of the bangles, anklets and little bells of the women
[who were] with their Beloved rose in the rasa-mandala as a loud tumult.

2408There, together with them, the Lord, the son of Devaki, shone exceedingly —
like a great emerald amid golden jewels.

2409With their steps, the movements of their arms, the play of their brows with smiles, their bending waists, the swaying cloths over their breasts, the earrings swinging at their cheeks, their faces perspiring, the knots of their braids and girdles loosened, Krishna's beloveds, singing of Him, shone like flashes of lightning in a ring of clouds.

2410Dancing, they sang aloud — with melodious voices, devoted to love,
delighted by Krishna's touch; with their singing this [universe] was filled.

2411One [of them], together with Mukunda, drew out modes that did not merge [with His voice]; pleased, He honored her: 'Excellent, excellent!' [Another] drew out the same [melody] in the dhruva measure — and to her He gave great honor."

2412Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gopala-champu, in the Purva-prabandha, in the twenty-sixth purana, up to the thirty-third verse — [a song] in a suitable raga:608 "Glory, glory, O essence of good qualities! O You who have descended, shining, in Gokula to fulfil in the world what is especially cherished! (Refrain.)

2413O You whose service is longed for by the Lotus-born, by Ishvara and by the consort of the Lord of Vaikuntha! You shine, O Lord, in the rasa, where the play grows ever richer, with Your own beloveds.

2414O You whose companions are like dancers, who hold all the arts, who create mutual joy! O You whose pain is soothed by the cowherd wives, whose great bliss is loudly proclaimed by embraces!

2415O You who take many forms throughout the circle encircled by sattvika [bhavas] born of exchanged glances! O You whose fulfilment of desire, aided by a price — the glances of the young women of Vraja — has come under [their] control!609

2416Plays interwoven with the steps of lotus feet, the movements of sprout-like hands and [the play of] brows, a series of bendings of the waist, the swinging of jeweled earrings, thrilling hair and sweat —

2417[all this] with You, who resemble a cloud, each lovely woman displays like lightning. But does this comparison point to any measure or degree [of difference] between you?

2418Among the sweet-voiced, eager to dance, rejoicing only in Your joy,
their hearts enveloped by the intoxication of the nectar of Your touch, bought by bhava,

2419young women who have flooded the Source of the universe with the bliss born of song — You who shine [among them] partake of that bliss. Obeisance to this Lord!

2420She who, together with You, astonished, sings the modes with utmost purity —
she makes all the others sing [a melody] held in check by her own skill.

2421She who in singing displays an excellence greater still, increasing joy —
she is Sri Radha, perfect in worship, honored by You with marks of esteem.610

2422She whose jasmine and bracelets slip off in the rasa, in the play born of weariness — she with exquisite art places her hand on Your shoulder, where an ornament shines.

2423And she who rapturously covers with kisses Your bolt-like arm upon her shoulder —
she rejoices, unmindful of her body, and her hair joyfully stands on end.

2424When on a pretext You touch the fine mirror of a cheek where an earring swings,
in the kiss, exchanging the juice of tambula, You melt.

2425This girl, for whom the jingling [of ornaments] in dance, song and movement creates a fine rhythm — O younger brother of Rama — has placed Your hand at her heart, as if it were an incomparable lotus.611

2426And now, O You whose body is surrounded by women wearied by the course of the rasa, O You in whom the sight of the drops of weariness on those circling about has awakened the greatest tenderness!

2427O You adorned with a multitude of garlands of bright glories that the poets have established! Glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, glory, O You who sport in the rasa!"

2428O Srinivasa, [here] the rasa play spread wide:
on the bank of the Yamuna there is no end to that beauty.

2429The night is bright with the rays of the full moon;
the beauty of the Yamuna's waters — how shall I describe it to others?612

2430Here Krishnachandra with His beloveds
sported in the waters of the Yamuna in many delightful ways.

2431Krishna, fond of fun, absorbed in sport in the kunjas —
how He rested, who could describe, however much [he tried]?

2432At daybreak Krishna with His beloveds —
how they went home, the wise describe.

2433Thus [it is said] in the same [work], in the twenty-ninth purana, up to the ninety-third verse, raga Lalita:
"[In Him] who then, awaking in the finest of kunjas,
saw the flood of the sun's rays,

2434who breaks the sleep of His beloved613
and gathers His companions —

2435in the Destroyer of Kamsa my mind is immersed,
in Him who wears a peacock feather on the crown of His head. (Refrain.)

2436[In Him] who again and again delights the throng of young women,
who together with her goes outside unwarily,614

2437who sets off along the path through the dense thicket
and there bestows much bliss,

2438who by hope has checked the poison of separation —
in [that] Radiance which brings eternal bliss [my mind is immersed]."615

2439In the play of the great rasa, of all the gopis
the heart's desires were fulfilled by the prince of Vraja.

2440The Sri rasa play is the abode of great bliss;
whoever hears of all this has his desires fulfilled.

2441O Srinivasa, Krishna, the enchanter of the worlds,
who enjoys the Sri rasa play, is the treasure of Radhika's life.

2442Radha, the enchantress of the worlds, who plays in the rasa,
dearer to Krishna than life, is the crown jewel of women.

2443Whatever gives Krishna joy, that She always does;
apart from Sri Radhika, nothing else pleases Krishna.

2444With Sri Radhika and Radhika's sakhis
[He] is always enraptured in the rasa play in Vrindavana.

2445Here one day there was great merriment;
as I tell of those events, the longing [to tell] grows.

2446Vrinda thought, "Today, in many ways,
I shall see the play of Rai and Kanu with the sakhis."

2447For this reason Vrinda, taking her attendants,
makes ready for the beginning of the rasa-lila.

2448The ways in which she arranges the dancing ground —
all those fine distinctions even the Natya-shastra does not know.616

2449As moonlight is pure and bright,
so is the dancing ground — its white beauty is wondrous.

2450In the spacious courtyard of this kunja dwelling
what wondrous beauty the moonlight creates!

2451On all sides are white seats of flowers, and above them all,
in the middle, she carefully places a white throne.

2452She puts rolls of tambula in jeweled caskets,
whose fragrance draws all hearts.
